  2. Create `tools/content/lib/course.js`:
     ```js
     /* Le cours tel que les outils de contenu le lisent : les mots et les phrases tels qu'ils
        sont écrits, jetons ({naam}, {stad}, {bedrijf}) non remplis, un par élément.

          const { course } = require('./course');
          const C = course(repo);
          C.NL          l'application chargée sans l'app ni l'état (NL.util, NL.gloss, NL.content)
          C.RAW         les collections du cours telles qu'elles sont écrites (test/lib/prose.js, raw())
          C.sources     un élément par mot ou phrase, dans l'ordre du cours : sa première inscription,
                        avec id, kind, unit et copies (les ids de ses autres inscriptions)
          C.byId(id)    la source d'un id ; undefined pour une copie ou un id inconnu

        Les éléments se forment comme build() les forme (src/content/index.js) : le genre et le
        néerlandais écrit, par NL.util.norm. Les modèles (patterns) n'en sont pas : leur
        néerlandais peut être celui d'une phrase, et une table indexée par le néerlandais ne
        les distinguerait pas. */
     const path = require('path');

     function course(repo) {
       const root = path.resolve(repo);
       const browser = require(path.join(root, 'test', 'lib', 'browser'));
       const { raw } = require(path.join(root, 'test', 'lib', 'prose'));
       const NL = browser.open({ root, seed: browser.SEED, skip: [browser.APP] }).NL;
       const RAW = raw(NL.content);
       const sources = [], byKey = new Map(), byNl = new Map();
       RAW.units.forEach(u => ['word', 'phrase'].forEach(kind => (u[kind + 's'] || []).forEach((x, i) => {
         const id = u.id + ':' + kind[0] + i;
         const key = kind + '|' + NL.util.norm(x.nl);
         const first = byKey.get(key);
         if (first) { first.copies.push(id); return; }
         if (byNl.has(x.nl)) throw new Error(id + ' and ' + byNl.get(x.nl) + ' share the Dutch « ' + x.nl + ' »: a table keyed by it could not tell them apart');
         const src = Object.assign({}, x, { id, kind, unit: u.id, copies: [] });
         byKey.set(key, src);
         byNl.set(x.nl, id);
         sources.push(src);
       })));
       const byId = new Map(sources.map(s => [s.id, s]));
       return { NL, RAW, sources, byId: id => byId.get(id) };
     }

     module.exports = { course };
     ```
  3. Create `tools/content/lib/kit.js`:
     ```js
     /* Le kit de répartition : Split, Check et Merge d'un genre de lignes de contenu, et leurs
        empreintes. Le contrat est celui de docs/agents/plan-runs/design-sitting.md (« The fan-out
        form ») et du tableau des fichiers de batch-controller.md ; ce qui est propre à un genre vit
        dans tools/content/kinds/<genre>.js, que loadKind() lit.

          const kit = require('./kit');
          kit.loadKind(repo, name)       le module d'un genre, vérifié
          kit.stamp(kind, src, NL)       l'empreinte d'une source : 8 hex
          kit.split(repo, kindDir)       { ok, lines } — écrit <lot>/input.json et split.txt
          kit.check(repo, batchDir)      { ok, lines } — n'écrit rien
          kit.merge(repo, kindDir)       { ok, lines } — écrit les tables du genre, ou rien

        Les lignes imprimées sont en anglais : ce sont les agents du kit, qui travaillent sur des
        pages anglaises, qui les lisent. */
     const fs = require('fs'), path = require('path'), crypto = require('crypto');
     const { course } = require('./course');
     const table = require('./table');

     const FILES = ['input.json', 'draft.json', 'review.json', 'retry.json', 'retry-review.json', 'disputes.md', 'rulings.json', 'change.json'];
     const KIT_FIELDS = ['id', 'stamp', 'unsure'];
     const VERDICT = /^(keep|dispute: .*\S.*|for maintainer: .*\S.*)$/;

     /* Le module d'un genre, vérifié : ce qu'il doit déclarer et ce qu'il peut déclarer sont
        ci-dessous. Le genre essai de test/tools/fanout.js en est un exemple. */
     function loadKind(repo, name) {
       const file = path.join(path.resolve(repo), 'tools', 'content', 'kinds', name + '.js');
       if (!fs.existsSync(file)) throw new Error('no kind module tools/content/kinds/' + name + '.js');
       const kind = Object.assign({ optional: [], verdictFields: [], forMaintainer: () => '', checkVerdict: () => [] }, require(file));
       const arrays = ['stamp', 'fields', 'optional', 'verdictFields', 'tables'];
       const fns = ['split', 'check', 'merge', 'forMaintainer', 'checkVerdict'];
       arrays.forEach(k => { if (!Array.isArray(kind[k])) throw new Error('kind ' + name + ': ' + k + ' is not an array'); });
       fns.forEach(k => { if (typeof kind[k] !== 'function') throw new Error('kind ' + name + ': ' + k + ' is not a function'); });
       if (kind.write !== undefined && typeof kind.write !== 'function') throw new Error('kind ' + name + ': write is not a function');
       if (!kind.fields.length) throw new Error('kind ' + name + ': fields is empty');
       kind.fields.concat(kind.optional).forEach(f => {
         if (KIT_FIELDS.concat(['copies']).indexOf(f) >= 0) throw new Error('kind ' + name + ': ' + f + ' is the kit\'s own field');
       });
       kind.verdictFields.forEach(f => {
         if (f === 'id' || f === 'verdict') throw new Error('kind ' + name + ': ' + f + ' is the kit\'s own verdict field');
       });
       kind.name = name;
       return kind;
     }

     /* L'empreinte d'une source : ce dont ses lignes sont écrites, haché. Le néerlandais en est
        toujours, puisqu'il est la clé des tables ; puis chaque champ que le genre nomme dans
        `stamp`. Un champ se lit comme un écran le lit :
          'meaning'        le sens de l'élément, langue par langue (NL.gloss.of)
          une chaîne ou une paire { fr, en } (note, be…)   langue par langue (NL.gloss.of)
          absent           null
          une fonction     ce qu'elle rend de la source
          autre chose      tel quel
        Un champ récrit sans changer ce qui s'en lit, une chaîne devenue paire, garde son empreinte. */
     function stamp(kind, src, NL) {
       const G = NL.gloss;
       const read = f => {
         if (typeof f === 'function') return f(src);
         if (f === 'meaning') return G.LANGS.map(l => G.of(src, l));
         const v = src[f];
         if (v === undefined) return null;
         if (typeof v === 'string' || (v && typeof v === 'object' && !Array.isArray(v) && ('fr' in v || 'en' in v))) return G.LANGS.map(l => G.of(v, l));
         return v;
       };
       const values = [src.nl].concat(kind.stamp.map(read));
       return crypto.createHash('sha1').update(JSON.stringify(values)).digest('hex').slice(0, 8);
     }

     const failed = lines => lines.some(l => /^fail /.test(l));
     const writeJson = (file, v) => fs.writeFileSync(file, JSON.stringify(v, null, 2) + '\n');

     /* Split : la source coupée en lots, une fois. Un dossier déjà coupé (split.txt) n'est pas
        récrit : ses lignes sont imprimées telles quelles. Un lot vide n'est pas écrit, et
        split.txt, écrit en dernier, ne liste que les lots écrits. */
     function split(repo, kindDir) {
       const name = path.basename(kindDir), list = path.join(kindDir, 'split.txt');
       if (fs.existsSync(list)) return { ok: true, lines: fs.readFileSync(list, 'utf8').split('\n').filter(Boolean) };
       let kind;
       try { kind = loadKind(repo, name); } catch (e) { return { ok: false, lines: ['fail ' + name + ' -: ' + e.message] }; }
       const C = course(repo);
       let batches;
       try { batches = kind.split(C, { repo: path.resolve(repo), kind, kindDir, course: () => C }); } catch (e) { return { ok: false, lines: ['fail ' + name + ' -: the kind\'s split threw: ' + e.message] }; }
       const lines = [], seen = new Map(), names = new Set();
       if (!Array.isArray(batches) || batches.some(b => !b || !Array.isArray(b.rows) || b.rows.some(r => !r || typeof r.id !== 'string'))) {
         return { ok: false, lines: ['fail ' + name + ' -: the kind\'s split returns a list of { batch, rows }, each row an object with its id'] };
       }
       batches.forEach(b => {
         if (!/^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$/.test(b.batch) || names.has(b.batch)) lines.push('fail ' + name + ' -: batch name « ' + b.batch + ' » is not a fresh name in lowercase letters, digits and dashes');
         names.add(b.batch);
         b.rows.forEach(r => {
           const src = C.byId(r.id);
           if (!src) lines.push('fail ' + name + ' ' + r.id + ': not an item (a copy, a pattern or an unknown id)');
           else if (seen.has(r.id)) lines.push('fail ' + name + ' ' + r.id + ': in batch ' + seen.get(r.id) + ' and in batch ' + b.batch);
           if ('stamp' in r || 'copies' in r) lines.push('fail ' + name + ' ' + r.id + ': stamp and copies are the kit\'s to write');
           seen.set(r.id, b.batch);
         });
       });
       if (failed(lines)) return { ok: false, lines };
       batches.filter(b => b.rows.length).forEach(b => {
         const rows = b.rows.map(r => {
           const src = C.byId(r.id), rest = Object.assign({}, r);
           delete rest.id;
           return Object.assign({ id: r.id, stamp: stamp(kind, src, C.NL), copies: src.copies.slice() }, rest);
         });
         fs.mkdirSync(path.join(kindDir, b.batch), { recursive: true });
         writeJson(path.join(kindDir, b.batch, 'input.json'), rows);
         lines.push(b.batch + ' ' + rows.length);
       });
       fs.mkdirSync(kindDir, { recursive: true });
       fs.writeFileSync(list, lines.map(l => l + '\n').join(''));
       return { ok: true, lines };
     }

     /* Un fichier JSON du lot : un tableau, ou une ligne `fail`. */
     function readArray(dir, file, out) {
       let v;
       try { v = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(path.join(dir, file), 'utf8')); } catch (e) { out.push('fail ' + file + ' -: not JSON (' + e.message.split('\n')[0] + ')'); return null; }
       if (!Array.isArray(v)) { out.push('fail ' + file + ' -: not a JSON array'); return null; }
       if (v.some(x => !x || typeof x !== 'object' || Array.isArray(x) || typeof x.id !== 'string')) { out.push('fail ' + file + ' -: an entry is not an object with an id'); return null; }
       return v;
     }

     /* Les ids d'un fichier contre ceux qu'il doit avoir, dans l'ordre de l'entrée. Rend les
        entrées attendues, chacune une fois. */
     function aligned(file, rows, ids, out) {
       const want = new Set(ids), seen = new Set(), good = [];
       rows.forEach(r => {
         if (!want.has(r.id)) out.push('fail ' + file + ' ' + r.id + ': not an entry this file holds');
         else if (seen.has(r.id)) out.push('fail ' + file + ' ' + r.id + ': twice');
         else { seen.add(r.id); good.push(r); }
       });
       ids.filter(id => !seen.has(id)).forEach(id => out.push('fail ' + file + ' ' + id + ': missing'));
       const order = ids.filter(id => seen.has(id));
       if (good.some((r, k) => r.id !== order[k])) out.push('fail ' + file + ' -: entries are not in the input\'s order');
       return good;
     }

     /* Une ligne écrite (brouillon, reprise, changement) : son empreinte, les champs du format, et
        les règles du genre. */
     function checkRow(file, row, input, kind, ctx, out) {
       const before = out.length;
       if (row.stamp !== input.stamp) out.push('fail ' + file + ' ' + row.id + ': stamp ' + row.stamp + ', input has ' + input.stamp);
       kind.fields.forEach(f => { if (row[f] === undefined) out.push('fail ' + file + ' ' + row.id + ': missing field ' + f); });
       const known = KIT_FIELDS.concat(kind.fields, kind.optional);
       Object.keys(row).forEach(k => { if (known.indexOf(k) < 0) out.push('fail ' + file + ' ' + row.id + ': unknown field ' + k); });
       if ('unsure' in row && (typeof row.unsure !== 'string' || !row.unsure.trim() || /\n/.test(row.unsure))) out.push('fail ' + file + ' ' + row.id + ': unsure is a reason on one line');
       if (out.length > before) return;
       let reasons;
       try { reasons = kind.check(row, input, ctx); } catch (e) { reasons = ['the kind\'s check threw: ' + e.message]; }
       reasons.forEach(why => out.push('fail ' + file + ' ' + row.id + ': ' + why));
     }

     /* Un verdict : sa forme, « for maintainer » sur exactement les lignes que le format envoie au
        mainteneur, et les champs que le format ajoute au verdict. */
     function checkVerdict(file, v, row, input, kind, ctx, out) {
       const known = ['id', 'verdict'].concat(kind.verdictFields);
       Object.keys(v).forEach(k => { if (known.indexOf(k) < 0) out.push('fail ' + file + ' ' + v.id + ': unknown field ' + k); });
       if (typeof v.verdict !== 'string' || !VERDICT.test(v.verdict)) { out.push('fail ' + file + ' ' + v.id + ': verdict is « keep », « dispute: <reason> » or « for maintainer: <reason> », on one line'); return; }
       const rule = kind.forMaintainer(row, input);
       const toMaintainer = /^for maintainer: /.test(v.verdict);
       if (rule && !toMaintainer) out.push('fail ' + file + ' ' + v.id + ': the format sends this row to the maintainer (' + rule + '): its verdict is « for maintainer: <reason> »');
       if (!rule && toMaintainer) out.push('fail ' + file + ' ' + v.id + ': « for maintainer » on a row the format does not send to the maintainer');
       let reasons;
       try { reasons = kind.checkVerdict(v, row, input, ctx); } catch (e) { reasons = ['the kind\'s verdict check threw: ' + e.message]; }
       reasons.forEach(why => out.push('fail ' + file + ' ' + v.id + ': ' + why));
     }

     const tally = vs => {
       const n = p => vs.filter(v => p.test(v.verdict)).length;
       const m = n(/^for maintainer: /);
       return n(/^keep$/) + ' keep, ' + n(/^dispute: /) + ' dispute' + (m ? ', ' + m + ' for maintainer' : '');
     };

     /* Les sections de disputes.md : « ## <id> » et les lignes qui suivent. */
     function sections(text) {
       const out = [];
       text.split(/\r?\n/).forEach(l => {
         const m = /^## (\S+)\s*$/.exec(l);
         if (m) out.push({ id: m[1], lines: [] });
         else if (out.length) out[out.length - 1].lines.push(l);
       });
       return out;
     }

     /* Lit et vérifie tout le lot. Rend les lignes, et ce qui a été lu (pour Merge) : un fichier
        n'y figure que s'il passe. */
     function readBatch(repo, batchDir) {
       const kindName = path.basename(path.dirname(batchDir)), batch = path.basename(batchDir);
       const lines = [], got = {};
       let kind;
       try { kind = loadKind(repo, kindName); } catch (e) { return { lines: ['fail ' + batch + ' -: ' + e.message], got, kind: null }; }
       let C = null;
       const ctx = { repo: path.resolve(repo), kind, kindDir: path.dirname(batchDir), batchDir, course: () => C || (C = course(repo)) };
       const has = f => fs.existsSync(path.join(batchDir, f));
       const step = (file, needs, body) => {
         if (!has(file)) return;
         if (needs.some(n => !got[n])) { lines.push('fail ' + file + ' -: ' + needs.filter(n => !got[n]).join(' and ') + ' missing or failing'); return; }
         const out = [];
         const v = body(out);
         lines.push.apply(lines, out.length ? out : [v.line]);
         if (!out.length) got[file] = v.value;
       };

       if (!has('input.json')) return { lines: ['fail input.json -: missing'], got, kind };
       step('input.json', [], out => {
         const rows = readArray(batchDir, 'input.json', out) || [];
         const ids = new Set();
         rows.forEach(r => {
           if (ids.has(r.id)) out.push('fail input.json ' + r.id + ': twice');
           ids.add(r.id);
           if (typeof r.stamp !== 'string' || !/^[0-9a-f]{8}$/.test(r.stamp)) out.push('fail input.json ' + r.id + ': stamp is not 8 hex');
           if (!Array.isArray(r.copies)) out.push('fail input.json ' + r.id + ': copies is not a list');
         });
         return { line: 'ok input.json ' + rows.length + ' rows', value: rows };
       });
       const input = got['input.json'] || [];
       const inputOf = new Map(input.map(r => [r.id, r]));
       const ids = pred => input.map(r => r.id).filter(pred);

       const rowsFile = (file, want) => out => {
         const rows = readArray(batchDir, file, out);
         if (rows) aligned(file, rows, want, out).forEach(r => checkRow(file, r, inputOf.get(r.id), kind, ctx, out));
         return { line: 'ok ' + file + ' ' + (rows || []).length + ' rows', value: rows };
       };
       const verdictsFile = (file, rowsOf) => out => {
         const rows = got[rowsOf], byId = new Map(rows.map(r => [r.id, r]));
         const vs = readArray(batchDir, file, out);
         if (vs) aligned(file, vs, rows.map(r => r.id), out).forEach(v => checkVerdict(file, v, byId.get(v.id), inputOf.get(v.id), kind, ctx, out));
         return { line: 'ok ' + file + ' ' + (vs ? tally(vs) : ''), value: vs };
       };
       const verdictOf = (file, id) => {
         const v = (got[file] || []).find(x => x.id === id);
         return v ? v.verdict : '';
       };

       step('draft.json', ['input.json'], rowsFile('draft.json', ids(() => true)));
       step('review.json', ['draft.json'], verdictsFile('review.json', 'draft.json'));
       step('retry.json', ['review.json'], rowsFile('retry.json', ids(id => /^dispute: /.test(verdictOf('review.json', id)))));
       step('retry-review.json', ['retry.json'], verdictsFile('retry-review.json', 'retry.json'));

       const disputed = ids(id => /^dispute: /.test(verdictOf('review.json', id)));
       step('disputes.md', disputed.length ? ['review.json', 'retry-review.json'] : ['review.json'], out => {
         const want = ids(id => /^for maintainer: /.test(verdictOf('review.json', id)) || /^(dispute|for maintainer): /.test(verdictOf('retry-review.json', id)));
         const secs = sections(fs.readFileSync(path.join(batchDir, 'disputes.md'), 'utf8')), seen = new Set();
         secs.forEach(s => {
           if (seen.has(s.id)) out.push('fail disputes.md ' + s.id + ': two sections');
           seen.add(s.id);
           if (want.indexOf(s.id) < 0) out.push('fail disputes.md ' + s.id + ': a section for a row that is not for the maintainer');
           ['Source:', 'Row:', 'First reader:'].forEach(h => {
             if (!s.lines.some(l => l.indexOf(h) === 0)) out.push('fail disputes.md ' + s.id + ': no « ' + h + ' » line');
           });
         });
         want.filter(id => !seen.has(id)).forEach(id => out.push('fail disputes.md ' + id + ': no section, and the row is for the maintainer'));
         return { line: 'ok disputes.md ' + secs.length + ' rows', value: secs.map(s => s.id) };
       });

       step('rulings.json', ['disputes.md'], out => {
         const rs = readArray(batchDir, 'rulings.json', out) || [];
         const secs = got['disputes.md'], seen = new Set();
         rs.forEach(r => {
           const bad = why => out.push('fail rulings.json ' + r.id + ': ' + why);
           if (seen.has(r.id)) bad('two rulings: the latest replaces the earlier one');
           seen.add(r.id);
           if (secs.indexOf(r.id) < 0) bad('no section in disputes.md');
           Object.keys(r).forEach(k => { if (['id', 'ruling', 'words', 'confirmed', 'date'].indexOf(k) < 0) bad('unknown field ' + k); });
           if (['keep', 'drop', 'change'].indexOf(r.ruling) < 0) bad('ruling is keep, drop or change');
           if (typeof r.confirmed !== 'boolean') bad('confirmed is true or false');
           if (r.ruling !== 'change' && r.confirmed !== true) bad('a ' + r.ruling + ' ruling is confirmed: true');
           if (r.ruling === 'change' && (typeof r.words !== 'string' || !r.words.trim())) bad('a change carries the maintainer\'s words');
           if (r.ruling !== 'change' && r.words !== null && typeof r.words !== 'string') bad('words is a string or null');
           if (typeof r.date !== 'string' || !/^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$/.test(r.date)) bad('date is YYYY-MM-DD');
         });
         secs.filter(id => !seen.has(id)).forEach(id => out.push('fail rulings.json ' + id + ': no ruling'));
         return { line: 'ok rulings.json ' + rs.length + ' rows', value: rs };
       });
       const ruling = id => (got['rulings.json'] || []).find(r => r.id === id);
       step('change.json', ['rulings.json'], rowsFile('change.json', ids(id => (ruling(id) || {}).ruling === 'change')));

       return { lines, got, kind, ctx, input };
     }

     /* Check : chaque fichier présent du lot, dans l'ordre du tableau ; un fichier inconnu est
        laissé de côté. */
     function check(repo, batchDir) {
       const lines = readBatch(repo, batchDir).lines;
       return { ok: !failed(lines), lines };
     }

     /* Ce que Merge prend d'une ligne d'entrée : { row } (la ligne prise), { drop: true }, ou
        { why } quand elle n'est pas réglée. L'ordre est celui du contrat : le brouillon que la
        relecture garde ; sinon la reprise que la seconde relecture garde ; sinon la décision du
        mainteneur, keep (la reprise, ou le brouillon sans reprise), change confirmé (change.json)
        ou drop (rien). */
     function settle(id, got) {
       const find = (file, x) => (got[file] || []).find(r => r.id === x);
       const draft = find('draft.json', id), review = find('review.json', id);
       const retry = find('retry.json', id), second = find('retry-review.json', id);
       const ruling = find('rulings.json', id);
       if (review && review.verdict === 'keep') return { row: draft, from: 'draft' };
       if (second && second.verdict === 'keep') return { row: retry, from: 'retry' };
       if (ruling && ruling.ruling === 'keep') return retry ? { row: retry, from: 'retry' } : { row: draft, from: 'draft' };
       if (ruling && ruling.ruling === 'drop') return { drop: true };
       if (ruling && ruling.ruling === 'change') {
         if (!ruling.confirmed) return { why: 'change not confirmed' };
         const change = find('change.json', id);
         return change ? { row: change, from: 'change' } : { why: 'change.json has no row' };
       }
       if (!got['draft.json']) return { why: 'no draft' };
       if (!review) return { why: 'no review' };
       if (/^dispute: /.test(review.verdict) && !retry) return { why: 'disputed, no retry' };
       if (retry && !second) return { why: 'no second review' };
       return { why: 'no ruling' };
     }

     /* Merge : chaque ligne réglée, ses valeurs écrites dans les tables du genre, sous le
        néerlandais de sa source. Refuse sans rien écrire : un genre jamais coupé, un lot qui ne
        passe pas Check, une ligne non réglée, une source qui a changé depuis Split. */
     function merge(repo, kindDir) {
       const name = path.basename(kindDir), list = path.join(kindDir, 'split.txt');
       if (!fs.existsSync(list)) return { ok: false, lines: ['fail ' + name + ' -: never split: run Split first'] };
       const batches = fs.readFileSync(list, 'utf8').split('\n').filter(Boolean).map(l => l.split(' ')[0]);
       const lines = [], rows = [];
       let kind = null;
       batches.forEach(b => {
         const r = readBatch(repo, path.join(kindDir, b));
         kind = r.kind || kind;
         if (failed(r.lines)) {
           r.lines.filter(l => /^fail /.test(l)).forEach(l => lines.push(l));
           lines.push('fail ' + name + ' -: batch ' + b + ' does not pass Check');
           return;
         }
         r.input.forEach(input => rows.push(Object.assign({ input, batch: b }, settle(input.id, r.got))));
       });
       if (failed(lines)) return { ok: false, lines };
       if (!rows.length) return { ok: true, lines: ['ok ' + name + ' 0 taken, 0 dropped'] };

       const C = course(repo);
       const ctx = { repo: path.resolve(repo), kind, kindDir, course: () => C };
       rows.forEach(r => {
         if (r.why) { lines.push('fail ' + name + ' ' + r.input.id + ': unsettled, ' + r.why); return; }
         const src = C.byId(r.input.id);
         if (!src) { lines.push('fail ' + name + ' ' + r.input.id + ': no longer an item'); return; }
         const now = stamp(kind, src, C.NL);
         if (now !== r.input.stamp) lines.push('fail ' + name + ' ' + r.input.id + ': stale, stamped ' + r.input.stamp + ' at Split, the source now stamps ' + now);
         r.src = src;
       });
       if (failed(lines)) return { ok: false, lines };

       const taken = rows.filter(r => r.row);
       const changes = {};
       kind.tables.forEach(t => { changes[t] = {}; });
       taken.forEach(r => {
         const values = kind.merge(r.row, r.input, r.src, ctx);
         Object.keys(values).forEach(t => {
           if (!changes[t]) throw new Error('kind ' + name + ': merge wrote table ' + t + ', which its tables do not name');
           if (values[t] !== undefined) changes[t][r.src.nl] = values[t];
         });
       });
       const files = kind.tables.map(t => path.join(path.resolve(repo), 'src', 'content', t + '.js'));
       files.forEach(f => { if (!fs.existsSync(f)) lines.push('fail ' + name + ' -: no table file ' + path.relative(path.resolve(repo), f).split(path.sep).join('/')); });
       if (failed(lines)) return { ok: false, lines };

       lines.push('ok ' + name + ' ' + taken.length + ' taken, ' + rows.filter(r => r.drop).length + ' dropped');
       kind.tables.forEach((t, k) => {
         const done = table.update(files[k], changes[t]);
         lines.push('ok ' + t + '.js ' + done.set + ' set, ' + done.removed + ' removed');
       });
       if (kind.write) (kind.write(taken.map(r => ({ id: r.input.id, row: r.row, input: r.input, src: r.src })), ctx) || []).forEach(l => lines.push(l));
       return { ok: true, lines };
     }

     module.exports = { FILES, loadKind, stamp, split, check, merge, settle };
     ```
  4. Create `tools/content/lib/table.js`. Its `UNSAFE` line builds U+2028 and U+2029 with
     `String.fromCharCode`. Do not type those two characters into the file: inside a regular expression
     literal, they end the line.
     ```js
     /* Les tables du contenu indexées par le néerlandais : src/content/<nom>.js, lues et récrites
        entières par Merge. Un fichier de table tient son en-tête (un commentaire : ce que la table
        tient, et quel genre l'écrit), puis ces lignes, et rien d'autre :

          NL.content.byDutch = NL.content.byDutch || {};
          NL.content.byDutch['be'] = {
            'goeiedag': 'goeiendag',
            'hallo': 'hey, salut',
          };

        Une entrée par ligne. La clé est le néerlandais tel qu'il est écrit, jetons non remplis ;
        les clés sont triées par unités de code. L'en-tête, tout ce qui précède la première ligne,
        est gardé tel quel, et les fins de ligne du fichier aussi (CRLF ou LF). Une valeur s'écrit
        en littéral : une chaîne entre apostrophes, un nombre, un booléen, null, une liste, un objet
        (ses clés dans leur ordre) ou une expression régulière. Récrire une table sans rien changer
        redonne les mêmes octets.

          const table = require('./table');
          table.load(file)              { head, eol, name, entries }
          table.serialize(t)            le texte du fichier
          table.update(file, changes)   { set, removed } : une valeur pose sa clé, null l'ôte
          table.literal(v)              le littéral d'une valeur

        Le nom d'une table est celui de son fichier : src/content/open.phrases.js tient
        NL.content.byDutch['open.phrases']. Le fichier est lu en l'exécutant à part, avec node:vm :
        c'est un fichier du dépôt, écrit par ce module ou relu en revue. */
     const fs = require('fs'), path = require('path'), vm = require('vm');

     const MARKER = 'NL.content.byDutch = NL.content.byDutch || {};';
     const ESC = { '\\': '\\\\', '\'': '\\\'', '\n': '\\n', '\r': '\\r', '\t': '\\t' };
     /* Ce qui s'échappe dans une chaîne : la barre oblique inverse, l'apostrophe, les caractères de
        contrôle, et U+2028 et U+2029, qui finissent une ligne dans un littéral JavaScript. */
     const UNSAFE = new RegExp('[\\\\\'\\u0000-\\u001f' + String.fromCharCode(0x2028, 0x2029) + ']', 'g');
     const quote = s => '\'' + s.replace(UNSAFE, c => ESC[c] || '\\u' + ('000' + c.charCodeAt(0).toString(16)).slice(-4)) + '\'';
     const key = k => /^[A-Za-z_$][\w$]*$/.test(k) ? k : quote(k);
     const kindOf = v => Object.prototype.toString.call(v);

     function literal(v) {
       if (v === null) return 'null';
       if (typeof v === 'string') return quote(v);
       if (typeof v === 'boolean') return String(v);
       if (typeof v === 'number' && isFinite(v)) return String(v);
       if (kindOf(v) === '[object RegExp]') return String(v);
       if (Array.isArray(v)) return '[' + v.map(literal).join(', ') + ']';
       if (kindOf(v) === '[object Object]') {
         const ks = Object.keys(v);
         ks.forEach(k => { if (v[k] === undefined) throw new Error('a table value holds undefined at « ' + k + ' »: write null, or leave the key out'); });
         return ks.length ? '{ ' + ks.map(k => key(k) + ': ' + literal(v[k])).join(', ') + ' }' : '{}';
       }
       throw new Error('a table value holds ' + (typeof v === 'object' ? kindOf(v) : typeof v) + ': a table holds strings, numbers, booleans, null, lists, objects and regular expressions');
     }

     function load(file) {
       const text = fs.readFileSync(file, 'utf8');
       const at = text.indexOf(MARKER);
       if (at < 0) throw new Error(file + ': no « ' + MARKER + ' » line');
       const name = path.basename(file, '.js');
       const sandbox = { NL: { content: {} } };
       vm.runInNewContext(text, sandbox, { filename: file });
       const all = sandbox.NL.content.byDutch;
       if (Object.keys(all).join('|') !== name) throw new Error(file + ': sets ' + Object.keys(all).map(n => 'byDutch[\'' + n + '\']').join(', ') + ', and a table file sets byDutch[\'' + name + '\'] alone');
       return { head: text.slice(0, at), eol: /\r\n/.test(text) ? '\r\n' : '\n', name, entries: all[name] };
     }

     function serialize(t) {
       const lines = [MARKER, 'NL.content.byDutch[' + quote(t.name) + '] = {']
         .concat(Object.keys(t.entries).sort().map(k => '  ' + quote(k) + ': ' + literal(t.entries[k]) + ','), ['};']);
       return t.head + lines.map(l => l + t.eol).join('');
     }

     function update(file, changes) {
       const t = load(file);
       let set = 0, removed = 0;
       Object.keys(changes).forEach(k => {
         if (changes[k] === null) {
           if (Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(t.entries, k)) { delete t.entries[k]; removed++; }
         } else { t.entries[k] = changes[k]; set++; }
       });
       const text = serialize(t);
       if (text !== fs.readFileSync(file, 'utf8')) fs.writeFileSync(file, text);
       return { set, removed };
     }

     module.exports = { MARKER, literal, load, serialize, update };
     ```
  5. Create `tools/content/lib/cache.js`:
     ```js
     /* Les données externes, épinglées : chaque fichier a son adresse, sa date, sa taille et son
        sha256, et vit dans .cache/ (ignoré par git), jamais dans un fichier versionné.

          const cache = require('./cache');
          cache.PINS                         les fichiers épinglés, par clé (« kaikki/nl.jsonl »)
          await cache.fetch(repo, names, { from, pins })   { ok, lines } : les fichiers nommés dans
                                             .cache/, vérifiés ; `from` copie d'un dossier au lieu de
                                             télécharger ; un nom est une clé ou son préfixe (« tatoeba »)
          cache.get(repo, key, pins)         le chemin d'un fichier en cache, à la bonne taille ; sinon
                                             une erreur qui dit la commande à lancer

        Un téléchargement se décompresse avec bzip2 (Git Bash et ubuntu l'ont), et un .tar se lit
        ici : aucun autre programme ne s'exécute sur ces fichiers. Un fichier dont le sha256
        diffère de l'épingle est effacé : la source a changé depuis sa date, et l'épingle est à
        refaire, dans une tâche, avec ce qui en dépend. */
     const fs = require('fs'), path = require('path'), crypto = require('crypto');
     const http = require('http'), https = require('https');
     const { spawnSync } = require('child_process');

     const TATOEBA = 'https://downloads.tatoeba.org/exports/';
     const PINS = {
       'kaikki/nl.jsonl': { url: 'https://kaikki.org/dictionary/Dutch/kaikki.org-dictionary-Dutch.jsonl', date: '2026-10-22', bytes: 256173778, sha256: '00c8ee4a95169bb1ec0ac9b495d43dc7746a1e59e9a44914bae8909f9f167121' },
       'tatoeba/eng_sentences.tsv': { url: TATOEBA + 'per_language/eng/eng_sentences.tsv.bz2', date: '2026-10-22', bytes: 108815802, sha256: 'ac9f0d48a44c7ac4f3eab724567774487b9841dcfcb3b2bcac48e1cc5636cd96' },
       'tatoeba/fra_sentences.tsv': { url: TATOEBA + 'per_language/fra/fra_sentences.tsv.bz2', date: '2026-10-22', bytes: 40588086, sha256: 'ef8fdee868f2cace15f3bd20ef149a37de991ae33ad5fc023eaa5175f2003eab' },
       'tatoeba/nld-eng_links.tsv': { url: TATOEBA + 'per_language/nld/nld-eng_links.tsv.bz2', date: '2026-10-22', bytes: 2744785, sha256: '6fc7aa1b58b40d9a661113fc05f26a9ca21989330bf0e737eaa32e4be264c6ac' },
       'tatoeba/nld-fra_links.tsv': { url: TATOEBA + 'per_language/nld/nld-fra_links.tsv.bz2', date: '2026-10-22', bytes: 991928, sha256: '413c5b42bca6a3c4ee9744fbbfc5a80eb4a1b3cf42c7161a0f06ecb9d0e12d2a' },
       'tatoeba/nld_sentences.tsv': { url: TATOEBA + 'per_language/nld/nld_sentences.tsv.bz2', date: '2026-10-22', bytes: 9779813, sha256: 'bd6a9f474d4c8caf677b1dcdb5744865ec6473c5d857b11aa203d9408b7e691a' },
       'tatoeba/nld_sentences_detailed.tsv': { url: TATOEBA + 'per_language/nld/nld_sentences_detailed.tsv.bz2', date: '2026-10-22', bytes: 19557176, sha256: '378ba55c8d6512edd09155bca53314b270555367e52b704a2c21aecb869e0f39' },
       'tatoeba/user_languages.csv': { url: TATOEBA + 'user_languages.tar.bz2', member: 'user_languages.csv', date: '2026-10-22', bytes: 2425571, sha256: '8770cd3ae712fd791fc9370f98f6b17abb6d05d151cc5e5b67fe0494163b9376' }
     };

     const dirOf = repo => path.join(path.resolve(repo), '.cache');
     const sha256 = file => crypto.createHash('sha256').update(fs.readFileSync(file)).digest('hex');

     /* Les clés que des noms désignent : une clé, ou toutes celles qui commencent par « nom/ ». */
     function select(names, pins) {
       const keys = Object.keys(pins);
       if (!names.length) return { keys, unknown: [] };
       const unknown = names.filter(n => !keys.some(k => k === n || k.indexOf(n + '/') === 0));
       return { keys: keys.filter(k => names.some(n => k === n || k.indexOf(n + '/') === 0)), unknown };
     }

     function get(repo, key, pins) {
       const pin = (pins || PINS)[key];
       if (!pin) throw new Error('no pin ' + key);
       const file = path.join(dirOf(repo), key);
       if (!fs.existsSync(file) || fs.statSync(file).size !== pin.bytes) {
         throw new Error('.cache/' + key + ' is missing: run node tools/content/fetch.js . ' + key);
       }
       return file;
     }

     /* Une adresse, enregistrée dans `file`, redirections suivies (cinq au plus). */
     function download(url, file, hops) {
       return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
         const lib = url.indexOf('https:') === 0 ? https : http;
         lib.get(url, res => {
           if (res.statusCode >= 300 && res.statusCode < 400 && res.headers.location) {
             res.resume();
             if ((hops || 0) >= 5) { reject(new Error('too many redirects')); return; }
             download(new URL(res.headers.location, url).toString(), file, (hops || 0) + 1).then(resolve, reject);
             return;
           }
           if (res.statusCode !== 200) { res.resume(); reject(new Error('HTTP ' + res.statusCode)); return; }
           const out = fs.createWriteStream(file);
           res.pipe(out);
           out.on('finish', resolve);
           out.on('error', reject);
           res.on('error', reject);
         }).on('error', reject);
       });
     }

     /* Le membre `name` d'une archive tar (ustar), lu sans programme externe. */
     function untar(tarFile, name, file) {
       const b = fs.readFileSync(tarFile);
       const field = (h, at, n) => h.subarray(at, at + n).toString('latin1').replace(/\0[\s\S]*$/, '');
       let at = 0;
       while (at + 512 <= b.length) {
         const h = b.subarray(at, at + 512);
         if (h.every(x => x === 0)) break;
         const size = parseInt(field(h, 124, 12).trim(), 8);
         if (field(h, 0, 100) === name) { fs.writeFileSync(file, b.subarray(at + 512, at + 512 + size)); return; }
         at += 512 + Math.ceil(size / 512) * 512;
       }
       throw new Error('no ' + name + ' in the archive');
     }

     /* bzip2 -dc archive > file, sans shell. */
     function bunzip(archive, file) {
       const fd = fs.openSync(file, 'w');
       try {
         const r = spawnSync('bzip2', ['-dc', archive], { stdio: ['ignore', fd, 'pipe'] });
         if (r.error) throw new Error('bzip2: ' + r.error.code + ' (Git Bash and ubuntu have it on PATH)');
         if (r.status !== 0) throw new Error('bzip2: ' + String(r.stderr).trim().split('\n')[0]);
       } finally { fs.closeSync(fd); }
     }

     async function one(repo, key, pin, from) {
       const file = path.join(dirOf(repo), key), part = file + '.part';
       fs.mkdirSync(path.dirname(file), { recursive: true });
       if (fs.existsSync(file) && fs.statSync(file).size === pin.bytes && sha256(file) === pin.sha256) return 'ok ' + key + ' (cached)';
       try {
         if (from) {
           const seed = path.join(from, path.basename(key));
           if (!fs.existsSync(seed)) return 'fail ' + key + ': no ' + path.basename(key) + ' in ' + from;
           fs.copyFileSync(seed, part);
         } else {
           const archive = part + (/\.bz2$/.test(pin.url) ? '.bz2' : '');
           await download(pin.url, archive);
           if (/\.bz2$/.test(pin.url)) {
             const tar = pin.member ? part + '.tar' : part;
             bunzip(archive, tar);
             fs.unlinkSync(archive);
             if (pin.member) { untar(tar, pin.member, part); fs.unlinkSync(tar); }
           }
         }
         const got = sha256(part);
         if (got !== pin.sha256) {
           fs.unlinkSync(part);
           return 'fail ' + key + ': sha256 ' + got.slice(0, 12) + '…, pinned ' + pin.sha256.slice(0, 12) + '… on ' + pin.date + ': the source changed, and the pin is to redo in a task';
         }
         fs.renameSync(part, file);
         return 'ok ' + key + ' ' + pin.bytes + ' bytes, sha256 ' + pin.sha256.slice(0, 12) + '…';
       } catch (e) {
         [part, part + '.bz2', part + '.tar'].forEach(f => { if (fs.existsSync(f)) fs.unlinkSync(f); });
         return 'fail ' + key + ': ' + e.message;
       }
     }

     async function fetch(repo, names, opts) {
       const pins = (opts && opts.pins) || PINS, from = opts && opts.from;
       const { keys, unknown } = select(names || [], pins);
       const lines = unknown.map(n => 'fail ' + n + ': no such pin');
       for (const key of keys) lines.push(await one(repo, key, pins[key], from));
       return { ok: !lines.some(l => /^fail /.test(l)), lines };
     }

     module.exports = { PINS, select, get, fetch };
     ```

     const cache = require('./lib/cache');

### Task 7: Flemish forms in one table
Class: mechanical
Ticket: {T-flemish}
Promises: none
Why: decision 6a. The Flemish pass (tasks 8 to 10) writes a `be` for each of the 370 items that lack one, and its
Merge writes them into a table keyed by the Dutch. Today the 61 `be` are arguments of the lexicons' `W(…)` and
`P(…)` calls, which Merge cannot reach: it writes table files only. This task moves them into `src/content/be.js`, a table
in task 6's format, and attaches that table to the items at load. It sets up the one list of tables that tasks
11, 20 and 24 extend. It also moves two things that task 8's Check reads:
- the spelling exceptions, `FLEMISH` in `test/content.js`, move to `test/data/flemish.tsv`;
- the Belgian senses of the pinned Wiktionary dump are extracted by `tools/content/kaikki.js`, for the
  `wiktionary:<lemma>` evidence.

After this task:
- **The list of tables.** `src/content/index.js` holds `TABLES`, one `{ table, field }` line per table keyed by
  the Dutch. `src/content/<table>.js` sets `NL.content.byDutch[<table>]`.
- **The attach.** `build()` looks up each item's first listing in each table, by the Dutch as the listing
  writes it (tokens unfilled). It puts the value on the item's `<field>`, filled.
- **The report.** `NL.content.tableReport[<table>]` is `{ attached, missing }`, or `null` when no loaded file
  set the table.
- **The guards.** `test/content.js` fails when:
  - a table is not loaded;
  - a key matches no word or phrase;
  - the list is empty;
  - a lexicon still writes a field that a table now holds (`MOVED`, `be` for now).
- **The tools follow.** `tools/content/lib/course.js` gives a source the fields its tables hold, as written.
  `test/lang.js` reads the tables' Dutch through `tree.visitTables`.
- **The spelling.** `test/lib/spelling.js` holds the spelling check: OpenTaal, the default names and
  `test/data/flemish.tsv`. `test/content.js` uses it, and so will task 8's kind module.
- **The extract.** `node tools/content/kaikki.js .` writes `.cache/kaikki/belgian.tsv` from the pinned
  `kaikki/nl.jsonl`. `kaikki.belgian(repo)` reads it.

This is a refactor for the 61 forms: every item is the same before and after, and the move script proves it.
The new guards and the extract are new behaviour, so step 1 has tests that fail on the old code.

Notes:
- **Line endings.** The working tree is CRLF. Match on content, not line numbers. The move script and the
  table writer keep each file's line endings.
- **Comment languages.** Comments are in English in `src/content/index.js`, as the file is. They are in
  French in `src/content/be.js`, the lexicons, `test/`, and the heads of `tools/`. What a tool prints is in
  English, as in task 6.
- **Why a script for the 61 forms.** They are data: 61 hand edits would be 61 chances of a typo. The script
  works from outside the repo and edits each listing line exactly once. It writes `be.js` with task 6's table
  writer, then rebuilds the items with `be.js` loaded. It refuses unless every item, field for field, is what
  it was. It is run once and not committed.
- **The `null` that stays.** A `be` followed by a note becomes `null`, so that `note` keeps its place among
  `W(nl, g, art, be, note)`'s arguments. A trailing `be` is simply dropped. `W` and `P` keep their signature.
  Task 24, which moves the notes, can drop both trailing parameters.
- **Only the first listing is looked up.** A later listing is an alias, and test/content.js already holds
  aliases to the same meaning. The script refuses a later listing that carries a `be`; none does.
- **The kaikki extract** lives in `.cache/`, which git ignores (task 6). Only a lemma that a row cites ever
  enters the repo (ATTRIBUTION.md). The script reads the dump line by line, as JSON, and runs nothing from it.
  `test/tools/sources.js` builds its own small dump in a temporary folder, with its own pin, so CI needs no
  `.cache/`.
- **Not here.** `TESTING.md` gets its rows for the kit's tests (`fanout.js`, `sources.js`) and for the table
  guard in task 42, as the outline places them. Later tasks replace the `content.js` row whole, so an edit
  here would break their anchors.
- **What a later table adds** (tasks 11, 20 and 24 add theirs):
  - Each table adds one line to `TABLES`, just above its closing line `]; // A new table: …`.
  - It adds its file to SRC after the lexicons, and to `test/smoke.js`'s `files:` list.
  - A table that holds a field the lexicons still write adds that field to `MOVED` in `test/content.js`.

     ```js
     /* L'orthographe du cours, écrite une fois : test/content.js la vérifie, et un genre du kit
        (tools/content/kinds/) épelle comme elle. Une forme néerlandaise est connue quand OpenTaal la
        connaît (test/data/nl-words.txt.gz), qu'elle est un des noms par défaut ({naam}, {stad},
        {bedrijf}), ou qu'elle est une forme flamande voulue de test/data/flemish.tsv, avec sa raison.
        « collega’s » se lit « collega », et un mot à trait d'union est connu quand chacune de ses
        parties l'est.

          const spelling = require('./lib/spelling');
          spelling.tokens(s)          les formes d'un texte, en minuscules, jetons {…} ôtés
          spelling.stem(t)            la forme sans son « ’s »
          spelling.readFlemish(file)  les formes de flemish.tsv : une Map forme → raison
          const S = spelling.open(root, NL)   NL : l'application chargée (NL.content.DEFAULTS)
          S.forms                     les formes d'OpenTaal (un Set)
          S.flemish                   les formes flamandes voulues (une Map forme → raison)
          S.known(t)                  vrai si la forme t est connue
          S.flemishOf(t)              la forme de flemish.tsv que t emploie, ou null

        flemish.tsv : des lignes de commentaire (« # … »), puis une ligne par forme, triée par unités de
        code, une fois chacune : la forme, une tabulation, la raison. readFlemish refuse le reste. */
     const fs = require('fs'), path = require('path'), zlib = require('zlib');

     const tokens = s => String(s || '').toLowerCase().replace(/\{[a-z]+\}/g, ' ').split(/[^a-zà-ÿ'’-]+/)
       .map(t => t.replace(/^[-'’]+|[-'’]+$/g, '')).filter(t => t.length > 1);
     const stem = t => t.replace(/[’']s$/, '');                                // collega’s, auto’s, da’s

     function readFlemish(file) {
       const out = new Map();
       let last = null;
       fs.readFileSync(file, 'utf8').split(/\r?\n/).forEach((l, i) => {
         if (!l || l[0] === '#') return;
         const cells = l.split('\t'), at = file + ':' + (i + 1) + ': ';
         if (cells.length !== 2 || !cells[0] || !cells[1].trim()) throw new Error(at + 'une ligne est une forme, une tabulation et sa raison');
         if (last !== null && !(last < cells[0])) throw new Error(at + '« ' + cells[0] + ' » est hors de l’ordre, ou deux fois : les formes sont triées, une fois chacune');
         out.set(cells[0], cells[1]);
         last = cells[0];
       });
       return out;
     }

     function open(root, NL) {
       const words = path.join(root, 'test', 'data', 'nl-words.txt.gz');
       if (!fs.existsSync(words)) throw new Error(words + ' est absent. Régénérer : node test/tools/build-wordlist.js');
       const forms = new Set(zlib.gunzipSync(fs.readFileSync(words)).toString('utf8').split('\n'));
       const flemish = readFlemish(path.join(root, 'test', 'data', 'flemish.tsv'));
       /* Le prénom, la commune et l'employeur par défaut ne sont pas du néerlandais. */
       const names = new Set(Object.keys(NL.content.DEFAULTS).map(k => NL.content.DEFAULTS[k].toLowerCase()));
       const flemishOf = t => (flemish.has(stem(t)) ? stem(t) : null);
       const known = t => forms.has(t) || names.has(t) || forms.has(stem(t)) || flemish.has(stem(t)) ||
         (t.indexOf('-') >= 0 && t.split('-').every(p => p.length < 2 || forms.has(p)));   // java-ontwikkelaar
       return { forms, flemish, known, flemishOf };
     }

     module.exports = { tokens, stem, readFlemish, open };
     ```

     ```js
     /* Les sources externes du kit, lues depuis le cache épinglé (tools/content/lib/cache.js) :
        l'extrait des sens belges du Wiktionnaire (tools/content/kaikki.js).
          node test/tools/sources.js .
        Tout se joue sur un fichier écrit ici, dans un dossier temporaire, avec son épingle :
        rien n'est téléchargé et le dépôt n'est jamais écrit.

        Ce que ce contrôle ne voit pas : le vrai fichier. Il vit dans .cache/, que la CI n'a pas ;
        ce que ses sens disent, on le lit dans l'extrait, au moment de s'en servir. */
     const fs = require('fs'), path = require('path'), os = require('os'), crypto = require('crypto');
     const { spawnSync } = require('child_process');
     const ROOT = path.resolve(process.argv[2] || path.join(__dirname, '..', '..'));
     const kaikki = require(path.join(ROOT, 'tools', 'content', 'kaikki'));

     let checks = 0, fails = 0;
     const ok = (c, m) => { checks++; if (!c) { console.log('  FAIL: ' + m); fails++; } };
     const same = (got, want, m) => ok(JSON.stringify(got) === JSON.stringify(want), m + ' : ' + JSON.stringify(got) + ', attendu ' + JSON.stringify(want));
     const rejects = async (p, re, m) => {
       let e = null;
       try { await p(); } catch (x) { e = x; }
       ok(e && re.test(e.message), m + ' : ' + (e ? e.message : 'rien n\'est levé'));
     };
     const TMP = fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'vlaams-sources-'));
     const EMPTY = fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'vlaams-sources-'));
     const sha = s => crypto.createHash('sha256').update(s).digest('hex');
     const pinOf = s => ({ 'kaikki/nl.jsonl': { url: 'http://127.0.0.1/', date: '2026-10-22', bytes: Buffer.byteLength(s), sha256: sha(s) } });
     const DUMP = path.join(TMP, '.cache', 'kaikki', 'nl.jsonl');
     const EXTRACT = path.join(TMP, '.cache', 'kaikki', 'belgian.tsv');
     /* Un outil, lancé comme un agent le lance : ses lignes et son code de sortie. */
     const run = (script, args) => {
       const r = spawnSync(process.execPath, [path.join(ROOT, 'tools', 'content', script)].concat(args), { encoding: 'utf8' });
       return { code: r.status, lines: (r.stdout || '').split(/\r?\n/).filter(Boolean) };
     };

     async function main() {
       console.log('SOURCES EXTERNES');

       /* ==================================================== 1. kaikki : les sens belges */
       const entries = [
         { word: 'goesting', pos: 'noun', senses: [{ tags: ['Belgium'], glosses: ['desire, appetite'] }, { glosses: ['taste'] }] },
         { word: 'fiets', pos: 'noun', senses: [{ glosses: ['bicycle'] }] },
         { word: 'amai', pos: 'intj', senses: [{ tags: ['Belgium', 'colloquial'], glosses: ['wow'] }, { tags: ['Flanders'], glosses: ['oh dear'] }] },
         { word: 'kot', pos: 'noun', senses: [{ raw_tags: ['in Belgium'], glosses: ['student room'] }] },
         { word: 'schoon', pos: 'adj', senses: [{ tags: ['Brabant'], raw_tags: ['Brabant'], glosses: ['beautiful'] }] },
         { word: 'gij', pos: 'pron', senses: [{ tags: ['Flemish', 'dialectal'], glosses: ['you'] }] },
         { word: 'tab', pos: 'noun', senses: [{ tags: ['Belgium'], glosses: ['a\tb\nc'] }, { tags: ['Belgium'], glosses: ['a\tb\nc'] }] },
         { word: 'leeg', pos: 'adj' },
         { word: 'stoel', pos: 'noun', senses: [{ tags: ['Belgium'] }] }
       ];
       const dump = entries.map(e => JSON.stringify(e)).join('\n') + '\n\n';
       fs.mkdirSync(path.dirname(DUMP), { recursive: true });
       fs.writeFileSync(DUMP, dump);
       const pins = pinOf(dump);
       same(await kaikki.extract(TMP, { pins }), { senses: 7, lemmas: 6 }, 'extract compte les sens marqués, une fois chacun, et leurs lemmes');
       same(fs.readFileSync(EXTRACT, 'utf8'), [
         '# kaikki/nl.jsonl sha256 ' + sha(dump),
         'amai\tintj\tBelgium\twow',
         'amai\tintj\tFlanders\toh dear',
         'gij\tpron\tFlemish\tyou',
         'goesting\tnoun\tBelgium\tdesire, appetite',
         'kot\tnoun\tin Belgium\tstudent room',
         'stoel\tnoun\tBelgium\t',
         'tab\tnoun\tBelgium\ta b c'
       ].join('\n') + '\n', 'l\'extrait : son épingle, puis un sens par ligne, trié, sans tabulation ni saut de ligne dans une case');
       ok(!fs.existsSync(EXTRACT + '.part'), 'aucun fichier partiel ne reste');
       const B = kaikki.belgian(TMP, { pins });
       same(B.get('amai'), [{ pos: 'intj', labels: ['Belgium'], gloss: 'wow' }, { pos: 'intj', labels: ['Flanders'], gloss: 'oh dear' }],
         'belgian rend les sens d\'un lemme, dans l\'ordre de l\'extrait');
       same(['fiets', 'schoon', 'leeg'].filter(w => B.has(w)), [], 'un sens sans marque, ou marqué Brabant seulement, n\'est pas belge');
       same([kaikki.marks({ tags: ['Belgium', 'Brabant'], raw_tags: ['in the Netherlands and Belgium', 'Brabant'] }), kaikki.marks({})],
         [['Belgium', 'in the Netherlands and Belgium'], []], 'marks garde Belgium, Flanders, Flemish, et un raw_tag qui nomme la Belgique');
       await rejects(() => kaikki.belgian(TMP, { pins: pinOf(dump + ' ') }),
         /^\.cache\/kaikki\/belgian\.tsv comes from another pin of kaikki\/nl\.jsonl: run node tools\/content\/kaikki\.js \.$/,
         'un extrait d\'une autre épingle est refusé');

       const bad = dump.replace('\n', '\n{"word": \n');
       fs.writeFileSync(DUMP, bad);
       const before = fs.readFileSync(EXTRACT, 'utf8');
       await rejects(() => kaikki.extract(TMP, { pins: pinOf(bad) }), /^kaikki\/nl\.jsonl:2: not JSON$/, 'une ligne qui n\'est pas du JSON est refusée, avec son numéro');
       same(fs.readFileSync(EXTRACT, 'utf8'), before, 'un extract refusé n\'écrit rien');
       await rejects(() => kaikki.extract(TMP, { pins }),
         /^\.cache\/kaikki\/nl\.jsonl is missing: run node tools\/content\/fetch\.js \. kaikki\/nl\.jsonl$/, 'un fichier qui n\'a pas la taille de son épingle n\'est pas lu');
       fs.unlinkSync(EXTRACT);
       await rejects(() => kaikki.belgian(TMP, { pins }), /^\.cache\/kaikki\/belgian\.tsv is missing: run node tools\/content\/kaikki\.js \.$/,
         'sans extrait, belgian dit la commande à lancer');
       same(run('kaikki.js', [EMPTY]), { code: 1, lines: ['fail .cache/kaikki/nl.jsonl is missing: run node tools/content/fetch.js . kaikki/nl.jsonl'] },
         'kaikki.js sans le fichier épinglé dit la commande à lancer');
       same(run('kaikki.js', []), { code: 1, lines: ['usage: node tools/content/kaikki.js <repo>'] }, 'kaikki.js sans dépôt dit son usage');
       console.log('  kaikki         7 sens belges sur 9 entrées, Brabant écarté, extrait daté par son épingle');

       console.log('\n' + checks + ' contrôles, ' + (fails === 0 ? 'SOURCES CONFORMES' : fails + ' ÉCHEC(S)'));
     }

     const clean = () => [TMP, EMPTY].forEach(d => fs.rmSync(d, { recursive: true, force: true }));
     main().then(() => {
       clean();
       process.exit(fails ? 1 : 0);
     }, e => {
       clean();
       console.log('CRASH ' + (e && e.stack || e));
       process.exit(1);
     });
     ```

     Do not add it to the repo:
     ```js
     /* One-off: moves the Flemish forms (be) out of the two lexicons into src/content/be.js.
        Run once from outside the repository, before src/content/be.js is listed in build.sh:
          node move-be.js <repo>
        It refuses unless every listing edit matches exactly once, and unless the items built
        afterwards (be.js loaded after the lexicons) equal the items built before, key for key. */
     const fs = require('fs'), path = require('path');
     const root = path.resolve(process.argv[2]);
     const browser = require(path.join(root, 'test', 'lib', 'browser'));
     const table = require(path.join(root, 'tools', 'content', 'lib', 'table'));
     const { course } = require(path.join(root, 'tools', 'content', 'lib', 'course'));
     const LEX = ['src/content/lexicon.a1.js', 'src/content/lexicon.a1b.js'];
     const BE = 'src/content/be.js';

     const canon = v => Array.isArray(v) ? v.map(canon)
       : v && typeof v === 'object' && !(v instanceof RegExp) ? Object.keys(v).sort().reduce((o, k) => { o[k] = canon(v[k]); return o; }, {})
       : v;
     async function items(files) {
       const B = browser.open({ root, seed: browser.SEED, files, skip: [browser.APP] });
       await B.NL.state.open();
       B.NL.content.refresh();
       return { json: JSON.stringify(canon(B.NL.content.allItems())), NL: B.NL };
     }

     (async () => {
       const SRC = browser.sources(root);
       if (SRC.indexOf(BE) >= 0) throw new Error(BE + ' is already in build.sh: run this before listing it');
       const before = await items(SRC);
       const C = course(root);
       /* Only an item's first listing carries a be; a later listing with one would be lost. */
       const firsts = new Set(C.sources.map(s => s.id));
       C.RAW.units.forEach(u => ['word', 'phrase'].forEach(kind => (u[kind + 's'] || []).forEach((x, i) => {
         const id = u.id + ':' + kind[0] + i;
         if (typeof x.be === 'string' && !firsts.has(id)) throw new Error(id + ' is a later listing and has a be');
       })));
       const moving = C.sources.filter(s => typeof s.be === 'string');
       const texts = LEX.map(f => fs.readFileSync(path.join(root, f), 'utf8'));
       const eol = /\r\n/.test(texts[0]) ? '\r\n' : '\n';
       const lines = texts.map(t => t.split(eol));
       moving.forEach(s => {
         const call = (s.kind === 'word' ? 'W(' : 'P(') + table.literal(s.nl) + ',';
         const hits = [];
         lines.forEach((ls, f) => ls.forEach((l, n) => { if (l.indexOf(call) >= 0) hits.push([f, n]); }));
         if (hits.length !== 1) throw new Error(s.id + ': ' + hits.length + ' lines hold « ' + call + ' »');
         const [f, n] = hits[0], l = lines[f][n], be = ', ' + table.literal(s.be);
         const last = l.split(be + ')').length - 1, mid = l.split(be + ', {').length - 1;
         if (last + mid !== 1) throw new Error(s.id + ': « ' + be + ' » followed by « ) » or « , { » is not on its line exactly once');
         lines[f][n] = last ? l.replace(be + ')', ')') : l.replace(be + ', {', ', null, {');
       });
       const entries = {};
       moving.forEach(s => { entries[s.nl] = s.be; });
       const head = [
         '/* Les formes flamandes : ce qu\'on dit vraiment en Brabant flamand, là où le néerlandais',
         '   standard dit autre chose. Produis le nl, comprends le be. Une entrée par mot ou phrase,',
         '   sous son néerlandais tel que le lexique l\'écrit, jetons non remplis ; un mot peut avoir',
         '   plusieurs formes, séparées par des virgules. build() (src/content/index.js) la pose sur',
         '   l\'élément, au champ be. Merge du genre flemish (tools/content/kinds/flemish.js) récrit ce',
         '   fichier ; une forme qu\'OpenTaal ne connaît pas a sa raison dans test/data/flemish.tsv. */'
       ].join(eol) + eol;
       fs.writeFileSync(path.join(root, BE), table.serialize({ head, eol, name: 'be', entries }));
       LEX.forEach((f, i) => fs.writeFileSync(path.join(root, f), lines[i].join(eol)));
       const at = SRC.indexOf('src/content/lexicon.a1b.js') + 1;
       const after = await items(SRC.slice(0, at).concat([BE], SRC.slice(at)));
       const report = after.NL.content.tableReport.be;
       if (before.json !== after.json) throw new Error('the items differ after the move');
       if (report.attached !== moving.length || report.missing.length) throw new Error('be.js: ' + JSON.stringify(report));
       console.log('ok ' + moving.length + ' be moved, ' + after.NL.content.allItems().length + ' items identical');
     })().catch(e => { console.log('FAIL ' + e.message); process.exitCode = 1; });
     ```

  7. Create `tools/content/kaikki.js`:
     ```js
     /* Les sens que le Wiktionnaire anglais marque belges ou flamands, tirés du fichier épinglé
        kaikki/nl.jsonl (kaikki.org, tools/content/lib/cache.js). La preuve « wiktionary:<lemme> »
        d'une forme flamande se vérifie ici : le lemme cité a un sens ainsi marqué. L'extrait vit
        dans .cache/kaikki/belgian.tsv, jamais dans un fichier versionné : rien du Wiktionnaire
        n'entre au dépôt, sauf le lemme qu'une preuve cite (ATTRIBUTION.md).

          node tools/content/kaikki.js <repo>    écrit l'extrait, depuis .cache/kaikki/nl.jsonl
          const kaikki = require('./tools/content/kaikki');
          await kaikki.extract(repo, { pins })   { senses, lemmas } : écrit l'extrait
          kaikki.belgian(repo, { pins })         Map lemme → [{ pos, labels, gloss }], dans l'ordre de
                                                 l'extrait ; une erreur qui dit la commande à lancer si
                                                 l'extrait manque, ou s'il vient d'une autre épingle
          kaikki.marks(sense)                    les marques d'un sens du fichier, [] s'il n'en a pas

        Un sens est retenu quand un de ses tags est Belgium, Flanders ou Flemish, ou qu'un de ses
        raw_tags nomme la Belgique, la Flandre ou le flamand (« in Belgium »). Brabant n'en est pas :
        le Brabant est aussi aux Pays-Bas. L'extrait est une ligne d'en-tête, « # kaikki/nl.jsonl
        sha256 <épingle> », puis une ligne par sens, triée par unités de code, une fois chacune :
        le lemme, sa nature (pos), ses marques séparées par « , », sa première glose, séparés par
        des tabulations. Le fichier épinglé est lu ligne à ligne, en JSON : rien ne s'en exécute. */
     const fs = require('fs'), path = require('path'), readline = require('readline');
     const cache = require('./lib/cache');

     const KEY = 'kaikki/nl.jsonl';
     const OUT = 'kaikki/belgian.tsv';
     const TAGS = ['Belgium', 'Flanders', 'Flemish'];
     const RAW_TAG = /belgi|flanders|flemish/i;
     const head = pins => '# ' + KEY + ' sha256 ' + (pins || cache.PINS)[KEY].sha256;
     const cell = s => String(s == null ? '' : s).replace(/[\t\r\n]+/g, ' ').trim();

     const marks = sense => (sense.tags || []).filter(t => TAGS.indexOf(t) >= 0)
       .concat((sense.raw_tags || []).filter(t => RAW_TAG.test(t)));

     async function extract(repo, opts) {
       const pins = (opts && opts.pins) || cache.PINS;
       const file = cache.get(repo, KEY, pins);
       const rows = new Set();
       let n = 0;
       const lines = readline.createInterface({ input: fs.createReadStream(file, 'utf8'), crlfDelay: Infinity });
       for await (const line of lines) {
         n++;
         if (!line.trim()) continue;
         let entry;
         try { entry = JSON.parse(line); } catch (e) { throw new Error(KEY + ':' + n + ': not JSON'); }
         (entry.senses || []).forEach(s => {
           const m = marks(s);
           if (m.length) rows.add([cell(entry.word), cell(entry.pos), m.map(cell).join(', '), cell((s.glosses || [])[0])].join('\t'));
         });
       }
       const sorted = [...rows].sort();
       const out = path.join(path.resolve(repo), '.cache', OUT);
       fs.writeFileSync(out + '.part', [head(pins)].concat(sorted).join('\n') + '\n');
       fs.renameSync(out + '.part', out);
       return { senses: sorted.length, lemmas: new Set(sorted.map(r => r.split('\t')[0])).size };
     }

     function belgian(repo, opts) {
       const pins = (opts && opts.pins) || cache.PINS;
       const file = path.join(path.resolve(repo), '.cache', OUT);
       if (!fs.existsSync(file)) throw new Error('.cache/' + OUT + ' is missing: run node tools/content/kaikki.js .');
       const lines = fs.readFileSync(file, 'utf8').split('\n').filter(Boolean);
       if (lines[0] !== head(pins)) throw new Error('.cache/' + OUT + ' comes from another pin of ' + KEY + ': run node tools/content/kaikki.js .');
       const map = new Map();
       lines.slice(1).forEach(l => {
         const [word, pos, labels, gloss] = l.split('\t');
         if (!map.has(word)) map.set(word, []);
         map.get(word).push({ pos, labels: labels.split(', '), gloss });
       });
       return map;
     }

     module.exports = { extract, belgian, marks };

     if (require.main === module) {
       const repo = process.argv[2];
       if (!repo) { console.log('usage: node tools/content/kaikki.js <repo>'); process.exit(1); }
       extract(repo).then(r => {
         console.log('ok .cache/' + OUT + ' ' + r.senses + ' senses, ' + r.lemmas + ' lemmas');
       }, e => { console.log('fail ' + e.message); process.exit(1); });
     }
     ```

### Task 8: flemish scripts
Class: mechanical
Ticket: {T-flemish}
Promises: none
Why: decision 6a. The fan-out `flemish` (task 9) gives every word and phrase without a `be` a Flemish form,
or says that a Flemish colleague says the standard. Each form comes with its evidence: a rule, a lemma that
Wiktionary marks Belgian, or `none`, which goes to the maintainer. Task 6's `split.js`, `check.js` and
`merge.js` carry the fan-out, and they dispatch to one module per kind. This task writes the kind's module,
`tools/content/kinds/flemish.js`, against task 6's API (`parts/notes-kit.md`, section 2). It reads task 7's
table `be.js`, its spelling check `test/lib/spelling.js` and its extract `.cache/kaikki/belgian.tsv`.

After this task:
- **Split** cuts one batch per unit, in course order. A batch holds every word and phrase of that unit that
  `be.js` does not hold. The lexicon's `null`, which keeps a note's place until task 24, is not a form.
  - An input row is `{ id, stamp, copies, nl, kind, unit, meaning, siblings, rules }`.
  - `meaning` is `NL.gloss.meaning(src)`.
  - `siblings` are the sources with the same sense (`NL.gloss.sameSense`), as `{ nl, be }`, where `be` is
    `null` when there is none.
  - `rules` maps each evidence `rule:<a>[+<b>…]` that applies to the text it gives. A text Check would
    refuse as too thin is left out: a phrase's that keeps fewer tiles than Check asks (« Dat is klaar. »
    gets no `rule:da`, whose « Da’s klaar. » has 2), and a word's that only turns its article into `’t`
    (« het hoofd » gets no `rule:t`). So every text in `rules` passes Check as it stands.
  - The stamp is `[nl, meaning, be]`, as the outline's « Fan-outs » line says: a form that another task
    gave a source between Split and Merge makes its row stale. The flemish kind stamps a field that its
    own Merge writes, so a second run of a Merge that succeeded fails as stale. That is expected, because
    each merge task runs once (notes-kit.md, section 5).
- **The six rules**, as code (`RULES`), in the order they apply:

  | Rule | What it does |
  |---|---|
  | `kunde` | kunt u, kun je → kunde; hebt u, heeft u, heb je → hebde; bent u, ben je → zijde |
  | `ge` | u, je → ge |
  | `da` | dat is → da’s; dat → da; wat → wa |
  | `nie` | niet → nie |
  | `t` | het → ’t |
  | `is` | eens → is |

  They act on whole words and keep the first letter's case. A sentence-initial `’t` passes its capital to
  the next word: « ’t Regent weer. ».
- **Check** (`check(row, input, ctx)`) gives, in English, every reason a written row breaks the format:
  1. `be` is `null` and `evidence` is `null`, or `be` is a trimmed string on one line.
  2. `evidence` is `rule:<rule>[+<rule>…]`, `wiktionary:<lemma>` or `none`.
  3. `be` is not the Dutch itself.
  4. A word's forms are comma-separated, none empty, none twice, and the first is not the Dutch.
  5. A phrase's `be` has at least `min(3, tiles of nl)` tiles. A word's first form is not `nl` with only its
     article turned into `’t`: everyone says that, so `be` is `null`.
  6. The `{…}` tokens are kept.
  7. `rule:` cites known rules, in their order, once each. Each one changes something, and together they give
     exactly `be`.
  8. `wiktionary:<lemma>`: the lemma is in the pinned extract, and `be` uses it.
  9. Every token of `be` that OpenTaal does not know has a reason from its evidence:
     - the citing rule's reason;
     - the Wiktionary lemma, for a form that starts with it;
     - for `none`, the maintainer's keeping.
- **The maintainer.** `forMaintainer` names `evidence: none`. The kit then requires the verdict
  `for maintainer: <reason>` on exactly those rows.
- **The reading list.** `readWhole` gives `'new be'` for every row that writes a form (task 33).
- **Merge** writes `be` into `src/content/be.js`, under the source's raw Dutch, and nothing for `be: null`.
  Its `write` adds to `test/data/flemish.tsv` one line `form<TAB>reason` for each new form OpenTaal does not
  know. The reason comes from the evidence. The lines are kept sorted, after the comments, with the file's
  line endings. It prints `ok flemish.tsv <n> added[: <forms>]`. Run a second time, it prints
  `fail flemish <id>: stale, …` for every row it wrote, exits 1 and writes nothing; the test checks that.

Files:
- Create: `tools/content/kinds/flemish.js`
- Test: `test/tools/fanout.js` (one block, just above the summary line)

Notes:
- **Where it runs.** The test copies the repo into a temporary folder (`build.sh`, `src`, `test/lib`,
  `test/data`, `tools`) and runs the kit's scripts from that copy, because `check.js` finds its repo from its
  own path. It needs no `.cache/`: it writes a one-line extract there under the real pin.
- **What the test removes.** In the copy, the test takes its sources out of `be.js`, and `allez` and `hebde`
  out of `flemish.tsv`. So the test still holds after task 30's Merge has given some of these sources a
  form.
- **Its names stay in its block.** It uses task 6's helpers (`same`, `ok`, `put`, `text`, `TMP`, `ROOT`,
  `C`, `course`, `kit`, `table`, `cache`, `spawnSync`), and its own `runFr` rather than changing the shared
  `run`. The block is not numbered: tasks 12, 13, 21, 27, 28 and 33 add theirs at the same place.
- **The spelling.** The module requires `test/lib/spelling.js`, which task 7 wrote for both test/content.js
  and this kind. `spelling.tokens` drops `’t`, a single letter once the apostrophe is gone. So rule `t`
  writes no line in flemish.tsv.
- **Partial rules.** A rule applies to every occurrence of its words. A form that applies one only (« Ik
  stuur u een mail » with `ge` on the subject alone) is not `rule:` evidence: Check says what the rule
  gives, and the drafter cites `none`.
- **Language.** Comments are in French; what Check and Merge print is in English, as in task 6.
- **Counts.** At this point in the run, the split cuts 360 rows in 12 batches. The test's copy cuts 362,
  because it also takes two forms out of `be.js`. After task 30, the test's count follows what the fan-out
  merged (358 in the proof), so a later task that quotes this line writes `<n> lignes`.
