     ```js
         fs.writeFileSync(EXTRACT, '# kaikki/nl.jsonl sha256 ' + cache.PINS['kaikki/nl.jsonl'].sha256 + '\nvelo\tnoun\tBelgium\t(essai)\n');
         const K = require(path.join(FR, 'tools', 'content', 'kinds', 'flemish'));
         const CF = course(FR);

         /* Les règles : celles que be.js suit déjà, sur des mots entiers, majuscule gardée. */
         same(K.RULES.map(r => r.name), ['kunde', 'ge', 'da', 'nie', 't', 'is'], 'six règles, dans leur ordre');
         [['Dat is lekker.', 'rule:da'], ['Wat betekent dat?', 'rule:da'], ['Is dat alles?', 'rule:da'], ['Sorry, ik heb dat niet verstaan.', 'rule:da+nie'],
           ['Kunt u mij helpen?', 'rule:kunde'], ['Hoe laat is het?', 'rule:t'], ['Hoeveel is het?', 'rule:t'], ['nog eens', 'rule:is']].forEach(([nl, ev]) =>
           same(K.outputs(nl)[ev], C.NL.content.byDutch.be[nl], 'les règles écrivent ce que be.js tient déjà : « ' + nl + ' », ' + ev));
         same(K.compose('Wat is dat? Dat is het.', ['da', 't']), { text: 'Wa is da? Da’s ’t.', idle: [] }, '« dat is » se contracte, et une règle garde la majuscule');
         same(K.compose('Het regent. Kunt u het?', ['kunde', 't']).text, '’t Regent. Kunde ’t?', '« ’t » passe sa majuscule au mot suivant');
         same(K.compose('Water, niets en wattig.', ['da', 'nie']), { text: 'Water, niets en wattig.', idle: ['da', 'nie'] }, 'une règle ne touche que des mots entiers');
         const all = K.outputs('Kunt u dat niet eens?');
         same([Object.keys(all).length, all['rule:kunde+da+nie+is'], 'rule:kunde+ge' in all], [23, 'Kunde da nie is?', false],
           'outputs donne chaque combinaison où chaque règle change quelque chose');
         same(K.outputs('Goedemorgen.'), {}, 'sans règle qui s\'applique, rien');

         /* Split : un lot par unité, ses mots et ses phrases sans forme flamande. */
         const KD = path.join(FR, 'drafts', 'flemish');
         const want = CF.RAW.units.map(u => [u.id, CF.sources.filter(s => s.unit === u.id && !s.be).length]).filter(x => x[1]).map(x => x.join(' '));
         same(runFr('split.js', [FR, KD]), { code: 0, lines: want }, 'Split coupe un lot par unité, des mots et des phrases que be.js ne tient pas');
         const rowOf = id => JSON.parse(text(path.join(KD, CF.byId(id).unit, 'input.json'))).find(r => r.id === id);
         ok(!rowOf('overleven:w0'), 'un mot que be.js tient n\'est pas recoupé');
         const sorry = CF.byId('overleven:p3');
         same(rowOf('overleven:p3'), {
           id: 'overleven:p3', stamp: kit.stamp(kit.loadKind(FR, 'flemish'), sorry, CF.NL), copies: [],
           nl: 'Sorry, ik heb dat niet verstaan.', kind: 'phrase', unit: 'overleven', meaning: CF.NL.gloss.meaning(sorry), siblings: [],
           rules: { 'rule:da': 'Sorry, ik heb da niet verstaan.', 'rule:nie': 'Sorry, ik heb dat nie verstaan.', 'rule:da+nie': 'Sorry, ik heb da nie verstaan.' }
         }, 'une ligne d\'entrée : le néerlandais, son genre, son unité, son sens, ses frères de sens et ce que les règles en font');
         same(rowOf('overleven:w2').siblings.map(s => s.nl), ['de dag'], 'les frères de sens d\'une source sont dans sa ligne');

         /* Check : les raisons du genre, une par une. */
         const ctx = { repo: FR, course: () => CF };
         const why = (id, be, evidence, c) => K.check({ id, be, evidence }, rowOf(id), c || ctx);
         Object.keys(PICK).forEach(id => same(why(id, PICK[id].be, PICK[id].evidence), [], 'une ligne juste passe : ' + id + ', ' + PICK[id].evidence));
         same(why('overleven:w12', null, null), [], 'be null, sans preuve : le néerlandais suffit');
         same(why('overleven:w12', null, 'none'), ['evidence is null when be is null'], 'be null n\'a pas de preuve');
         same(why('overleven:w12', ' nie', 'rule:nie'), ['be is a form on one line, or null'], 'be est une forme sur une ligne');
         same(why('overleven:w12', 'nie', 'rule'), ['evidence is rule:<rule>[+<rule>…], wiktionary:<lemma> or none'], 'une preuve a sa forme');
         same(why('overleven:w12', 'Niet', 'none'), ['be is the Dutch itself: with nothing Flemish to teach, be is null'], 'be n\'est pas le néerlandais');
         same(why('onderweg:w0', 'de fiets, de velo', 'wiktionary:velo'), ['a word\'s first form is the Flemish one, and here it is the Dutch itself'],
           'la première forme d\'un mot est la flamande');
         same(why('onderweg:w0', 'de velo, , de fiets', 'wiktionary:velo'), ['a word\'s forms are separated by commas, none empty, none twice'], 'pas de forme vide');
         same(why('overleven:p9', 'Kunde?', 'none'), ['be has 1 tiles: a phrase\'s be has at least 3'], 'une phrase garde de quoi faire ses tuiles');
         same([why('werkbasis:p7', 'Da’s klaar.', 'rule:da'), rowOf('werkbasis:p7').rules], [['be has 2 tiles: a phrase\'s be has at least 3'], {}],
           'une sortie de règle qui laisse trop peu de tuiles est refusée, et Split ne l\'offre pas');
         same([why('dokter:w2', '’t hoofd', 'rule:t'), why('dokter:w2', '’t hoofd, het hoofd', 'none'), rowOf('dokter:w2').rules],
           [['only the article changes, « ’t » for « het »: everyone says that, so be is null'], ['only the article changes, « ’t » for « het »: everyone says that, so be is null'], {}],
           'un mot dont seul l\'article devient « ’t » n\'a rien de flamand à apprendre, et Split ne l\'offre pas');
         same(why('ikengij:p4', 'Ik werk bij de firma.', 'none'), ['be keeps the Dutch\'s {…} tokens: « {bedrijf} »'], 'be garde les jetons du néerlandais');
         same(why('overleven:p3', PICK['overleven:p3'].be, 'rule:da+zeg'), ['no rule « zeg »: the rules are kunde, ge, da, nie, t, is'], 'une règle inconnue est nommée');
         same(why('overleven:p3', PICK['overleven:p3'].be, 'rule:nie+da'), ['rules are cited once each, in the order kunde, ge, da, nie, t, is'], 'les règles se citent dans leur ordre');
         same(why('overleven:p3', PICK['overleven:p3'].be, 'rule:da+nie+t'), ['rule t changes nothing here'], 'une règle citée change quelque chose');
         same(why('overleven:p3', PICK['overleven:p3'].be, 'rule:da'), ['rule:da gives « Sorry, ik heb da niet verstaan. », not be'], 'les règles citées donnent be, exactement');
         same(why('onderweg:w0', 'de velo, de fiets', 'wiktionary:fietske'), ['« fietske » has no Belgian or Flemish sense in the pinned Wiktionary extract'],
           'le lemme est dans l\'extrait');
         same(why('onderweg:w0', 'het rijwiel, de fiets', 'wiktionary:velo'), ['be does not use the lemma « velo »'], 'be emploie le lemme');
         same(why('onderweg:w0', 'het velootje, de fiets', 'wiktionary:velo'), [], 'une forme tirée du lemme a sa raison, même inconnue d\'OpenTaal');
         same(why('onderweg:w0', 'de velo, het fietske', 'wiktionary:velo'),
           ['« fietske » is not a form OpenTaal knows, and wiktionary:velo does not account for it: correct it, or cite evidence none'], 'une forme inconnue sans raison est nommée');
         same(why('weekend:p1', PICK['weekend:p1'].be, 'rule:t'), [
           'rule:t gives « ’t Regent weer. », not be',
           '« allez » is not a form OpenTaal knows, and rule:t does not account for it: correct it, or cite evidence none'
         ], 'chaque raison est dite');
         fs.renameSync(EXTRACT, EXTRACT + '.old');
         same(why('onderweg:w0', PICK['onderweg:w0'].be, 'wiktionary:velo', { repo: FR, course: () => CF }), ['.cache/kaikki/belgian.tsv is missing: run node tools/content/kaikki.js .'],
           'sans extrait, une preuve du Wiktionnaire dit la commande qui manque');
         fs.renameSync(EXTRACT + '.old', EXTRACT);
         same([K.forMaintainer(PICK['weekend:p1']), K.forMaintainer(PICK['dokter:p6']), K.forMaintainer({ be: null, evidence: null })], ['evidence none', '', ''],
           'evidence none, et elle seule, va au mainteneur');
         same([K.readWhole(PICK['dokter:p6']), K.readWhole({ be: null, evidence: null })], ['new be', ''], 'le relecteur lit en entier chaque forme nouvelle');

         /* De bout en bout : chaque lot rédigé (be null, sauf les lignes de l'essai) et relu,
            check.js, puis Merge, et Merge relancée. */
         const batches = text(path.join(KD, 'split.txt')).split('\n').filter(Boolean).map(l => l.split(' ')[0]);
         let rows = 0;
         batches.forEach(b => {
           const dir = path.join(KD, b), inp = JSON.parse(text(path.join(dir, 'input.json')));
           rows += inp.length;
           put(dir, 'draft.json', inp.map(r => Object.assign({ id: r.id, stamp: r.stamp }, PICK[r.id] || { be: null, evidence: null })));
           put(dir, 'review.json', inp.map(r => ({ id: r.id, verdict: PICK[r.id] && PICK[r.id].evidence === 'none' ? 'for maintainer: evidence none' : 'keep' })));
         });
         const WEEKEND = path.join(KD, 'weekend'), DOKTER = path.join(KD, 'dokter');
         const review = text(path.join(WEEKEND, 'review.json'));
         put(WEEKEND, 'review.json', review.replace('"for maintainer: evidence none"', '"keep"'));
         same(runFr('check.js', [WEEKEND]).lines.filter(l => /^fail /.test(l)),
           ['fail review.json weekend:p1: the format sends this row to the maintainer (evidence none): its verdict is « for maintainer: <reason> »'],
           'une ligne sans preuve va au mainteneur, quoi qu\'en dise la relecture');
         put(WEEKEND, 'review.json', review);
         put(WEEKEND, 'disputes.md', '## weekend:p1\nSource: Het regent weer.\nRow: Allez, ’t regent weer. (none)\nFirst reader: for maintainer: evidence none\nYour ruling:\n');
         put(WEEKEND, 'rulings.json', [{ id: 'weekend:p1', ruling: 'keep', words: null, confirmed: true, date: '2026-10-22' }]);
         same(runFr('check.js', [WEEKEND]).code, 0, 'le lot, avec la décision du mainteneur, passe');
         const draft = text(path.join(DOKTER, 'draft.json'));
         put(DOKTER, 'draft.json', draft.replace('"rule:kunde"', '"rule:ge"'));
         same(runFr('check.js', [DOKTER]).lines.filter(l => /^fail /.test(l)), [
           'fail draft.json dokter:p6: rule:ge gives « Heeft ge een voorschrift nodig? », not be',
           'fail draft.json dokter:p6: « hebde » is not a form OpenTaal knows, and rule:ge does not account for it: correct it, or cite evidence none',
           'fail review.json -: draft.json missing or failing'
         ], 'check.js dit les raisons du genre, et ne lit pas la suite');
         put(DOKTER, 'draft.json', draft);

         const n0 = Object.keys(table.load(BE).entries).length, tsv0 = text(TSV);
         const MERGED_FR = ['ok flemish ' + rows + ' taken, 0 dropped', 'ok be.js 4 set, 0 removed', 'ok flemish.tsv 2 added: allez, hebde'];
         same(runFr('merge.js', [FR, KD]), { code: 0, lines: MERGED_FR },
           'Merge prend chaque ligne, n\'écrit rien pour be null, et inscrit dans flemish.tsv les formes qu\'OpenTaal ne connaît pas');
         const entries = table.load(BE).entries;
         same(Object.keys(PICK).map(id => entries[CF.byId(id).nl]), Object.keys(PICK).map(id => PICK[id].be), 'be.js tient chaque forme sous son néerlandais');
         same(Object.keys(entries).length, n0 + 4, 'et rien d\'autre');
         const forms = spelling.readFlemish(TSV), eol = /\r\n/.test(tsv0) ? '\r\n' : '\n';
         same([forms.get('allez'), forms.get('hebde')], ['forme flamande sans source écrite, gardée par le mainteneur', '« hebt ge » contracté, flamand parlé'],
           'chaque forme nouvelle a la raison que sa preuve donne');
         same(forms.size, tsv0.split(/\r?\n/).filter(l => l && l[0] !== '#').length + 2, 'flemish.tsv garde ses formes');
         ok(text(TSV).split(eol).every(l => !/[\r\n]/.test(l)) && text(TSV).indexOf(tsv0.split(/\r?\n/).filter(l => l[0] === '#').join(eol) + eol) === 0,
           'flemish.tsv garde ses commentaires en tête et ses fins de ligne');
         const beAfter = text(BE), tsvAfter = text(TSV);
         const again = runFr('merge.js', [FR, KD]);
         same([again.code, again.lines.map(l => l.replace(/: stale, stamped [0-9a-f]{8} at Split, the source now stamps [0-9a-f]{8}$/, ': stale'))],
           [1, ['overleven:p3', 'onderweg:w0', 'dokter:p6', 'weekend:p1'].map(id => 'fail flemish ' + id + ': stale')],
           'le tampon couvre be : relancée après un succès, Merge refuse comme périmée chaque ligne dont elle a écrit la forme');
         ok(text(BE) === beAfter && text(TSV) === tsvAfter, 'refusée, Merge n\'écrit rien');
         console.log('  flemish        ' + batches.length + ' lots, ' + rows + ' lignes ; six règles ; Check, Merge et flemish.tsv');
       }
     ```

- [ ] **Step 3: Write the kind.** Create `tools/content/kinds/flemish.js`:
     ```js
     /* Le genre flemish : la forme flamande des mots et des phrases qui n'en ont pas encore. La tâche
        « FAN flemish » du plan en écrit les lignes ; ce module les coupe, les vérifie et les fond
        (tools/content/lib/kit.js). Une ligne porte deux champs :
          be        la forme flamande, ou null quand un collègue flamand dit la forme standard. Un mot
                    peut en donner plusieurs, séparées par « , », la flamande d'abord : c'est elle que
                    « Comment le dit-on ici ? » demande.
          evidence  ce qui l'atteste, null quand be l'est :
                      rule:<règle>[+<règle>…]   les règles de RULES, dans leur ordre, une fois chacune :
                                                be est exactement ce qu'elles font du néerlandais
                      wiktionary:<lemme>        un lemme que le Wiktionnaire anglais marque belge ou
                                                flamand (tools/content/kaikki.js), et que be emploie
                      none                      rien de cela : la ligne va au mainteneur
        Merge pose be dans src/content/be.js, sous le néerlandais, et inscrit dans
        test/data/flemish.tsv chaque forme de be qu'OpenTaal ne connaît pas, avec la raison que sa
        preuve donne. Les lignes imprimées sont en anglais, comme celles du kit. */
     const fs = require('fs'), path = require('path');
     const kaikki = require('../kaikki');
     const spelling = require(path.join(__dirname, '..', '..', '..', 'test', 'lib', 'spelling'));

     /* Un mot entier : ni lettre, ni apostrophe, ni trait d'union de part et d'autre. Les formes
        remplacent les mots dans l'ordre donné, et gardent la majuscule du premier ; une forme qui
        commence par une apostrophe (’t) la passe au mot suivant : « ’t Regent weer. ». */
     const EDGE = 'A-Za-zÀ-ÿ’\'-';
     const CAP = '\u0001';
     function swapper(swaps) {
       const steps = swaps.map(([from, to]) => {
         const re = new RegExp('(?<![' + EDGE + '])' + from.split(' ').join('\\s+') + '(?![' + EDGE + '])', 'gi');
         const upper = /^[a-z]/.test(to) ? to[0].toUpperCase() + to.slice(1) : to + CAP;
         return s => s.replace(re, m => (m[0] === m[0].toLowerCase() ? to : upper));
       });
       return s => steps.reduce((t, step) => step(t), s)
         .replace(new RegExp(CAP + '(\\s*)(\\S)', 'g'), (m, sp, c) => sp + c.toUpperCase()).split(CAP).join('');
     }

     /* Les six règles du flamand parlé, dans l'ordre où elles s'appliquent : « kunde » avant « ge »,
        puisque « kunt u » est un tout. `why` donne, pour chaque forme qu'une règle écrit, la raison
        que flemish.tsv inscrit quand OpenTaal ne la connaît pas. */
     const RULES = [
       { name: 'kunde',
         apply: swapper([['kunt u', 'kunde'], ['kun je', 'kunde'], ['hebt u', 'hebde'], ['heeft u', 'hebde'], ['heb je', 'hebde'], ['bent u', 'zijde'], ['ben je', 'zijde']]),
         why: { kunde: '« kunt ge » contracté, flamand parlé', hebde: '« hebt ge » contracté, flamand parlé', zijde: '« zijt ge » contracté, flamand parlé' } },
       { name: 'ge', apply: swapper([['u', 'ge'], ['je', 'ge']]), why: { ge: 'flamand parlé pour « u » et « je »' } },
       { name: 'da', apply: swapper([['dat is', 'da’s'], ['dat', 'da'], ['wat', 'wa']]), why: { da: 'flamand parlé pour « dat »', wa: 'flamand parlé pour « wat »' } },
       { name: 'nie', apply: swapper([['niet', 'nie']]), why: { nie: 'flamand parlé pour « niet »' } },
       { name: 't', apply: swapper([['het', '’t']]), why: {} },
       { name: 'is', apply: swapper([['eens', 'is']]), why: { is: 'flamand parlé pour « eens »' } }
     ];
     const NONE_WHY = 'forme flamande sans source écrite, gardée par le mainteneur';
     const rank = name => RULES.findIndex(r => r.name === name);

     /* Le néerlandais où les règles nommées s'appliquent, dans l'ordre de RULES : { text, idle },
        idle les règles qui n'y changent rien. */
     function compose(nl, names) {
       const idle = [];
       const text = RULES.filter(r => names.indexOf(r.name) >= 0).reduce((s, r) => {
         const out = r.apply(s);
         if (out === s) idle.push(r.name);
         return out;
       }, nl);
       return { text, idle };
     }

     /* Ce que les règles font d'un néerlandais : une entrée par combinaison où chaque règle change
        quelque chose, sous la preuve qui la cite, les plus courtes d'abord. */
     function outputs(nl) {
       const live = RULES.filter(r => r.apply(nl) !== nl).map(r => r.name);
       const sets = [];
       for (let mask = 1; mask < (1 << live.length); mask++) sets.push(live.filter((n, k) => mask & (1 << k)));
       const out = {};
       sets.sort((a, b) => a.length - b.length).forEach(names => {
         const c = compose(nl, names);
         if (!c.idle.length) out['rule:' + names.join('+')] = c.text;
       });
       return out;
     }

     /* Ce qu'une forme laisse de trop peu à apprendre, en anglais comme Check le dit ; '' sinon. Une
        phrase garde trois tuiles, ou toutes celles du néerlandais s'il en a moins. Un mot dont seul
        l'article change (« ’t hoofd ») n'apprend rien de flamand : tout le monde le dit ainsi. */
     function thin(form, src, U) {
       if (src.kind === 'phrase') {
         const want = Math.min(3, U.tiles(src.nl).length), n = U.tiles(form).length;
         return n < want ? 'be has ' + n + ' tiles: a phrase\'s be has at least ' + want : '';
       }
       const t = RULES[rank('t')].apply(src.nl);
       return t !== src.nl && U.norm(form.split(',')[0].trim()) === U.norm(t)
         ? 'only the article changes, « ’t » for « het »: everyone says that, so be is null' : '';
     }

     /* Les sorties des règles que Split offre pour une source : celles que thin laisse passer
        (« Dat is klaar. » n'offre pas « Da’s klaar. », « het hoofd » n'offre pas « ’t hoofd »). */
     function offered(s, U) {
       const out = outputs(s.nl);
       Object.keys(out).forEach(e => { if (thin(out[e], s, U)) delete out[e]; });
       return out;
     }

     /* La raison qu'une forme de be prend dans flemish.tsv, selon la preuve ; null quand la preuve
        n'en rend pas compte. */
     function reasonOf(token, evidence) {
       const form = spelling.stem(token);
       if (evidence === 'none') return NONE_WHY;
       if (/^rule:/.test(evidence)) {
         const r = evidence.slice(5).split('+').map(n => RULES[rank(n)]).find(x => x && x.why[form]);
         return r ? r.why[form] : null;
       }
       const lemma = evidence.slice('wiktionary:'.length);
       return spelling.tokens(lemma).some(l => form.indexOf(l) === 0)
         ? 'belgicisme : le Wiktionnaire anglais marque « ' + lemma + ' » belge' : null;
     }

     /* L'orthographe et l'extrait du Wiktionnaire, lus une fois par lecture d'un lot. */
     const memo = new WeakMap();
     function tools(ctx) {
       if (!memo.has(ctx)) {
         const NL = ctx.course().NL;
         let belgian = null;
         memo.set(ctx, {
           NL,
           S: spelling.open(ctx.repo, NL),
           belgian: () => {
             if (!belgian) {
               try { belgian = { map: kaikki.belgian(ctx.repo) }; } catch (e) { belgian = { error: e.message }; }
             }
             return belgian;
           }
         });
       }
       return memo.get(ctx);
     }

     const EVIDENCE = /^(rule:[a-z]+(\+[a-z]+)*|wiktionary:\S(.*\S)?|none)$/;
     const slots = s => (s.match(/\{[a-z]+\}/g) || []).sort().join(' ');

     /* Split : un lot par unité, dans l'ordre du cours ; une ligne par mot ou phrase que be.js ne
        tient pas (le null que le lexique garde devant une note n'est pas une forme). */
     function split(C) {
       const G = C.NL.gloss, U = C.NL.util;
       const batches = [];
       C.RAW.units.forEach(u => {
         const rows = C.sources.filter(s => s.unit === u.id && !s.be).map(s => ({
           id: s.id,
           nl: s.nl,
           kind: s.kind,
           unit: s.unit,
           meaning: G.meaning(s),
           siblings: C.sources.filter(o => o !== s && G.sameSense(s, o)).map(o => ({ nl: o.nl, be: o.be || null })),
           rules: offered(s, U)
         }));
         batches.push({ batch: u.id, rows });
       });
       return batches;
     }

     function check(row, input, ctx) {
       const be = row.be, evidence = row.evidence;
       if (be === null) return evidence === null ? [] : ['evidence is null when be is null'];
       if (typeof be !== 'string' || !be.trim() || be !== be.trim() || /\n/.test(be)) return ['be is a form on one line, or null'];
       if (typeof evidence !== 'string' || !EVIDENCE.test(evidence)) return ['evidence is rule:<rule>[+<rule>…], wiktionary:<lemma> or none'];
       const T = tools(ctx), U = T.NL.util, why = [];

       if (U.norm(be) === U.norm(input.nl)) why.push('be is the Dutch itself: with nothing Flemish to teach, be is null');
       if (input.kind === 'word') {
         const forms = be.split(',').map(f => f.trim());
         if (forms.some(f => !f) || new Set(forms.map(U.norm)).size < forms.length) why.push('a word\'s forms are separated by commas, none empty, none twice');
         else if (forms.length > 1 && U.norm(forms[0]) === U.norm(input.nl)) why.push('a word\'s first form is the Flemish one, and here it is the Dutch itself');
       }
       const little = thin(be, input, U);
       if (little) why.push(little);
       if (slots(be) !== slots(input.nl)) why.push('be keeps the Dutch\'s {…} tokens: « ' + slots(input.nl) + ' »');

       if (/^rule:/.test(evidence)) {
         const names = evidence.slice(5).split('+');
         const unknown = names.filter(n => rank(n) < 0);
         if (unknown.length) why.push('no rule « ' + unknown.join(', ') + ' »: the rules are ' + RULES.map(r => r.name).join(', '));
         else if (names.some((n, k) => k && rank(n) <= rank(names[k - 1]))) why.push('rules are cited once each, in the order ' + RULES.map(r => r.name).join(', '));
         else {
           const c = compose(input.nl, names);
           if (c.idle.length) why.push('rule ' + c.idle.join(', ') + ' changes nothing here');
           else if (c.text !== be) why.push(evidence + ' gives « ' + c.text + ' », not be');
         }
       } else if (/^wiktionary:/.test(evidence)) {
         const lemma = evidence.slice('wiktionary:'.length), B = T.belgian();
         if (B.error) why.push(B.error);
         else if (!B.map.has(lemma)) why.push('« ' + lemma + ' » has no Belgian or Flemish sense in the pinned Wiktionary extract');
         else if (!spelling.tokens(lemma).every(l => spelling.tokens(be).some(t => t.indexOf(l) === 0))) why.push('be does not use the lemma « ' + lemma + ' »');
       }

       const seen = new Set();
       spelling.tokens(be).forEach(t => {
         if (seen.has(t)) return;
         seen.add(t);
         if (!T.S.known(t) && reasonOf(t, evidence) === null) {
           why.push('« ' + t + ' » is not a form OpenTaal knows, and ' + evidence + ' does not account for it: correct it, or cite evidence none');
         }
       });
       return why;
     }

     /* flemish.tsv récrit : ses commentaires d'abord, puis ses formes et les nouvelles, triées par
        unités de code ; ses fins de ligne gardées. */
     function write(taken, ctx) {
       const file = path.join(ctx.repo, 'test', 'data', 'flemish.tsv');
       const S = tools(ctx).S;
       const added = new Map();
       taken.filter(x => x.row.be !== null).forEach(x => spelling.tokens(x.row.be).forEach(t => {
         const form = spelling.stem(t);
         if (S.known(t) || added.has(form)) return;
         const why = reasonOf(t, x.row.evidence);
         if (why === null) throw new Error(x.id + ': « ' + t + ' » has no reason from ' + x.row.evidence + ': run Check');
         added.set(form, why);
       }));
       const names = [...added.keys()].sort();
       if (names.length) {
         const text = fs.readFileSync(file, 'utf8'), eol = /\r\n/.test(text) ? '\r\n' : '\n';
         const lines = text.split(/\r?\n/).filter(Boolean);
         const forms = lines.filter(l => l[0] !== '#').concat(names.map(n => n + '\t' + added.get(n)));
         fs.writeFileSync(file, lines.filter(l => l[0] === '#').concat(forms.sort()).map(l => l + eol).join(''));
       }
       return ['ok flemish.tsv ' + names.length + ' added' + (names.length ? ': ' + names.join(', ') : '')];
     }

     /* Le tampon couvre be : une forme qu'une autre tâche donnerait à une source entre Split et Merge
        rend sa ligne périmée. Merge écrit be lui-même, donc le relancer après un succès le refuse aussi :
        une tâche de fusion ne le lance qu'une fois. */
     module.exports = {
       stamp: ['meaning', 'be'],
       fields: ['be', 'evidence'],
       tables: ['be'],
       split,
       check,
       forMaintainer: row => (row.evidence === 'none' ? 'evidence none' : ''),
       merge: row => ({ be: row.be === null ? undefined : row.be }),
       write,
       readWhole: row => (row.be === null ? '' : 'new be'),
       RULES,
       compose,
       outputs
     };
     ```

### Task 9: FAN flemish
Class: fan-out
Ticket: {T-flemish}
Kind: flemish
Drafting after: 1, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8
Split: node tools/content/split.js . "<WS>/drafts/flemish"
Check: node tools/content/check.js "<WS>/drafts/flemish/<batch>"
Merged by: task 30
Why: decision 6a, « Every item, with evidence ». Today 61 items carry a Flemish form, and every other word and
phrase teaches only the Dutch of the Netherlands' textbooks. No corpus attests tussentaal, so each new form
carries its evidence: a rule of spoken Flemish (task 8's six, as code), a lemma that English Wiktionary labels
Belgian (task 7's pinned extract), or `none`. A `none` row goes to the maintainer by rule (kit line (iii)), and
the maintainer reads every new form at the content check (task 33's `readWhole`). Split cuts 360 rows (270 words,
90 phrases) in 12 unit batches: overleven 18, ikengij 29, tijd 48, bakker 28, thuis 31, familie 29, onderweg 32,
werkbasis 32, dedag 30, winkel 28, dokter 30, weekend 25. 27 of them (2 words, 25 phrases) have a rule whose text
Check accepts. Tasks 10 to 29a run beside the drafting. None of them edits a word's or a phrase's `nl`, meaning or
`be`, which the stamp covers. Task 24 drops the lexicon's `null` placeholders, and Split already treats them as
no form.

#### Format

```json
{"id": "overleven:p11", "stamp": "08c9fc4b", "be": "Da’s goed, merci.", "evidence": "rule:da"}
```

- One row per input row, in its order. Copy `id` and `stamp` unchanged, then give `be` and `evidence`, and no
  other field except `unsure`.
- `be` is what a Flemish colleague from Brabant says for `nl` at work, written as they say it.
- `be` is `null` when they say `nl` as it stands, and `evidence` is then `null` too. Most rows are `null`: there
  is no quota.
- `be` is `null` when `nl` is already the Flemish word: « goesting », « plezant », « amai », « ambetant »,
  « hesp », « pistolet », « living », « voormiddag », « namiddag ».
- `be` is `null` for a word whose only change would be its article, `het` to `’t` (« ’t hoofd »). Everyone says
  that, in Flanders and in the Netherlands, so it teaches nothing Flemish, and Check refuses it. In a phrase,
  `’t` stays a rule like the others: « ’t Is half drie. ».
- `"evidence": "rule:<rules>"` means that `be` is, character for character, the text the row's `rules` holds
  under that key. Cite only a key that `rules` lists. Each key there already passes Check.
- A rule changes every occurrence of its words. A form that changes only some of them is not that rule's form:
  cite `none`.
- `"evidence": "wiktionary:<lemma>"` names a lemma of `.cache/kaikki/belgian.tsv` that `be` uses, for example
  « de velo, de fiets » with `wiktionary:velo`. That file is the pinned extract: one lemma per line, then its
  part of speech, its Belgian or Flemish labels and its gloss.
- `"evidence": "none"` means that no rule and no lemma give the form. The row goes to the maintainer by rule,
  with no retry. Its reader gives `for maintainer: <reason>`, whatever they find.
- A word may give several forms, separated by commas, with the Flemish form first: « Comment le dit-on ici ? »
  asks for the first. The standard form may follow it, but never comes first.
- A phrase's `be` keeps at least 3 tiles, or all of `nl`'s if `nl` has fewer.
- `be` keeps `nl`'s `{naam}`, `{stad}` and `{bedrijf}` tokens as they are.
- Write the typographic apostrophe, as `rules` does: « da’s », « ’t ».
- Every word of `be` is either spelled the way OpenTaal spells it, or accounted for by its evidence: the rule's
  form, the lemma, or, for `none`, the maintainer's keeping. Check names any word it cannot account for.
- `siblings` lists the items with the same sense. Your form agrees with theirs.
- A row you doubt carries `"unsure": "<why, in one line>"`. Check still checks it, and the reader reads it first.
- A verdict carries `id` and `verdict`, and no other field.

#### Reader focus

- Would a Flemish colleague from Brabant say it at work? Dispute a form that only one dialect says (West
  Flemish, Limburg), and Dutch of the Netherlands passed off as Flemish.
- Does `be` mean what `meaning` says, in the same register? A meaning marked « (formal) » addresses someone with
  u. A `ge` there must suit the scene, a shop or a doctor's surgery: dokter:p6, winkel:p3.
- `ge` replaces only the subject. The mechanical `rule:ge` also turns an object `u` into `ge`, and that form is
  wrong:
  - « Ik stuur u een mail. » (werkbasis:p5)
  - « en bij u? », after a preposition (weekend:p3)
- After an inverted verb, `ge` takes the verb's `-t`: « doet ge », run together « doede ». So « Wat doe ge »
  (dedag:p8) and « Heeft ge » are wrong. For « heeft u », `kunde` gives « hebde ».
- `wat` that means « a bit »: is « wa » what is said in « Het gaat al wat beter. » (dokter:p7)?
- A word whose only change is `’t` for its article, and a `nl` that is already Flemish, both get `null`.
- A Wiktionary lemma can be dated, or local to one city. Is it current at work today?
- Siblings agree: the same sense gets the same Flemish form.
- `unsure` rows first.
- On a `none` row, your reason says what you found: who says it, and where. The maintainer rules on it.

### Task 10: Tatoeba source
Class: mechanical
Ticket: {T-sentences}
Promises: none
Why: decision 5a. In task 14, a drafter picks one or two Tatoeba sentences for each word without a sentence,
and credits them under CC BY. This task writes the source those sentences come from,
`tools/content/tatoeba.js`, in three parts:
- **The extract.** It reads the pinned Tatoeba files through task 6's cache. It writes
  `.cache/tatoeba/extract.tsv`, which holds every Dutch sentence that has both an English and a French
  translation. Each sentence carries its author, whether the author is a native speaker, and the id and
  author of each translation. The credit (task 13) needs those authors.
- **Loading.** `load` reads the extract back, by id and by form.
- **Ranking.** `rank` gives a word's candidates, ranked the way the design measured them:
  - from 4 to 8 tiles;
  - nothing borrowed from a later unit;
  - no form beyond the word's own that the course has not taught by the word's unit: not one, not even an
    inflection of a word the course has taught (#12, story 39);
  - none of the default names;
  - then sentences without je or jij first, then native authors first, then fewer tiles.

The course's order moves into `test/lib/sequence.js`: which unit first teaches a form, and the function words
that never count. Before this task, test/content.js held it alone. Now the tool and the content check count
the same way. `spelling.named` joins `test/lib/spelling.js`, so that one function says when a sentence names
`{naam}`, `{stad}` or `{bedrijf}`.

Files:
- Create: `tools/content/tatoeba.js`, `test/lib/sequence.js`
- Modify: `tools/content/lib/cache.js` (two pins changed, one dropped), `test/lib/spelling.js` (`named`),
  `test/content.js` (check 3 reads `test/lib/sequence.js`), `ATTRIBUTION.md`, `test/run-all.sh` (a comment)
- Test: `test/tools/sources.js` (a second section), `test/tools/fanout.js` (two counts of task 6's pins)

Notes:
- **The pins.** Task 6 pinned `eng_sentences.tsv` and `fra_sentences.tsv`, which name no author. The credit
  names the author of every translation, and only the `_sentences_detailed.tsv` files give it. So this task
  pins those two in their place. It drops `nld_sentences.tsv`, which `nld_sentences_detailed.tsv` already
  holds. That leaves seven pins, six of them Tatoeba's. task 6's own test counts them in two places, which
  step 1 updates.
- **The test file.** The outline names `test/tools/sources.js` as this task's new test. Task 7 created that
  file for the Wiktionary extract, so this task adds a second section to it. The section builds its own
  six small files and their pins in the suite's temporary folder, as task 7's section does. It needs no
  `.cache/` and downloads nothing.
- **The fixture's « Gent ».** One sentence in the fixture names the default city. That is how the test checks
  that `rank` leaves out a sentence that `spelling.named` flags. The fixture's first unit teaches « Gent » as
  a phrase, as the course writes the default city, so `spelling.named` is the only rule that leaves the
  sentence out. No content table names it.
- **`test/content.js`.** Its check 3 changes only where it reads the course's order from. That part is a
  refactor: the check prints the same line and the same count.
- **What the forms do not see.** `sequence.forms` knows a noun's plurals, a verb's stems and their -t form,
  and an adjective's -e form. It cannot build any other inflected form, such as a participle or an
  irregular plural, so such a form counts as never taught. A homograph counts as the course's word. The
  file's head says so too.
- **Never taught means not taught yet, inflections included.** Issue #12, story 39: « an example sentence uses
  only vocabulary I have already met ». So `rank` offers no candidate with a form, beyond the word's own,
  that no unit up to the word's teaches, and task 12's Check refuses one. An inflected form of another word
  counts as never taught (« oude » when the course has taught « oud »): `sequence.forms` guesses by the
  ending, with no lexicon, so it cannot tell an inflection reliably. Asked for another word's forms, it would
  take « Engelsen » for a plural of « het Engels », and « Fransen » of « het Frans ». It serves the word's
  own forms only, where the drafter and the reader see the guess. Allowing the inflections it does recognise
  would give a candidate to two more words of the course, « dag » and « tot ziens », both through
  « Goede dag. Tot ziens. ». The fixture's sentences 17 and 19 check the rule: one uses « vriendelijk », which
  the course never teaches, and one « oude ».
- **Who reads what.** Tasks 11, 12 and 13 read `sequence`, `spelling.named`, `tatoeba.load`, `tatoeba.rank`
  and `tatoeba.JE`. Task 21 reads `sequence.firstUnits` and `sequence.ahead`.
- **Language.** The comments are in French. The tool prints in English, as task 6's tools do.

  5. Create `test/lib/sequence.js`:
     ```js
     /* L'ordre du cours, écrit une fois : test/content.js tient les phrases d'exemple à ce que le
        cours a déjà enseigné, et les outils de contenu (tools/content/) classent et vérifient les
        phrases d'une source de la même façon.

          const sequence = require('./lib/sequence');
          sequence.GRAMMAR                 les mots-outils (un Set) : on n'écrit pas une phrase sans
                                           eux, ils ne comptent jamais
          sequence.firstUnits(units)       Map forme → index de la première unité dont un mot ou une
                                           phrase écrit cette forme (spelling.tokens)
          sequence.forms(item, NL)         les formes d'un mot qu'une phrase peut employer (un Set) :
                                           ses formes, et pour un mot d'une forme, un pluriel (nom),
                                           un radical et sa forme en -t (verbe), une forme en -e (autre)
          sequence.ahead(text, ui, first)  les formes du texte qu'une unité après ui enseigne
          sequence.unmet(text, ui, first, own)   les formes du texte qu'aucune unité jusqu'à ui
                                           n'enseigne et que le Set own ne contient pas

        ui est l'index d'une unité dans l'ordre du cours, first ce que firstUnits() rend. Une forme
        n'est comptée qu'une fois par texte. Ce que ces formes NE voient PAS : une forme fléchie
        qu'elles ne savent pas former (un participe, un pluriel irrégulier) compte comme jamais
        enseignée ; un homographe compte comme le mot du cours. Une forme fléchie d'un AUTRE mot du
        cours (« oude » quand le cours a enseigné « oud ») compte aussi comme jamais enseignée :
        forms() devine par la terminaison, sans lexique, et prendrait « Engelsen » pour le pluriel de
        « het Engels » ; il ne sert qu'aux formes du mot lui-même. */
     const { tokens } = require('./spelling');

     const GRAMMAR = new Set(('ik ge gij je jij u hij ze zij we wij het de een is ben bent zijn was heb hebt ' +
       'heeft had kan kunt kun wil wilt moet mag ga gaat gaan doe doet niet nie geen en of maar want dat dit ' +
       'die deze er hier daar ook nog al wel te in op van met voor aan bij naar uit om over door tot me mijn ' +
       'uw zo heel veel wat wie waar hoe nu dan als zich eens even graag ja nee').split(' '));

     function firstUnits(units) {
       const first = new Map();
       units.forEach((u, ui) => (u.words || []).concat(u.phrases || []).forEach(it =>
         tokens(it.nl).forEach(t => { if (!first.has(t)) first.set(t, ui); })));
       return first;
     }

     function forms(item, NL) {
       const b = NL.util.bare(item.nl).toLowerCase(), own = tokens(b), f = new Set(own);
       if (own.length !== 1) return f;
       const cls = NL.gloss.wordClass(item, 'en');
       if (cls === 'noun') ['en', 's', 'n', '\'s', '’s'].forEach(e => f.add(b + e));
       else if (cls === 'verb') {
         const st = b.slice(0, -2), stems = [st];
         if (/([^aeiou])\1$/.test(st)) stems.push(st.slice(0, -1));                  // zitten → zit
         const m = st.match(/^(.*[^aeiou])([aeiou])([^aeiou])$/);                     // maken → maak
         if (m) stems.push(m[1] + m[2] + m[2] + m[3]);
         stems.forEach(s => {
           const end = s.replace(/v$/, 'f').replace(/z$/, 's');                       // leven → leef, lezen → lees
           [s, end, end + 't'].forEach(x => f.add(x));
         });
       } else f.add(b + 'e');
       return f;
     }

     const uniq = text => [...new Set(tokens(text))];
     const ahead = (text, ui, first) => uniq(text).filter(t => !GRAMMAR.has(t) && first.has(t) && first.get(t) > ui);
     const unmet = (text, ui, first, own) => uniq(text).filter(t =>
       !GRAMMAR.has(t) && !(first.has(t) && first.get(t) <= ui) && !own.has(t));

     module.exports = { GRAMMAR, firstUnits, forms, ahead, unmet };
     ```
  6. Create `tools/content/tatoeba.js`:
     ```js
     /* Les phrases de Tatoeba (tatoeba.org, CC BY 2.0 FR) traduites en anglais ET en français, avec
        leurs auteurs, tirées des fichiers épinglés tatoeba/… (tools/content/lib/cache.js). L'extrait
        vit dans .cache/tatoeba/extract.tsv, jamais dans un fichier versionné : seules les phrases
        choisies entrent au dépôt, chacune créditée dans docs/attribution/tatoeba.tsv (ATTRIBUTION.md).

          node tools/content/tatoeba.js <repo>   écrit l'extrait, depuis .cache/tatoeba/
          const tatoeba = require('./tools/content/tatoeba');
          await tatoeba.extract(repo, { pins })  { nld, eng, fra } : écrit l'extrait, rend ses comptes
          tatoeba.load(repo, { pins })           { nld, eng, fra, byForm } : les phrases de l'extrait,
                                                 par id ; une erreur qui dit la commande à lancer si
                                                 l'extrait manque, ou s'il vient d'autres épingles
          tatoeba.rank(T, item, seq)             les candidates d'un mot du cours, 8 au plus, classées
          tatoeba.JE                             je, jij, jou, jouw : le tutoiement que le cours
                                                 n'enseigne pas (il enseigne ge et gij)

        Une phrase néerlandaise : { id, text, owner, native, eng: [id…], fra: [id…] } ; une
        traduction : { id, text, owner }. Un id est un nombre ; owner vaut '' quand Tatoeba n'en
        nomme pas ; native est vrai quand l'auteur se dit de langue maternelle néerlandaise
        (user_languages.csv, niveau 5). byForm : Map forme → les phrases néerlandaises qui l'écrivent.
        seq : { NL, first, ui } (test/lib/sequence.js), et known, facultatif : une fonction qui dit
        si une forme s'écrit ainsi (test/lib/spelling.js, S.known). Une candidate :
        { id, nl, owner, en: [{ id, text, owner }], fr: [{ id, text, owner }], tiles }.

        Une candidate écrit le mot (une de ses formes ; les formes d'un mot de plusieurs formes, à la
        suite), a de 4 à 8 tuiles, n'emprunte rien à une unité ultérieure, n'emploie hors des formes du
        mot que ce que le cours a enseigné jusqu'à l'unité du mot (#12, récit 39 : pas une forme jamais
        enseignée, pas même fléchie d'un mot vu ; test/lib/sequence.js dit pourquoi), ne nomme ni le
        prénom, ni la commune, ni l'employeur par défaut, et, quand seq.known est donné, n'a que des
        formes qu'il connaît. Le classement : sans je, jij, jou ni jouw d'abord (le cours enseigne ge
        et gij), puis d'un auteur de langue maternelle, puis moins de tuiles, et l'id.

        L'extrait est une ligne d'en-tête qui nomme les épingles lues, puis une ligne par phrase, par
        langue et par id : « nld », id, auteur, 1 ou 0, texte, ids anglais et ids français séparés
        par « , » ; « eng » ou « fra », id, auteur, texte. Une phrase néerlandaise n'y est que si une
        traduction anglaise ET une française existent. Les fichiers épinglés se lisent ligne à ligne,
        comme du texte : rien ne s'en exécute. */
     const fs = require('fs'), path = require('path'), readline = require('readline');
     const cache = require('./lib/cache');
     const { tokens, named } = require('../../test/lib/spelling');
     const sequence = require('../../test/lib/sequence');

     const KEYS = ['tatoeba/nld_sentences_detailed.tsv', 'tatoeba/eng_sentences_detailed.tsv', 'tatoeba/fra_sentences_detailed.tsv',
       'tatoeba/nld-eng_links.tsv', 'tatoeba/nld-fra_links.tsv', 'tatoeba/user_languages.csv'];
     const OUT = 'tatoeba/extract.tsv';
     const JE = ['je', 'jij', 'jou', 'jouw'];
     const head = pins => '# ' + KEYS.map(k => k + ' ' + (pins || cache.PINS)[k].sha256).join(' ');
     const cell = s => String(s == null ? '' : s).replace(/[\t\r\n]+/g, ' ').trim();
     const owner = s => (s === '\\N' ? '' : cell(s));

     async function each(file, fn) {
       const lines = readline.createInterface({ input: fs.createReadStream(file, 'utf8'), crlfDelay: Infinity });
       for await (const line of lines) if (line) fn(line.split('\t'));
     }

     async function extract(repo, opts) {
       const pins = (opts && opts.pins) || cache.PINS;
       const file = KEYS.map(k => cache.get(repo, k, pins));
       const links = { eng: new Map(), fra: new Map() };
       for (const [lang, f] of [['eng', file[3]], ['fra', file[4]]]) {
         await each(f, c => {
           const from = Number(c[0]), to = Number(c[1]);
           if (!links[lang].has(from)) links[lang].set(from, []);
           links[lang].get(from).push(to);
         });
       }
       const native = new Set();
       await each(file[5], c => { if (c[0] === 'nld' && c[1] === '5' && c[2]) native.add(c[2]); });
       const nld = new Map();
       await each(file[0], c => {
         const id = Number(c[0]);
         if (c[1] === 'nld' && links.eng.has(id) && links.fra.has(id)) nld.set(id, { id, owner: owner(c[3]), text: cell(c[2]) });
       });
       const tr = { eng: new Map(), fra: new Map() };
       for (const [lang, f] of [['eng', file[1]], ['fra', file[2]]]) {
         const want = new Set();
         nld.forEach(s => links[lang].get(s.id).forEach(id => want.add(id)));
         await each(f, c => {
           const id = Number(c[0]);
           if (c[1] === lang && want.has(id)) tr[lang].set(id, { id, owner: owner(c[3]), text: cell(c[2]) });
         });
       }
       /* Une traduction effacée depuis le lien n'est pas dans son fichier : le lien tombe, et la
          phrase avec lui si c'était sa seule traduction dans cette langue. */
       const kept = [...nld.values()].map(s => Object.assign(s, {
         native: native.has(s.owner),
         eng: links.eng.get(s.id).filter(id => tr.eng.has(id)).sort((a, b) => a - b),
         fra: links.fra.get(s.id).filter(id => tr.fra.has(id)).sort((a, b) => a - b)
       })).filter(s => s.eng.length && s.fra.length).sort((a, b) => a.id - b.id);
       const used = { eng: new Set(), fra: new Set() };
       kept.forEach(s => ['eng', 'fra'].forEach(l => s[l].forEach(id => used[l].add(id))));
       const lines = [head(pins)].concat(kept.map(s => ['nld', s.id, s.owner, s.native ? 1 : 0, s.text, s.eng.join(','), s.fra.join(',')].join('\t')));
       ['eng', 'fra'].forEach(l => [...used[l]].sort((a, b) => a - b).forEach(id => {
         const t = tr[l].get(id);
         lines.push([l, id, t.owner, t.text].join('\t'));
       }));
       const out = path.join(path.resolve(repo), '.cache', OUT);
       fs.writeFileSync(out + '.part', lines.join('\n') + '\n');
       fs.renameSync(out + '.part', out);
       return { nld: kept.length, eng: used.eng.size, fra: used.fra.size };
     }

     function load(repo, opts) {
       const pins = (opts && opts.pins) || cache.PINS;
       const file = path.join(path.resolve(repo), '.cache', OUT);
       if (!fs.existsSync(file)) throw new Error('.cache/' + OUT + ' is missing: run node tools/content/tatoeba.js .');
       const lines = fs.readFileSync(file, 'utf8').split('\n').filter(Boolean);
       if (lines[0] !== head(pins)) throw new Error('.cache/' + OUT + ' comes from other pins of tatoeba: run node tools/content/tatoeba.js .');
       const T = { nld: new Map(), eng: new Map(), fra: new Map(), byForm: new Map() };
       const ids = s => s.split(',').map(Number);
       lines.slice(1).forEach(l => {
         const c = l.split('\t');
         if (c[0] === 'nld') T.nld.set(Number(c[1]), { id: Number(c[1]), text: c[4], owner: c[2], native: c[3] === '1', eng: ids(c[5]), fra: ids(c[6]) });
         else T[c[0]].set(Number(c[1]), { id: Number(c[1]), text: c[3], owner: c[2] });
       });
       T.nld.forEach(s => new Set(tokens(s.text)).forEach(t => {
         if (!T.byForm.has(t)) T.byForm.set(t, []);
         T.byForm.get(t).push(s);
       }));
       return T;
     }

     function rank(T, item, seq) {
       const NL = seq.NL, U = NL.util;
       const own = sequence.forms(item, NL), word = tokens(U.bare(item.nl));
       const run = s => (' ' + tokens(s).join(' ') + ' ').indexOf(' ' + word.join(' ') + ' ') >= 0;
       const pool = new Set();
       if (word.length === 1) own.forEach(f => (T.byForm.get(f) || []).forEach(s => pool.add(s)));
       else (T.byForm.get(word[0]) || []).forEach(s => { if (run(s.text)) pool.add(s); });
       const je = c => (tokens(c.nl).some(t => JE.indexOf(t) >= 0) ? 1 : 0);
       return [...pool].map(s => ({ s, tiles: U.tiles(s.text).length }))
         .filter(x => x.tiles >= 4 && x.tiles <= 8 && !sequence.unmet(x.s.text, seq.ui, seq.first, own).length &&
           !sequence.ahead(x.s.text, seq.ui, seq.first).length && !named(x.s.text, NL) && (!seq.known || tokens(x.s.text).every(seq.known)))
         .map(x => ({
           id: x.s.id, nl: x.s.text, owner: x.s.owner, native: x.s.native,
           en: x.s.eng.map(id => ({ id, text: T.eng.get(id).text, owner: T.eng.get(id).owner })),
           fr: x.s.fra.map(id => ({ id, text: T.fra.get(id).text, owner: T.fra.get(id).owner })),
           tiles: x.tiles
         }))
         .sort((a, b) => je(a) - je(b) || (b.native ? 1 : 0) - (a.native ? 1 : 0) || a.tiles - b.tiles || a.id - b.id)
         .slice(0, 8)
         .map(c => ({ id: c.id, nl: c.nl, owner: c.owner, en: c.en, fr: c.fr, tiles: c.tiles }));
     }

     module.exports = { extract, load, rank, KEYS, JE };

     if (require.main === module) {
       const repo = process.argv[2];
       if (!repo) { console.log('usage: node tools/content/tatoeba.js <repo>'); process.exit(1); }
       extract(repo).then(r => {
         console.log('ok .cache/' + OUT + ' ' + r.nld + ' Dutch sentences, ' + r.eng + ' English, ' + r.fra + ' French');
       }, e => { console.log('fail ' + e.message); process.exit(1); });
     }
     ```

### Task 11: Sourced sentences table
Class: mechanical
Ticket: {T-sentences}
Promises: none
Why: decision 5a. The sentences that task 14 takes from Tatoeba, and those task 36 writes for the words the
maintainer names, live in a table of their own, `src/content/sourced.js`. They follow other rules than the
hand-written ones in `src/content/examples.js`:
- a Tatoeba sentence is kept as Tatoeba writes it (decision 5b);
- each one carries `src`, the number of its Dutch sentence, or `'gen'`;
- each Tatoeba one is credited in `docs/attribution/tatoeba.tsv`.

This task writes the empty table and its header-only credit file. It also adds the guards that every later
merge must pass:
- a word has its sentences in one file, never both;
- each sentence has its five fields and a gap the cloze can hide;
- the credit file and the table agree;
- no sourced sentence uses a form, beyond its word's own and its gap, that the course has not taught by
  the word's unit: a demand for zero, not a budget (#12, story 39).

Files:
- Create: `src/content/sourced.js`, `docs/attribution/tatoeba.tsv`
- Modify: `build.sh` (`SRC`), `src/content/examples.js` (it attaches the table's sentences)
- Test: `test/content.js` (a new section after check 3)
- Build: `index.html`, `artifact.html`

Notes:
- **Option B: a literal table, loaded before `examples.js`.** The outline says S(...) and « after examples.js
  in SRC ». Neither works:
  - `S(...)` is local to `examples.js`, so a table cannot call it.
  - A table attached after `examples.js`, as `be.js` is, would put its sentences on the built items alone.
    `test/content.js` checks 1, 3 and 6 and `test/dehet.js` read the raw units, so they would miss them, and
    `build()` replaces `drills` anyway.

  So `sourced.js` writes `NL.content.byDutch['sourced']`, a literal table of plain objects
  `{ nl, fr, en, gap, src }`. It loads just before `examples.js`, which puts each entry on its word as
  `drills`, exactly where its own sentences go. Every reader that sees a hand-written sentence then sees a
  sourced one.
- **The keys.** Each key is the raw Dutch of the word's first listing, tokens unfilled, as in `be.js`.
  `NL.content.sourcedReport` is `{ attached, missing }`. A word that has sentences in `examples.js` keeps
  those, and the new check refuses the key.
- **No `TABLES` entry, no `HOLDS`.** `sourced` is not in `NL.content.TABLES`. Its `fr` and `en` reach
  `owed()`, `visitCourse` and the check files through `units[…].words[…].drills`, as the hand-written
  sentences do. Adding it to `HOLDS` in `test/lib/prose.js` would count every sentence twice.
- **Zero, not a budget.** The check lists every sourced sentence that uses a form the course has not
  taught by its word's unit, through `sequence.unmet` (task 10). The word's own forms and its gap do not
  count. It demands none, because #12, story 39 says « an example sentence uses only vocabulary I have
  already met », and the spec lets a budget replace a demand for zero only if it can only go down. So there
  is no `NEVER_TAUGHT_BUDGET`, and no merge (tasks 34 and 41) raises anything. Check (task 12) refuses such
  a sentence before Merge. This check is not redundant with it: it holds the merged sentences to the rule
  when the course changes around them, a word moved to a later unit for instance. Its message names each
  sentence and its forms. A Tatoeba sentence is kept as Tatoeba writes it, so the fix is to teach the form
  earlier or to remove the sentence.
- **The seeded page.** The last check loads a page with a one-sentence table in place of `sourced.js`. It
  writes that table under `.cache/sourced-…/` and removes it. The sentence's `fr` and `en` are `-` because
  only its cloze is read. The word is the first one with an article, no token, fewer than three tiles and
  no hand-written sentence. Today that is `ikengij:w24` « het Engels ».
- **Waits for 10.** The section reads `sequence` and `spelling.named` from task 10.
- **Language.** The comments and messages are in French, as in the files they join.

### Task 12: examples scripts: Split and Check
Class: mechanical
Ticket: {T-sentences}
Promises: none
Why: decisions 5a and 5b. In the fan-out `examples` (task 14), each word without an example sentence gets
one or two Tatoeba sentences, as Tatoeba writes them, each with an English and a French translation that
Tatoeba links to it. This task writes the kind's module, `tools/content/kinds/examples.js`, against task 6's
API (`parts/notes-kit.md`, section 2). It ranks with task 10's `tatoeba.rank` and holds each sentence to the
rules task 11's check holds the table to.

After this task:
- **Split** takes every word (not phrase) of the course that has no sentence and at least one candidate.
  It cuts them into batches of whole units, in course order, as few as hold about 40 rows each (`MAX`),
  with the largest as small as it can be. On the course at this point that is two batches:
  `overleven-tijd` 49 and `bakker-weekend` 27, 76 rows.
  - An input row is `{ id, stamp, copies, nl, unit, art, meaning, candidates }`. `art` is `null` for a word
    without one, and `meaning` is `NL.gloss.meaning(src)`.
  - `candidates` are `tatoeba.rank`'s, at most 8, each
    `{ id, nl, owner, en: [{ id, text, owner }], fr: [{ id, text, owner }], tiles }`.
- **A written row** is `{ id, stamp, sentences }`, with 0 to 2 sentences, plus `skip`, a reason on one line,
  when there is none. A sentence is `{ src, nl, gap, en, enSrc, fr, frSrc }`, plus `edited`, a reason on one
  line, when `en` or `fr` is not Tatoeba's text.
- **Check** gives, in English, every reason a row breaks the format:
  1. `sentences` is a list of 0 to 2 objects. With none, `skip` says why; with some, there is no `skip`.
  2. Each sentence has exactly its seven fields, plus `edited` when it applies, and `nl`, `gap`, `en` and
     `fr` each fit on one line.
  3. `src` is one of the row's candidates, and `nl` is that sentence as the pinned extract writes it.
  4. `enSrc` and `frSrc` are translations Tatoeba links to `src`. `en` and `fr` are their text, or `edited`
     says why not. `edited` with both translations as written is refused.
  5. The rules (`RULES`), at the word's unit:
     - from 4 to 8 tiles;
     - the gap is the word, one tile as `nl` writes it, that the cloze can hide;
     - nothing borrowed from a later unit;
     - no form, beyond the word's own and its gap, that the course has not taught by the word's unit, not
       even an inflection of a word it has taught (#12, story 39);
     - every form known to OpenTaal or listed in `test/data/flemish.tsv`;
     - no default name and no `{…}` token;
     - `en` and `fr` hold the same digits.
  6. Two sentences are not one sentence.
- **The stamp** is the meaning, the article and the number of hand-written sentences
  (`src/content/examples.js`). The sourced sentences are not in it: Merge writes them, and a second Merge
  must not find its own rows stale.
- **The reading list.** `readWhole` gives `'edited translation'` for a row with an `edited` sentence.

Files:
- Create: `tools/content/kinds/examples.js`
- Test: `test/tools/fanout.js` (one block, just above the summary line)

Notes:
- **Merge is task 13's.** The kind already exports `merge`, because task 6's `loadKind` requires it. It
  writes `{ nl, fr, en, gap, src }` into `sourced`. Task 13 tests it and adds the credit (`write`).
- **What the stamp leaves out.** Tasks 15 to 33 run while task 14 drafts. Task 30 writes `be` and
  `test/data/flemish.tsv`, and neither is stamped. No task adds a sentence or changes a word's article or
  meaning.
- **Where it runs.** As task 8's block does, this one copies the repo into the suite's temporary folder and
  runs the kit's scripts from there. It also copies `docs/attribution`, and empties `src/content/sourced.js`
  in the copy, so the block still holds after tasks 34 and 41 have filled the table. It writes its own
  extract of four sentences under the real pins, so it needs no `.cache/`. `anna`, `bob`, `carl` and `dora`
  are invented Tatoeba user names.
- **The measured counts.** `cut` is tested on the course's counts per unit, written into the block (76 words
  in 11 units). Split on the real repo gives the same two batches; task 14 checks it.
- **Not one form the course has not taught.** #12, story 39: « an example sentence uses only vocabulary I
  have already met ». Check refuses a sentence with any form, beyond the word's own and its gap, that no unit
  up to the word's teaches. An inflection of a taught word counts too: task 10 says why `sequence.forms`
  cannot tell one. `rank` already offers no such candidate, so on a Tatoeba row the rule repeats it; it is
  what holds the sentences that examples-gen (task 13) has the drafter write. The block checks one never-taught
  form (« vloeiend »), two, and an inflection (« leert », when the course teaches « leren »).
- **`sig`.** The kind keeps its own copy of the signature that `test/content.js` uses for the digits and
  tokens of a pair. Folding the two would change `test/content.js` for no behaviour.
- **Its names stay in its block.** It uses task 6's helpers (`same`, `ok`, `put`, `text`, `TMP`, `ROOT`,
  `course`, `kit`, `table`, `cache`, `spawnSync`) and its own `runEx`. Task 13 extends the block's end.
- **Language.** The comments are in French. What Check prints is in English, as in task 6.

- [ ] **Step 3: Write the kind.** Create `tools/content/kinds/examples.js`:
  ```js
  /* Le genre examples (décision 5a) : une ou deux phrases de Tatoeba pour chaque mot du cours qui
     n'a pas de phrase d'exemple. Split range les candidates de chacun (tools/content/tatoeba.js) et
     coupe les mots qui en ont en lots d'unités entières ; le rédacteur en prend une ou deux, telles
     que Tatoeba les écrit (5b), chacune avec une traduction anglaise et une française que Tatoeba
     lui lie ; Check refait à HEAD les règles du classement ; Merge écrit les phrases dans
     src/content/sourced.js, sous le néerlandais du mot.

     Une ligne écrite : { id, stamp, sentences: [phrase…] }, de 0 à 2 phrases, et skip, la raison
     sur une ligne, quand il n'y en a aucune. Une phrase : { src, nl, gap, en, enSrc, fr, frSrc },
     et edited, la raison sur une ligne, quand en ou fr n'est pas le texte de Tatoeba.

     L'empreinte : le sens, l'article et le nombre de phrases écrites à la main
     (src/content/examples.js). Les phrases sourcées n'y sont pas : Merge les écrit, et une
     seconde Merge ne doit pas trouver ses propres lignes périmées.

     Le genre examples-gen (tools/content/kinds/examples-gen.js) reprend d'ici RULES, cut, MAX et
     stamp. Ce que Check imprime est en anglais, comme le reste du kit. */
  const tatoeba = require('../tatoeba');
  const sequence = require('../../../test/lib/sequence');
  const spelling = require('../../../test/lib/spelling');
  const { tokens } = spelling;

  const MAX = 40;
  const FIELDS = ['src', 'nl', 'gap', 'en', 'enSrc', 'fr', 'frSrc'];

  const line = s => typeof s === 'string' && s.trim() !== '' && !/[\r\n]/.test(s);
  /* Les chiffres et les {jetons} d'un texte, triés : test/content.js tient le fr et l'en de chaque
     paire du cours à la même signature, avec la même fonction. */
  const sig = s => (String(s).match(/\d+|\{[a-z]+\}/g) || []).sort().join('|');
  const hand = s => (s.drills || []).filter(d => !('src' in d)).length;

  /* Ce que le cours donne aux règles, une fois par chargement : l'ordre des unités, la première
     unité de chaque forme, l'orthographe, et l'extrait de Tatoeba quand on le demande. */
  const memo = new WeakMap();
  function seen(C, repo) {
    if (!memo.has(C)) memo.set(C, { order: C.RAW.units.map(u => u.id), first: sequence.firstUnits(C.RAW.units), S: spelling.open(repo, C.NL), T: null });
    return memo.get(C);
  }
  const extractOf = (C, repo) => {
    const v = seen(C, repo);
    return v.T || (v.T = tatoeba.load(repo));
  };

  /* Les règles d'une phrase pour un mot, à l'unité du mot : ce que test/content.js tient des
     phrases sourcées, et ce que le classement de Tatoeba demande. « at » nomme la phrase. */
  function RULES(d, at, src, C, repo) {
    const U = C.NL.util, v = seen(C, repo), out = [];
    const ui = v.order.indexOf(src.unit), own = sequence.forms(src, C.NL);
    const ts = U.tiles(d.nl), gap = tokens(d.gap);
    if (ts.length < 4 || ts.length > 8) out.push(at + ' has ' + ts.length + ' tiles: 4 to 8');
    const cloze = C.NL.ex.get('cloze').build(Object.assign({}, src, { drills: [d] }));
    if (cloze.gap !== d.gap || cloze.shown === d.nl || gap.length !== 1 || !own.has(gap[0])) {
      out.push(at + ': gap « ' + d.gap + ' » is not the word, one tile as nl writes it, that the cloze can hide');
    }
    const ahead = sequence.ahead(d.nl, ui, v.first);
    if (ahead.length) out.push(at + ' borrows from a later unit: ' + ahead.join(', '));
    /* #12, récit 39 : rien que le cours n'enseigne jamais, pas même une forme fléchie d'un mot vu. */
    const never = sequence.unmet(d.nl, ui, v.first, new Set([...own, ...gap])).filter(t => ahead.indexOf(t) < 0);
    if (never.length) out.push(at + ' uses forms the course never teaches: ' + never.join(', '));
    const unknown = tokens(d.nl).filter(t => !v.S.known(t));
    if (unknown.length) out.push(at + ': ' + unknown.map(t => '« ' + t + ' »').join(', ') + ' not a form OpenTaal knows');
    if ([d.nl, d.en, d.fr].some(s => spelling.named(s, C.NL))) out.push(at + ' names no one by default and holds no {…} token');
    if (sig(d.en) !== sig(d.fr)) out.push(at + ': en and fr do not hold the same digits');
    return out;
  }

  /* Les lots : des unités entières, dans l'ordre du cours, autant de lots qu'il en faut pour que
     chacun tienne à peu près MAX lignes, et le plus gros le plus petit possible. Un lot porte le
     nom de sa première unité, et de sa dernière quand il en a plusieurs. */
  function cut(groups, max) {
    const total = groups.reduce((n, g) => n + g.rows.length, 0);
    if (!total) return [];
    const want = Math.ceil(total / max);
    const pack = cap => groups.reduce((out, g) => {
      const last = out[out.length - 1];
      if (last && last.n + g.rows.length <= cap) { last.units.push(g); last.n += g.rows.length; } else out.push({ units: [g], n: g.rows.length });
      return out;
    }, []);
    let cap = Math.max.apply(null, [Math.ceil(total / want)].concat(groups.map(g => g.rows.length)));
    while (pack(cap).length > want) cap++;
    return pack(cap).map(p => ({
      batch: p.units[0].unit + (p.units.length > 1 ? '-' + p.units[p.units.length - 1].unit : ''),
      rows: [].concat.apply([], p.units.map(g => g.rows))
    }));
  }

  /* Split : chaque mot sans phrase qui a au moins une candidate, avec ses candidates. */
  function split(C, ctx) {
    const T = extractOf(C, ctx.repo), v = seen(C, ctx.repo), groups = [];
    C.sources.forEach(s => {
      if (s.kind !== 'word' || (s.drills && s.drills.length)) return;
      const candidates = tatoeba.rank(T, s, { NL: C.NL, first: v.first, ui: v.order.indexOf(s.unit), known: v.S.known });
      if (!candidates.length) return;
      if (!groups.length || groups[groups.length - 1].unit !== s.unit) groups.push({ unit: s.unit, rows: [] });
      groups[groups.length - 1].rows.push({ id: s.id, nl: s.nl, unit: s.unit, art: s.art || null, meaning: C.NL.gloss.meaning(s), candidates });
    });
    return cut(groups, MAX);
  }

  /* Check : les phrases prises parmi les candidates de la ligne, telles que l'extrait épinglé les
     écrit, leurs traductions liées, et les règles. */
  function check(row, input, ctx) {
    const out = [], list = row.sentences;
    if (!Array.isArray(list) || list.length > 2 || list.some(d => !d || typeof d !== 'object' || Array.isArray(d))) return ['sentences is a list of 0 to 2 sentences'];
    if (!list.length && !line(row.skip)) out.push('a row with no sentence says why in skip, on one line');
    if (list.length && 'skip' in row) out.push('skip is for a row with no sentence');
    if (!list.length) return out;
    const C = ctx.course(), src = C.byId(input.id);
    let T;
    try { T = extractOf(C, ctx.repo); } catch (e) { return out.concat([e.message]); }
    list.forEach((d, j) => {
      const at = 'sentence ' + (j + 1);
      const keys = Object.keys(d).filter(k => k !== 'edited');
      if (keys.slice().sort().join() !== FIELDS.slice().sort().join()) {
        out.push(at + ' has the fields ' + FIELDS.join(', ') + ' (and edited when a translation is not Tatoeba\'s), not ' + Object.keys(d).join(', '));
        return;
      }
      if (![d.nl, d.gap, d.en, d.fr].every(line)) { out.push(at + ': nl, gap, en and fr are each a string on one line'); return; }
      const s = T.nld.get(d.src);
      if (!(input.candidates || []).some(c => c.id === d.src) || !s) { out.push(at + ': src ' + d.src + ' is not one of the row\'s candidates'); return; }
      if (d.nl !== s.text) out.push(at + ': nl is not Tatoeba\'s sentence ' + d.src + ', « ' + s.text + ' »: a sentence is taken as Tatoeba writes it');
      const changed = [];
      [['en', 'eng'], ['fr', 'fra']].forEach(([l, k]) => {
        const id = d[l + 'Src'], t = T[k].get(id);
        if (s[k].indexOf(id) < 0 || !t) { out.push(at + ': ' + l + 'Src ' + id + ' is not a translation Tatoeba links to ' + d.src); return; }
        if (d[l] !== t.text) changed.push(l + ' « ' + d[l] + ' » is not Tatoeba\'s ' + id + ', « ' + t.text + ' »');
      });
      if (changed.length && !line(d.edited)) changed.forEach(c => out.push(at + ': ' + c + ': take it as written, or say why in edited'));
      if (!changed.length && 'edited' in d) out.push(at + ': edited is for a translation that is not Tatoeba\'s, and both are');
      RULES(d, at, src, C, ctx.repo).forEach(r => out.push(r));
    });
    if (list.length === 2 && (list[0].src === list[1].src || C.NL.util.norm(list[0].nl) === C.NL.util.norm(list[1].nl))) out.push('the two sentences are one sentence');
    return out;
  }

  module.exports = {
    stamp: ['meaning', 'art', hand],
    fields: ['sentences'],
    optional: ['skip'],
    tables: ['sourced'],
    split,
    check,
    merge: row => ({ sourced: row.sentences.length ? row.sentences.map(d => ({ nl: d.nl, fr: d.fr, en: d.en, gap: d.gap, src: d.src })) : undefined }),
    readWhole: row => (row.sentences || []).some(d => 'edited' in d) ? 'edited translation' : '',
    MAX, RULES, cut
  };
  ```

### Task 13: examples Merge, and the examples-gen scripts
Class: mechanical
Ticket: {T-sentences}
Promises: none
Why: decisions 5a and 5c. Two things are still missing for the sentences to reach the course:
- **The `examples` Merge.** Task 12's kind already maps a row to its sentences. This task adds the credit
  that every Tatoeba sentence owes under CC BY: Merge rewrites `docs/attribution/tatoeba.tsv` from what
  `src/content/sourced.js` holds.
- **The kind `examples-gen`.** For the words the maintainer names at gate 35 (task 35), because Tatoeba gives
  them no good sentence, a drafter writes one sentence each (task 36). Its reader first writes their own
  English and French of the Dutch, the second, independent translation that decision 5c asks for.

After this task:
- **`examples` Merge** writes each taken row's sentences under the word's raw Dutch in `sourced.js`, as
  `{ nl, fr, en, gap, src }`, in the row's order. A row with no sentence writes nothing. Its `write` then
  rewrites `docs/attribution/tatoeba.tsv` whole, keeping its comments and its line endings:
  - one line per Tatoeba sentence that `sourced.js` holds, sorted by word, then by number:
    `word nld nld_owner eng eng_owner fra fra_owner adapted`, separated by tabs;
  - a sentence of this Merge takes its authors from its input row's candidate. An earlier line is kept as it
    was, as long as `sourced.js` still holds its sentence;
  - an author Tatoeba does not name is written `-`. `adapted` names the translations the row changed
    (`edited`): `-`, `en`, `fr` or `en fr`.

  It prints `ok tatoeba.tsv <n> rows`.
- **`examples-gen` Split** reads `named.txt` in the kind's folder: one raw Dutch per line, and a blank line
  or a line starting with `#` does not count.
  - Without the file, it fails: `named.txt is missing: …`.
  - It refuses a name that is not a word of the course, a word that already has sentences, and a word named
    twice, all in one line.
  - It cuts the named words into batches of whole units, as `examples` does. An input row is
    `{ id, stamp, copies, nl, unit, art, meaning }`, and the stamp is `examples`'.
  - A file that names no word cuts 0 rows, and Merge then prints `ok examples-gen 0 taken, 0 dropped` and
    writes nothing.
- **`examples-gen` rows and Check.** A written row is `{ id, stamp, sentence: { nl, gap, en, fr } }`. Check
  holds the sentence to `examples`' `RULES`, so it uses nothing the course has not taught by the word's unit
  (#12, story 39), and to the course's « you »: `ge` or `gij`, never one of `tatoeba.JE` (`je`, `jij`,
  `jou`, `jouw`).
- **The verdict.** `verdictFields` is `['en', 'fr']`, and `checkVerdict` requires both on every verdict, each
  on one line: the reader's own translations of `nl`, written before reading the row's.
- **`examples-gen` Merge** writes `[{ nl, fr, en, gap, src: 'gen' }]` into `sourced`. It has no `write`, so
  the credit file does not change: a generated sentence owes Tatoeba nothing.
- **The reading list.** `readWhole` gives `'generated sentence'` for every row, so the maintainer reads each
  one whole (task 33).

Files:
- Create: `tools/content/kinds/examples-gen.js`
- Modify: `tools/content/kinds/examples.js` (the credit, `write`, and the exports `CREDITS` and `line`)
- Test: `test/tools/fanout.js` (the end of task 12's block)

Notes:
- **Why a second Merge changes nothing.** `examples` stamps the meaning, the article and the number of
  hand-written sentences, not the sourced ones. So a second Merge finds its rows fresh, writes the same
  values and the same credit, and the test checks that the file is unchanged.
- **The credit and task 11's check.** `test/content.js` holds `tatoeba.tsv` and `sourced.js` to each other:
  every sentence with a numeric `src` is credited, and nothing else is. `write` is what keeps that true after
  a merge. It rebuilds the file from `sourced.js`, so a sentence Merge replaced loses its line.
- **What the test's copy holds before Merge.** The block puts a sentence of « sorry », with its credit line,
  into the copy's `sourced.js`, plus one credit line too many (« drie », 777). After Merge, the first is
  kept and the second is gone.
- **The folders.** The test runs `examples-gen`'s Split in four folders under its copy, named after what
  they hold: `sans-liste` (no `named.txt`), `mauvaise` (a bad one), `aucun` (no word named) and `drafts`.
  It runs `examples`' Split once more in `encore`, to see that a word with sentences is no longer offered.
- **Who reads what.** Task 14's Format follows `examples`' rows. Task 34 runs its Merge. Task 35 writes
  `named.txt`, task 36's Format follows `examples-gen`'s rows and verdict, and task 41 runs its Merge.
- **Language.** The comments are in French. What Split, Check and Merge print is in English.

     ```js
        cette Merge, prises dans leur ligne d'entrée, et celles d'avant, gardées telles qu'elles
        étaient. Triées par mot, puis par numéro. */
     function credit(taken, ctx) {
       const file = path.join(ctx.repo, 'docs', 'attribution', 'tatoeba.tsv');
       const was = fs.readFileSync(file, 'utf8'), eol = /\r\n/.test(was) ? '\r\n' : '\n';
       const all = was.split(/\r?\n/), head = all.filter(l => l[0] === '#');
       const old = all.filter(l => l && l[0] !== '#' && l !== CREDITS).map(l => l.split('\t'));
       const sourced = table.load(path.join(ctx.repo, 'src', 'content', 'sourced.js')).entries;
       const held = new Set();
       Object.keys(sourced).forEach(nl => sourced[nl].forEach(d => { if (Number.isInteger(d.src)) held.add(nl + '\t' + d.src); }));
       const rows = new Map();
       old.forEach(c => { if (held.has(c[0] + '\t' + c[1])) rows.set(c[0] + '\t' + c[1], c); });
       const owner = o => o || '-';
       taken.forEach(t => (t.row.sentences || []).forEach(d => {
         const c = t.input.candidates.find(x => x.id === d.src);
         const en = c.en.find(x => x.id === d.enSrc), fr = c.fr.find(x => x.id === d.frSrc);
         const adapted = [d.en !== en.text ? 'en' : '', d.fr !== fr.text ? 'fr' : ''].filter(Boolean).join(' ') || '-';
         rows.set(t.src.nl + '\t' + d.src, [t.src.nl, d.src, owner(c.owner), d.enSrc, owner(en.owner), d.frSrc, owner(fr.owner), adapted]);
       }));
       const sorted = [...rows.values()].sort((a, b) => (a[0] < b[0] ? -1 : a[0] > b[0] ? 1 : Number(a[1]) - Number(b[1])));
       fs.writeFileSync(file, head.concat([CREDITS], sorted.map(c => c.join('\t'))).join(eol) + eol);
       return ['ok tatoeba.tsv ' + sorted.length + ' rows'];
     }
     ```
  5. Same file. In `module.exports`, replace
     ```js
       merge: row => ({ sourced: row.sentences.length ? row.sentences.map(d => ({ nl: d.nl, fr: d.fr, en: d.en, gap: d.gap, src: d.src })) : undefined }),
       readWhole: row => (row.sentences || []).some(d => 'edited' in d) ? 'edited translation' : '',
       MAX, RULES, cut
     ```
     with
     ```js
       merge: row => ({ sourced: row.sentences.length ? row.sentences.map(d => ({ nl: d.nl, fr: d.fr, en: d.en, gap: d.gap, src: d.src })) : undefined }),
       write: credit,
       readWhole: row => (row.sentences || []).some(d => 'edited' in d) ? 'edited translation' : '',
       MAX, CREDITS, RULES, cut, line
     ```
  6. Create `tools/content/kinds/examples-gen.js`:
     ```js
     /* Le genre examples-gen (décision 5c) : une phrase écrite pour le cours, pour chaque mot que le
        mainteneur a nommé à la porte des phrases, parce que Tatoeba n'en donne pas de bonne. Les
        mots nommés sont dans named.txt, à côté des lots : le néerlandais du mot tel que son premier
        listage l'écrit, un par ligne ; une ligne vide ou qui commence par « # » ne compte pas. Un
        fichier sans mot coupe zéro ligne, et Merge n'écrit rien.

        Une ligne écrite : { id, stamp, sentence: { nl, gap, en, fr } }. Check tient les règles des
        phrases sourcées (tools/content/kinds/examples.js, RULES), et le tutoiement du cours : ge ou
        gij, jamais je, jij, jou ni jouw. Le lecteur écrit sa propre traduction anglaise et française
        de nl avant de lire celles de la ligne, et les donne dans son verdict (en, fr) : c'est la
        seconde traduction, indépendante, que la décision demande. Chaque phrase écrite est lue en
        entier par le mainteneur (readWhole). Merge l'écrit dans src/content/sourced.js avec
        src 'gen' ; aucun crédit à Tatoeba, puisqu'elle n'en vient pas. */
     const fs = require('fs'), path = require('path');
     const examples = require('./examples');
     const { JE } = require('../tatoeba');
     const { tokens } = require('../../../test/lib/spelling');

     const FIELDS = ['nl', 'gap', 'en', 'fr'];
     const { line } = examples;

     /* Split : les mots nommés, chacun un mot du cours encore sans phrase, une fois. */
     function split(C, ctx) {
       const file = path.join(ctx.kindDir, 'named.txt');
       if (!fs.existsSync(file)) throw new Error('named.txt is missing: it holds the words the maintainer named, one per line, or none');
       const named = fs.readFileSync(file, 'utf8').split(/\r?\n/).map(l => l.trim()).filter(l => l && l[0] !== '#');
       const words = C.sources.filter(s => s.kind === 'word'), bad = [];
       named.forEach((nl, k) => {
         const s = words.find(w => w.nl === nl);
         if (named.indexOf(nl) < k) bad.push('« ' + nl + ' » twice');
         else if (!s) bad.push('« ' + nl + ' » is not a word of the course');
         else if (s.drills && s.drills.length) bad.push('« ' + nl + ' » already has sentences');
       });
       if (bad.length) throw new Error('named.txt: ' + bad.join('; '));
       const groups = [];
       words.filter(s => named.indexOf(s.nl) >= 0).forEach(s => {
         if (!groups.length || groups[groups.length - 1].unit !== s.unit) groups.push({ unit: s.unit, rows: [] });
         groups[groups.length - 1].rows.push({ id: s.id, nl: s.nl, unit: s.unit, art: s.art || null, meaning: C.NL.gloss.meaning(s) });
       });
       return examples.cut(groups, examples.MAX);
     }

     /* Check : la phrase, ses quatre champs, les règles, et ge ou gij. */
     function check(row, input, ctx) {
       const d = row.sentence;
       if (!d || typeof d !== 'object' || Array.isArray(d) || Object.keys(d).sort().join() !== FIELDS.slice().sort().join()) {
         return ['sentence has the fields ' + FIELDS.join(', ')];
       }
       if (!FIELDS.every(k => line(d[k]))) return ['sentence: nl, gap, en and fr are each a string on one line'];
       const C = ctx.course(), out = examples.RULES(d, 'sentence', C.byId(input.id), C, ctx.repo);
       const je = tokens(d.nl).filter(t => JE.indexOf(t) >= 0);
       if (je.length) out.push('sentence: ' + je.map(t => '« ' + t + ' »').join(', ') + ' is not how the course says you: ge or gij');
       return out;
     }

     /* Le verdict : la traduction du lecteur, écrite de nl avant de lire celles de la ligne. */
     const checkVerdict = v => (line(v.en) && line(v.fr) ? [] : ['a verdict carries the reader\'s own en and fr of nl, each on one line']);

     module.exports = {
       stamp: examples.stamp,
       fields: ['sentence'],
       verdictFields: ['en', 'fr'],
       tables: ['sourced'],
       split,
       check,
       checkVerdict,
       merge: row => ({ sourced: [{ nl: row.sentence.nl, fr: row.sentence.fr, en: row.sentence.en, gap: row.sentence.gap, src: 'gen' }] }),
       readWhole: () => 'generated sentence'
     };
     ```
