  4. Create `tools/content/lib/explain.js`:
     ```js
     /* Les deux genres d'explications : explanations-be, chaque mot et chaque phrase dont la forme
        flamande n'est pas le néerlandais, et explanations, tous les autres. Leurs modules
        (tools/content/kinds/) ne font que choisir leur part ; ce qu'ils ont en commun est ici.

          const X = require('../lib/explain');
          X.kind('be')        le genre explanations-be : un lot be-words et un lot be-phrases, coupés par
                              unités entières au-delà de MAX lignes
          X.kind('rest')      le genre explanations : un lot par unité, dans l'ordre du cours
          X.flemish(src, NL)  vrai quand l'élément est du genre explanations-be
          X.chunks(name, rows)  des lignes en lots de MAX au plus, sans couper une unité

        Une ligne d'entrée porte, en plus de ce que le kit écrit (stamp, copies) :
          nl, kind, unit      la source
          be                  sa forme flamande, ou null
          meaning             son sens, langue par langue (NL.gloss.meaning)
          note                sa note telle que notes.js la tient, ou null
          also                ses « on dit aussi », [] s'il n'en a pas
          siblings            les éléments du même sens : { nl, be }
          vlaams              vrai quand « Comment le dit-on ici ? » la pose
          right               la bonne réponse de cet exercice, quand vlaams ; null sinon
          labelled            les sens belges que le Wiktionnaire anglais donne au néerlandais lui-même
                              (« pos (étiquettes): sens »), ou null
        Une ligne écrite porte note, une paire { fr, en } que Check lit avec les règles de checkNote.
        Les raisons sont en anglais : ce sont les agents du kit qui les lisent. */
     const path = require('path');
     const kaikki = require('../kaikki');
     const spelling = require(path.join(__dirname, '..', '..', '..', 'test', 'lib', 'spelling'));
     const { dutchWords } = require(path.join(__dirname, '..', '..', '..', 'test', 'lib', 'dutch'));

     /* Ce que l'empreinte couvre : ce que le rédacteur lit et ce que Merge écrit. Merge écrit la
        note, donc la relancer après un succès refuse comme périmée chaque ligne dont elle a changé
        la note : une tâche de fusion ne la lance qu'une fois. */
     const STAMP = ['be', 'meaning', 'note', 'also'];
     const MAX = 40;
     const NOTE_MAX = 160;
     const LANGS = ['fr', 'en'];
     /* Les guillemets de chaque langue. */
     const QUOTES = { en: ['“', '”'], fr: ['«', '»'] };
     /* Les mots-outils d'une langue qui n'ont rien à faire dans l'autre, hors des guillemets. « but »
        n'y est pas : « le but » est français. */
     const FR_IN_EN = 'le la les un une des du et est sont avec dans sur qui que pas ne il elle nous vous ce cette ces au aux mais ou où se sa ses leur très quand comme'.split(' ');
     const EN_IN_FR = 'the and of is are to with for you it this that not was were have has your what when which who from by if into do does'.split(' ');

     /* Les mots d'un texte, en minuscules, comme dutchWords les découpe. */
     const words = s => String(s).toLowerCase().split(/[^\p{L}\p{N}]+/u).filter(Boolean);

     const flemish = (src, NL) => typeof src.be === 'string' && NL.util.norm(src.be) !== NL.util.norm(src.nl);
     /* « Comment le dit-on ici ? » pose l'élément : un barreau de son genre l'offre, et l'élément s'y prête. */
     const vlaams = (src, NL) => NL.srs.RUNGS[src.kind].some(set => set.indexOf('vlaams') >= 0) && NL.srs.supports(src, 'vlaams');
     /* La bonne réponse de « Comment le dit-on ici ? », telle que l'exercice la juge. */
     function right(src, NL) {
       const ex = NL.ex.get('vlaams'), a = ex.answer(ex.build(src));
       if (typeof a !== 'string' || !a) throw new Error(src.id + ': the vlaams exercise gives no answer');
       return a;
     }
     /* Les sens belges du néerlandais lui-même : un mot sans son article, une phrase sans sa
        ponctuation finale. */
     function labelled(src, belgian, U) {
       const lemma = (src.kind === 'word' ? U.bare(src.nl) : src.nl.replace(/[.!?…]+$/, '')).toLowerCase();
       const senses = belgian.get(lemma);
       return senses ? senses.map(s => s.pos + ' (' + s.labels.join(', ') + '): ' + s.gloss) : null;
     }

     function rowOf(s, C, belgian) {
       const NL = C.NL, G = NL.gloss, v = vlaams(s, NL);
       return {
         id: s.id,
         nl: s.nl,
         kind: s.kind,
         unit: s.unit,
         be: typeof s.be === 'string' ? s.be : null,
         meaning: G.meaning(s),
         note: s.note || null,
         also: (s.also || []).slice(),
         siblings: C.sources.filter(o => o !== s && G.sameSense(s, o)).map(o => ({ nl: o.nl, be: typeof o.be === 'string' ? o.be : null })),
         vlaams: v,
         right: v ? right(s, NL) : null,
         labelled: labelled(s, belgian, NL.util)
       };
     }

     /* Des lignes dans l'ordre du cours, en lots de MAX au plus, sans couper une unité (une unité de
        plus de MAX lignes fait un lot à elle seule) : name, ou name-1, name-2… quand il en faut plusieurs. */
     function chunks(name, rows) {
       const out = [];
       let unit = null, these = [];
       const close = () => {
         const last = out[out.length - 1];
         if (last && last.length + these.length <= MAX) out[out.length - 1] = last.concat(these);
         else if (these.length) out.push(these);
       };
       rows.forEach(r => {
         if (r.unit !== unit) { close(); unit = r.unit; these = []; }
         these.push(r);
       });
       close();
       return out.length === 1 ? [{ batch: name, rows: out[0] }] : out.map((rows, k) => ({ batch: name + '-' + (k + 1), rows }));
     }

     function split(part) {
       return (C, ctx) => {
         const belgian = kaikki.belgian(ctx.repo);
         const mine = C.sources.filter(s => flemish(s, C.NL) === (part === 'be'));
         if (part === 'be') {
           return ['word', 'phrase'].reduce((acc, k) =>
             acc.concat(chunks('be-' + k + 's', mine.filter(s => s.kind === k).map(s => rowOf(s, C, belgian)))), []);
         }
         return C.RAW.units.map(u => ({ batch: u.id, rows: mine.filter(s => s.unit === u.id).map(s => rowOf(s, C, belgian)) }));
       };
     }

     /* L'orthographe et le néerlandais du cours, lus une fois par lecture d'un lot. */
     const memo = new WeakMap();
     function tools(ctx) {
       if (!memo.has(ctx)) {
         const NL = ctx.course().NL;
         memo.set(ctx, { NL, S: spelling.open(ctx.repo, NL), dutch: dutchWords(NL) });
       }
       return memo.get(ctx);
     }

     /* Un texte et ses citations : { quoted, outside, ok }. outside remplace chaque citation par
        « # », pour que la ponctuation qu'elle porte ne compte pas. ok est faux quand un guillemet
        est seul, imbriqué, ou qu'une citation est vide. */
     function quotes(s, L) {
       const [open, close] = QUOTES[L], quoted = [];
       let depth = 0, cur = '', outside = '', ok = true;
       Array.from(s).forEach(ch => {
         if (ch === open) { if (depth) ok = false; depth = 1; cur = ''; }
         else if (ch === close) {
           if (!depth || !cur.trim()) ok = false;
           else { quoted.push(cur.trim()); outside += '#'; }
           depth = 0;
         } else if (depth) cur += ch;
         else outside += ch;
       });
       if (depth) ok = false;
       return { quoted, outside, ok };
     }
     const sig = s => (String(s).match(/\d+|\{[a-z]+\}/g) || []).sort().join('|');
     /* Les phrases d'un texte : chaque fin (. ! ? …) suivie d'un blanc ou de la fin, et une de plus
        quand le texte ne finit pas sur l'une d'elles. */
     const sentences = s => (s.match(/[.!?…]+(?=\s|$)/g) || []).length + (/[.!?…]$/.test(s.trim()) ? 0 : 1);
     const list = ws => ws.map(w => '« ' + w + ' »').join(', ');

     /* Ce que la ligne rend citable, même hors des listes d'orthographe : son néerlandais, sa forme
        flamande, ses « on dit aussi ». */
     const ownForms = input => [input.nl, input.be || ''].concat(input.also);

     /* Les raisons qu'une note ne passe pas. */
     function checkNote(row, input, ctx) {
       const n = row.note;
       if (!n || typeof n !== 'object' || Array.isArray(n) || Object.keys(n).sort().join() !== 'en,fr' ||
         LANGS.some(l => typeof n[l] !== 'string' || !n[l].trim() || n[l] !== n[l].trim())) {
         return ['note is { "fr": …, "en": … }, each a text with no space at either end'];
       }
       const T = tools(ctx), U = T.NL.util, G = T.NL.gloss, why = [];
       const q = {}, unread = [];
       LANGS.forEach(l => {
         const s = n[l];
         if (Array.from(s).length > NOTE_MAX) why.push('note.' + l + ' is ' + Array.from(s).length + ' characters: at most ' + NOTE_MAX);
         if (/[<\n\r"]/.test(s)) why.push('note.' + l + ' holds <, a newline or a straight quote "');
         const other = QUOTES[l === 'en' ? 'fr' : 'en'];
         if (s.indexOf(other[0]) >= 0 || s.indexOf(other[1]) >= 0) { why.push('note.' + l + ' quotes with ' + QUOTES[l].join(' ') + ' only'); unread.push(l); }
         q[l] = quotes(s, l);
         if (!q[l].ok) { why.push('note.' + l + ' has a quote mark without its pair, a quote inside a quote, or an empty quote'); unread.push(l); }
         const k = sentences(q[l].outside);
         if (k > 2) why.push('note.' + l + ' has ' + k + ' sentences: at most 2');
         Object.keys(T.NL.content.DEFAULTS).forEach(key => {
           const name = T.NL.content.DEFAULTS[key];
           if (new RegExp('(^|[^\\p{L}])' + name.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g, '\\$&') + '($|[^\\p{L}])', 'iu').test(s)) why.push('note.' + l + ' names « ' + name + ' »: write {' + key + '}');
         });
         if (U.norm(s) === U.norm(G.of(input.meaning, l))) why.push('note.' + l + ' only repeats the meaning');
         const foreign = l === 'en' ? FR_IN_EN : EN_IN_FR;
         const hit = U.uniq(words(q[l].outside).filter(w => foreign.indexOf(w) >= 0));
         if (hit.length) why.push('note.' + l + ' uses ' + (l === 'en' ? 'French' : 'English') + ' words outside quotes: ' + list(hit));
       });
       if (sig(n.fr) !== sig(n.en)) why.push('note.fr and note.en hold different digits or {…} tokens');
       /* La suite lit les citations : il faut qu'elles se lisent, avec les guillemets de leur langue. */
       if (unread.length) return why;

       const set = l => U.uniq(q[l].quoted.map(U.norm)).sort();
       const fr = set('fr'), en = set('en');
       if (fr.join('|') !== en.join('|')) {
         why.push('note.fr and note.en quote different Dutch: only en ' + list(en.filter(x => fr.indexOf(x) < 0)) + '; only fr ' + list(fr.filter(x => en.indexOf(x) < 0)));
       }
       const own = new Set([].concat(...ownForms(input).map(f => spelling.tokens(f))));
       U.uniq(q.en.quoted.concat(q.fr.quoted)).forEach(seg => {
         const bad = U.uniq(spelling.tokens(seg).filter(t => !T.S.known(t) && !own.has(t)));
         if (bad.length) why.push('« ' + seg + ' » is quoted, but ' + list(bad) + ' is not Dutch that OpenTaal, flemish.tsv or this row knows: quotes hold Dutch only, a translation goes in parentheses');
       });
       const names = new Set([].concat(...Object.keys(T.NL.content.DEFAULTS).map(k => words(T.NL.content.DEFAULTS[k]))));
       const bareIn = l => new Set(words(q[l].outside.replace(/\{[a-z]+\}/g, ' ')).filter(w => w.length > 1 && T.dutch.has(w) && !names.has(w)));
       const enBare = bareIn('en'), both = Array.from(bareIn('fr')).filter(w => enBare.has(w));
       if (both.length) why.push(list(both) + ' is Dutch of the course, outside quotes in fr and in en: quote it, or say it another way');
       return why;
     }

     function kind(part) {
       return {
         stamp: STAMP,
         fields: ['note'],
         tables: ['notes'],
         split: split(part),
         check: checkNote,
         merge: row => ({ notes: row.note })
       };
     }

     module.exports = { kind, flemish, chunks };
     ```

     /* Le genre explanations : la note de chaque mot et de chaque phrase que explanations-be n'a pas.

### Task 28: explanations scripts: the « on dit aussi » and the decoys, and also.js as a table
Class: mechanical
Ticket: {T-explanations}
Promises: none
Why: decisions 8a and 8d. Task 27 wrote the two explanations kinds with the note alone. A row now also writes
its « on dit aussi » forms (decision 8a puts them in the same rows), and a Flemish row whose item
« Comment le dit-on ici ? » asks writes two decoys for that exercise (decision 8d).
- **`also`.** Every row writes `also`, a list of Dutch forms, `[]` for none. Each form becomes one more answer
  that the typed exercise accepts (`NL.ex.accepted`), so Check refuses:
  - an entry that is not a text on one line, or that holds more than one form (`/`, `;`, or a comma in a word);
  - the item's Dutch, or a Flemish form that `be.js` gives it;
  - the same form twice;
  - a noun without its article;
  - a word that OpenTaal and `flemish.tsv` do not know, as `test/content.js` refuses it;
  - the Dutch of another item, unless that item is a sibling of the same sense or the source already holds the
    form.
- **`decoys`.** An `explanations-be` row whose item the exercise asks (`vlaams`) writes exactly two decoys, two
  wrong answers to « Comment le dit-on ici ? ». Any other row writes none. Check refuses a pair:
  - whose two decoys are one answer after normalisation;
  - with a decoy that the course accepts for any item, the row's own `also` included;
  - with a decoy that does not end with the right answer's final punctuation;
  - with a decoy outside 60 % to 140 % of the right answer's length in characters;
  - with a decoy further from the Dutch than the right answer is, by more than 0.15 of `U.ratio`.
- **Merge.** It writes `notes.js`, `also.js` and, for `explanations-be`, `decoys.js`. An empty `also` list, or
  a row without decoys, removes the key.
- **`also.js` becomes a table.** Merge writes task 6's table format (`tools/content/lib/table.js`), keyed by
  the Dutch. Today `src/content/also.js` attaches its forms to the lexicon rows itself and reports through
  `NL.content.alsoReport`. It becomes a table that `TABLES` attaches at load, as `be.js`, `notes.js` and
  `decoys.js` are. A one-off script converts it and checks that the 430 items are built the same.
- **The reviewer.** A row that adds a form to `also` is read whole (`readWhole` gives `new also`): it adds an
  answer that the course accepts.
- **The course's Dutch.** Decoys and `also` forms show on screen in Dutch. `test/lib/dutch.js` (task 27) lists
  `also` and `decoys` among the Dutch keys, so `test/lang.js` 3a reads their words as the course's Dutch.

        accepte (NL.ex.accepted) : une seule forme néerlandaise, ni la source, ni sa forme flamande, un
        nom avec son article, l'orthographe que test/content.js exige, et pas le néerlandais d'un autre
        élément d'un autre sens. Une forme que la source tient déjà, ou celle d'un frère de sens, reste. */
     function checkAlso(row, input, ctx) {
       const also = row.also;
       if (!Array.isArray(also) || !also.every(oneLine)) return ['also is a list of Dutch forms, [] for none, each a text on one line with no space at either end'];
       const T = tools(ctx), U = T.NL.util, word = input.kind === 'word', why = [];
       const key = f => U.norm(word ? U.bare(f) : f);
       const art = (T.C.byId(input.id) || {}).art;
       const flemishForms = T.NL.content.beVariants(input).map(key);
       const near = new Set(input.siblings.map(s => key(s.nl)).concat(input.also.map(key)));
       const seen = new Set();
       also.forEach(f => {
         const k = key(f), say = s => why.push('also « ' + f + ' » ' + s);
         if (/[/;]/.test(f) || (word && f.indexOf(',') >= 0)) return say('holds more than one form: one form per entry');
         if (seen.has(k)) return why.push('also lists « ' + f + ' » twice');
         seen.add(k);
         if (k === key(input.nl)) return say('is the Dutch itself');
         if (flemishForms.indexOf(k) >= 0) return say('is a Flemish form in be.js');
         if (art && !/^(de|het) \S/i.test(f)) say('drops the article of « ' + input.nl + ' »');
         const bad = U.uniq(spelling.tokens(f).filter(t => !T.S.known(t)));
         if (bad.length) why.push('also « ' + f + ' »: ' + list(bad) + ' is not Dutch that OpenTaal or flemish.tsv knows: leave it out, and say why in unsure if it is Flemish');
         if (near.has(k)) return;
         const other = T.C.sources.find(s => s.id !== input.id && key(s.nl) === k);
         if (other) say('is the Dutch of ' + other.id + ', which is not of the same sense: an answer to one is not right for the other');
       });
       return why;
     }

     const PAIR = 'decoys is two wrong answers to « Comment le dit-on ici ? », each a text on one line with no space at either end';
     /* Les raisons que les leurres ne passent pas : deux mauvaises réponses à « Comment le dit-on
        ici ? », qu'aucun élément n'accepte, qui finissent comme la réponse, en ont la longueur à 40 %
        près, et ne s'éloignent pas du néerlandais plus que la réponse (0,15 de rapport au plus). Les
        « on dit aussi » de la ligne comptent pour sa source ; ceux qu'une autre ligne du lot écrit ne
        comptent qu'après Merge, où test/content.js les voit. */
     function checkDecoys(row, input, ctx) {
       const d = row.decoys;
       if (!input.vlaams) return d === undefined ? [] : ['decoys are for a row that « Comment le dit-on ici ? » asks (vlaams), and this one is not'];
       if (!Array.isArray(d) || d.length !== 2 || !d.every(oneLine)) return [PAIR];
       const T = tools(ctx), NL = T.NL, U = NL.util;
       if (U.norm(d[0]) === U.norm(d[1])) return ['decoys « ' + d[0] + ' » and « ' + d[1] + ' » are one answer'];
       const mine = NL.ex.accepted(Object.assign({}, input, { also: Array.isArray(row.also) ? row.also : input.also }));
       const end = s => (s.match(/[.!?…]+$/) || [''])[0];
       const shown = e => e ? '« ' + e + ' »' : 'no punctuation';
       const n = Array.from(input.right).length, lo = Math.ceil(n * 0.6), hi = Math.floor(n * 1.4);
       const least = U.ratio(input.right, input.nl) - 0.15, why = [];
       d.forEach(x => {
         const keys = U.uniq([U.norm(x), U.norm(U.bare(x))]), say = s => why.push('decoy « ' + x + ' » ' + s);
         const who = U.uniq((keys.some(k => mine.indexOf(k) >= 0) ? [input.id] : [])
           .concat(...keys.map(k => (T.owners.get(k) || []).filter(id => id !== input.id))));
         if (who.length) say('is an answer the course accepts, for ' + who.join(', '));
         if (end(x) !== end(input.right)) say('ends with ' + shown(end(x)) + ', and the answer with ' + shown(end(input.right)));
         const len = Array.from(x).length;
         if (len < lo || len > hi) say('is ' + len + (len === 1 ? ' character: ' : ' characters: ') + lo + ' to ' + hi + ', the length of the answer « ' + input.right + ' » give or take 40%');
         const r = U.ratio(x, input.nl);
         if (r < least) say('is further from the Dutch than the answer: ' + r.toFixed(2) + ', at least ' + least.toFixed(2));
       });
       return why;
     }

     function kind(part) {
       const be = part === 'be';
       return {
         stamp: STAMP,
         fields: ['note', 'also'],
         optional: be ? ['decoys'] : [],
         tables: be ? ['notes', 'also', 'decoys'] : ['notes', 'also'],
         split: split(part),
         check: (row, input, ctx) => checkNote(row, input, ctx).concat(checkAlso(row, input, ctx), be ? checkDecoys(row, input, ctx) : []),
         /* Le relecteur lit en entier la ligne qui ajoute un « on dit aussi » : une réponse de plus
            que la saisie accepte. */
         readWhole: (row, input) => Array.isArray(row.also) && row.also.some(f => input.also.indexOf(f) < 0) ? 'new also' : '',
         /* Une liste vide, ou une ligne sans leurres, ôte la clé. */
         merge: row => Object.assign({ notes: row.note, also: row.also.length ? row.also : null }, be ? { decoys: row.decoys || null } : {})
     ```

  11. Save this script **outside the worktree**, as `<WS>/tmp/move-also.js`. Do not add it to the repo:
      ```js
      /* One-off: rewrites src/content/also.js as a table keyed by the Dutch, in the format of
         tools/content/lib/table.js. Run once from outside the repository, after TABLES lists also
         and before also.js is a table:
           node move-also.js <repo>
         It refuses unless today's also.js attaches every entry, and unless the items built
         afterwards equal the items built before, key for key; then it puts also.js back as it was. */
      const fs = require('fs'), path = require('path');
      const root = path.resolve(process.argv[2]);
      const browser = require(path.join(root, 'test', 'lib', 'browser'));
      const table = require(path.join(root, 'tools', 'content', 'lib', 'table'));
      const { course } = require(path.join(root, 'tools', 'content', 'lib', 'course'));
      const ALSO = 'src/content/also.js';

      const canon = v => Array.isArray(v) ? v.map(canon)
        : v && typeof v === 'object' && !(v instanceof RegExp) ? Object.keys(v).sort().reduce((o, k) => { o[k] = canon(v[k]); return o; }, {})
        : v;
      async function items() {
        const B = browser.open({ root, seed: browser.SEED, files: browser.sources(root), skip: [browser.APP] });
        await B.NL.state.open();
        B.NL.content.refresh();
        return { json: JSON.stringify(canon(B.NL.content.allItems())), NL: B.NL };
      }

      (async () => {
        const file = path.join(root, ALSO), text = fs.readFileSync(file, 'utf8');
        if (text.indexOf('NL.content.byDutch') >= 0) throw new Error(ALSO + ' is already a table');
        const before = await items();
        const was = before.NL.content.alsoReport;
        if (!was || was.missing.length) throw new Error(ALSO + ' attaches no item for ' + JSON.stringify(was && was.missing));
        if (!before.NL.content.tableReport.hasOwnProperty('also')) throw new Error('TABLES in src/content/index.js does not list also: add its line first');
        const C = course(root), entries = {};
        C.sources.filter(s => s.also).forEach(s => { entries[s.nl] = s.also; });
        if (Object.keys(entries).length !== was.attached) throw new Error(was.attached + ' entries in ' + ALSO + ', ' + Object.keys(entries).length + ' items with also');
        const eol = /\r\n/.test(text) ? '\r\n' : '\n';
        const head = [
          '/* Les « on dit aussi » : d\'autres façons de dire la même chose. Une entrée par mot ou phrase,',
          '   sous son néerlandais tel que le lexique l\'écrit, jetons non remplis ; la valeur est une liste',
          '   de formes néerlandaises. La réponse tapée les accepte en plus de la cible et de sa forme',
          '   flamande (NL.ex.accepted), et le panneau les liste après coup (« On dit aussi : … »). Du',
          '   néerlandais seulement, jamais stocké : l\'élément du contenu les porte, pas l\'enregistrement',
          '   de la personne. build() (src/content/index.js) pose la liste sur l\'élément, au champ also.',
          '   « bonjour » et « salut », c\'est le même salut : hallo, goeiedag et dag s\'acceptent l\'un',
          '   l\'autre (hallo et goeiedag par leur sens commun). Merge des genres explanations-be et',
          '   explanations récrit ce fichier. */'
        ].join(eol) + eol;
        fs.writeFileSync(file, table.serialize({ head, eol, name: 'also', entries }));
        const after = await items();
        const report = after.NL.content.tableReport.also;
        const wrong = before.json !== after.json ? 'the items differ after the move'
          : !report || report.attached !== was.attached || report.missing.length ? ALSO + ': ' + JSON.stringify(report) : '';
        if (wrong) {
          fs.writeFileSync(file, text);
          throw new Error(wrong + '; ' + ALSO + ' is back as it was');
        }
        console.log('ok ' + report.attached + ' entries moved, ' + after.NL.content.allItems().length + ' items identical');
      })().catch(e => { console.log('FAIL ' + e.message); process.exitCode = 1; });
      ```
      Run it once, from the worktree:

      node "<WS>/tmp/move-also.js" .
      ```

### Task 29: Hand-written prose to the quote rule
Class: mechanical
Ticket: {T-langmarks}
Promises: none
Why: decision 10 is that quotes are the mark: a passage between « » or “ ” in the course's prose is Dutch, and
nothing else is. `NL.gloss.quoted` declares each quoted passage `nl-BE`. Task 17 made the rule hold on screen and
counted what still breaks it. After task 23a, the hand-written prose breaks it in two ways.
- **Quotes that are not Dutch.** There are 36 of them (`QUOTE_BUDGET = 36`). Each is a translation, read in the
  Dutch voice, and a translation goes in brackets or plain. 25 of the 36 are in the notes of words and phrases,
  which task 24 moved to `src/content/notes.js` (`byDutch.notes`) and M1 and M2 rewrite. The other 11 are here:
  - 7 in the grammar explanations;
  - 2 in sheet notes;
  - 1 in a loan's note;
  - 1 in a free task's `what` (« a form of “you” »).
- **Dutch that nothing marks.** This Dutch is written bare in prose that goes out in both languages. On an
  English page it is read in the English voice. It sits in:
  - the 10 bare `<b>` of the grammar cards (decision 10 names them: `het`, `ons/onze`, `ge-`, `-t`, `-d`, each
    twice);
  - six pattern rules (« ik werk / jij werkt … »), where the outline says three. The recon missed
    `g-getallen`, `g-halfuur` and `g-perfect-intro`;
  - plain words in the explanations (`jij`, `hij`, `kun je`, `het`, `werken` → `gewerkt` …);
  - three unit blurbs, four `what` of free tasks, five `het`/`de` rules, five loan notes and four sheet notes.

The outline's items (1) to (5) are all here. Item (2), scenario notes and the outro, needs no change: neither has
a quote outside the course's Dutch, and the new check below finds no bare Dutch in them.

A new check, 6d.4, makes the second fault visible. It reads every prose text of the course that has a French
side and an English side. It takes the words each side leaves outside `nl-BE`, and keeps those that are:
- in both sides;
- in the course's Dutch;
- not one of the names `{naam}`, `{stad}` and `{bedrijf}` stand for.

A word left over is Dutch written bare. French and English do not share Dutch words by chance. Nine words are
shared on purpose: office English, a brand, an article. They are listed in `SHARED_OK`, each with its reason, and
each must still be hit.

The notes of words and phrases stay out of 6d.4 until M1 and M2 rewrite them: it skips every path under
`byDutch.notes[`, where task 24 put them. After task 24 no prose field is left under `units[i].words` or
`.phrases`, so that is the only skip.

Then 6d.3 learns that an affix cited with its hyphen (« -tje », “ge-”) is Dutch by its form. Five new `QUOTE_OK`
entries cover the words that are now cited but are not in the course: `lijn`, `jam`, `vrachtwagen`, `vork`,
`bijgevoegd`. The budget falls to 25, the item notes alone.

One test follows the content. `test/typed.js` reads the needs a free answer ticks with `text()`, which puts a
space where each tag was. Once a `what` cites its Dutch (« om … »), the cited word carries its own `<span>`.
`text()` then reads `“ om … ”`, and the check that « Ik begin om half negen » ticks `“om …”` fails. The helper
reads the ticked need whole, through `joined()`.

          ne voit pas le néerlandais qu'un seul côté écrit, ni celui que le cours n'enseigne pas. */
       const q4 = () => {
         const B = boot();
         return B.NL.state.open().then(() => {
           const NL = B.NL, dutch = dutchWords(NL), names = new Set(), shared = new Set(), nu = [];
           const words = s => s.toLowerCase().split(/[^\p{L}\p{N}]+/u).filter(Boolean);
           Object.keys(NL.content.DEFAULTS).forEach(k => words(String(NL.content.DEFAULTS[k])).forEach(w => names.add(w)));
           const bare = (f, s, l) => new Set([].concat(...runs(f === 'explain' ? NL.gloss.prose(s) : NL.gloss.quoted(s), l)
             .filter(r => r.lang !== 'nl-BE').map(r => words(r.text))));
           let fields = 0;
           tree.visitCourse(NL.content, (v, key, where) => {
             if (!v || typeof v !== 'object' || typeof v.fr !== 'string' || typeof v.en !== 'string') return;
             if ((QUOTED_FIELDS.indexOf(key) < 0 && key !== 'explain') || /^byDutch\.notes\[/.test(where)) return;
             fields++;
             const en = bare(key, v.en, 'en');
             const both = Array.from(bare(key, v.fr, 'fr')).filter(w => en.has(w) && dutch.has(w) && !names.has(w));
             both.forEach(w => { if (SHARED_OK[w]) shared.add(w); });
             if (both.some(w => !SHARED_OK[w])) nu.push(where + ' [' + both.filter(w => !SHARED_OK[w]).join(', ') + ']');
           });
           nu.forEach(n => ok(false, '6d : ' + n + ' : du néerlandais du cours, écrit pareil en français et en anglais hors de nl-BE — le citer, ou dans explain lui donner class="nl"'));
           Object.keys(SHARED_OK).forEach(w => ok(shared.has(w), '6d : « ' + w + ' » n’est plus écrit pareil dans les deux langues, ou plus du néerlandais du cours : son exception est de trop'));
           ok(fields > 0, '6d : aucun texte lu en deux langues, le contrôle est creux');
           console.log('  néerlandais nu  ' + fields + ' champs lus en deux langues, ' + Object.keys(SHARED_OK).length + ' exceptions');
         });
       };

       return [q1, q2, q3, q4].reduce((p, c) => p.then(c), Promise.resolve());
     ```
     `runs`, `tree`, `dutchWords`, `QUOTED_FIELDS` and `boot` are already in the file.

### Task 29a: The rest of the Dutch in prose is marked
Class: mechanical
Ticket: {T-langmarks}
Promises: none
Why: the maintainer ruled on the Dutch that task 29 left unmarked: phase 3 marks it. Two places are left.
- **Titles.** `title` and `h` cannot quote (6d.3), so their Dutch carries `class="nl"`, with no quotes. It is
  written bare today in:
  - six grammar titles (« radical+t », « Ge et gij », « Half drie », « De ou het », « Mijn, uw, ons et onze »,
    « avec hebben »);
  - two sheet headings (« u ou je ? », « zijn et hebben »);
  - the de / het page, which is `dehetTitle` and its body and column heads in `fr.js` and `en.js`, plus the
    `de / het` of its tile and eyebrow.

  Each screen that shows a title escapes it today, so a `class="nl"` would show as text. Those screens show it
  through `NL.gloss.prose` instead, which declares it `nl-BE`.
- **The one-language tables.** `sounds`, `faux` and `fauxEn` in `reference.js` are written in one language each
  (`NL.content.anchors`). Their prose (`say`, `trap`) follows the quote rule like all other prose:
  - the Dutch goes in quotes (« het kantoor », “uiteindelijk”);
  - a French or English word that was quoted loses its quotes (« brillant », “eventually”);
  - a letter that was quoted becomes `<b>`, as the table already writes one (`<b>ou</b>`).

  `say` is HTML like `explain`, so its quoted Dutch carries `class="nl"` inside the quotes. `trap` is plain text,
  shown through `NL.gloss.quoted`. Today `library.js` escapes it.

The guard reads those tables. `REFERENCE_TABLES` lists them beside the loans, and `eachText` and the planted check
6d.2 read every table in it. The name keeps them apart from `C.TABLES`, task 24's tables keyed by the Dutch
(`byDutch.notes` among them). Three checks are new:
- **6d.5** plants a `<span class="nl">zqN</span>` in every `title` and `h`, and fails on a screen that shows one
  undeclared.
- **6d.6** reads the de / het page and its tile in both languages. It fails on a word of the course's Dutch
  that both languages show outside `nl-BE`.
- **6d.7** gives the learner's name, town and company as a tag (`<u>zqmine</u>`). It fails on any screen that
  shows that tag as HTML. The next paragraph says why.

`place` is in the ruling, and this task does not carry that part out as written. No `place` has any Dutch to
mark. The four places are `{stad}` or `{bedrijf}` and a time. `fill()` (`src/content/index.js:14`) puts the
learner's own town and company into them as typed, with nothing escaped. Shown through `NL.gloss.prose`, that
text would go into the page as HTML: markup in a setting, a synced meta or a backup would run. So `place` stays
escaped text, outside `HTML_FIELDS`. 6d.7 holds that line for every field shown as HTML. A `place` that one day
carries Dutch needs a ruling first.

       const q5 = () => planted(['title', 'h'], n => '<span class="nl">zq' + n + '</span>', /<span class="nl" lang="nl-BE">zq(\d+)<\/span>/g);

       /* 6d.6. La page de / het et sa tuile, écrites par les tables fr et en : un mot du néerlandais du
          cours que les deux langues y montrent hors de nl-BE (« het », « de / het ») porte class="nl". Les

             ok(tile !== '', '6d (' + l + ') : la tuile de / het manque, le contrôle est creux');
             NL.ui.go('dehet');
             return new Set([].concat(...runs(tile + B.app.innerHTML, l).filter(r => r.lang !== 'nl-BE').map(r => words(r.text))));
           };
           const fr = page('fr', French), en = page('en', English);
           const both = Array.from(fr).filter(w => en.has(w) && dutch.has(w) && !named.has(w) && !SHARED_OK[w]);
           ok(both.length === 0, '6d : la page de / het montre nu, en français comme en anglais, ' + both.join(', ') + ' — lui donner class="nl"');
         });
       };

          porte, reste échappé. Planté d'une balise (<u>zqmine</u>), il ne paraît comme balise sur aucun
          écran, et il paraît échappé dans les conversations. views() remet l'état à zéro, réglages

           });

           ok(escaped > 0, '6d : le texte de l’apprenant ne paraît dans aucune conversation, le contrôle est creux');
         });

Class: mechanical

Promises: none
Why: decision 6a, « Every item, with evidence ». Task 9's drafters, its readers and the maintainer have settled
every row of the kind `flemish`, and this task carries the rows into `src/`. Task 6's `merge.js` runs task 8's
kind. It writes each form into `src/content/be.js` under its source's raw Dutch. For each new form that OpenTaal
does not know, it adds a line to `test/data/flemish.tsv`, with the reason its evidence gives. A `be: null` row
writes nothing. The new forms reach the learner through the `vlaams` exercise and « Comment le dit-on ici ? »,
so `test/pace.js` and `test/journey.js` may move. This task reports their numbers and changes no threshold.
The flemish kind stamps fields that its own Merge writes, so a second run of a Merge that succeeded fails as
stale. That is expected, because each merge task runs once.

### Task 31: FAN explanations-be
Class: fan-out
Ticket: {T-explanations}
Kind: explanations-be
Drafting after: 1, 3, 4, 6, 17, 24, 25, 26, 27, 28, 30
Split: node tools/content/split.js . "<WS>/drafts/explanations-be"
Check: node tools/content/check.js "<WS>/drafts/explanations-be/<batch>"
Merged by: task 38
Why: decisions 8c and 8d. Every word and phrase gets an explanation (decision 8a), and the items whose Flemish
form is not their Dutch come first: the maintainer reads them at gate 39 before the other 361 − N are
drafted (decision 8c). A row writes the note in French and in English and the « on dit aussi » forms. For an
item that « Comment le dit-on ici ? » asks (`vlaams`), it also writes two decoys for that exercise: wrong
answers that a learner could give and that no Fleming says (decision 8d). Split cuts 60 + N rows, N being the
items that task 30 gave a Flemish form. In the proof, before task 30, that was `be-words` 37 and `be-phrases`
23, with 38 of the 60 `vlaams`. A batch above 40 rows is cut by whole units into `be-words-1`, `be-words-2`
and so on, so the number of batches is known only after task 30. 25 of the 60 have a note today, and 21 of
those already meet this format. Tasks 32 to 37 run beside the drafting: tests, the reading tool, `sourced.js`
and `open.phrases.js`. None of them changes a Flemish item's `be`, meaning, note or `also`, which the stamp
covers.

#### Format

```json
{"id": "bakker:p9", "stamp": "46507715", "note": {"fr": "« Da’s » contracte « dat is » : on l’entend partout en Flandre, et on écrit « dat is ».", "en": "“Da’s” runs “dat is” together: you hear it all over Flanders, and write “dat is”."}, "also": [], "decoys": ["Dat’s lekker.", "Da’s lekkere."]}
```

- One row per input row, in its order. Copy `id` and `stamp` unchanged, then give `note`, `also` and, on a row
  whose `vlaams` is true, `decoys`. No other field except `unsure`.
- `note` says what `meaning` does not: where the Flemish form comes from, when and to whom it is said, what
  is said in the Netherlands instead, a trap for a French speaker. Check refuses a note that only repeats the
  meaning.
- `note` is `{"fr": …, "en": …}`, the same note in French and in English. Each side is one line of at most 160
  characters and 2 sentences, with no `<` and no straight double quote. Write the typographic apostrophe, `’`.
- Quotes hold Dutch only (decision 8b): « … » in `fr`, “…” in `en`, no quote inside a quote, and both sides
  quote the same Dutch. A translation goes in parentheses, unquoted:
  `« Ik heb er geen goesting in » (je n’ai pas envie)`.
- Every quoted word is Dutch that OpenTaal or `flemish.tsv` knows, or a word of the row's own forms (`nl`, `be`,
  `also`). A French or an English word is never quoted:
  `Vient tout droit du français embêtant.`
- A word of the course that both sides leave bare is refused: quote it, « het », not het.
- Each side is written in its own language. Outside quotes, Check refuses French function words in `en` (le,
  la, et, est, avec…) and English ones in `fr` (the, and, of, is, with…).
- Both sides hold the same digits and the same `{naam}`, `{stad}` and `{bedrijf}` tokens. Write a default name
  as its token, never the name itself.
- `note` in the input is today's note, or `null`. Keep it word for word when it meets this format and says
  something true and worth saying; otherwise rewrite it, keeping what it says that is right (decision 8a).
- `also` lists the other Dutch forms that the typed exercise should accept for this item, in this sense, `[]`
  for none. One form per entry (no `/`, no `;`, and for a word no comma), a noun with its article, each word spelled
  as OpenTaal or `flemish.tsv` knows it. Check refuses `nl` itself, a form that `be` gives, the same form twice,
  and the Dutch of another item unless that item is a sibling or the input's `also` already holds it. Keep the
  input's forms unless one is wrong. A form you add becomes a right answer, so the reader reads the row whole.
- `decoys`, on a `vlaams` row only: two wrong answers to « Comment le dit-on ici ? », whose right answer is
  `right`. Each one is a slip a learner could make and that no Fleming says (decision 8d): the Dutch spelling
  half kept, a wrong ending, a contraction in the wrong place. Check refuses:
  - two decoys that are one answer;
  - a decoy that the course accepts for any item, the row's `also` included. Punctuation does not count: for
    `bakker:p9` above, whose `right` is « Da’s lekker. », the decoy « Da’s lekker! » is the right answer;
  - a decoy that does not end with `right`'s final punctuation;
  - a decoy outside 60 % to 140 % of `right`'s length;
  - a decoy further from `nl` than `right` is, by more than 0.15 of `U.ratio`.
- `siblings` lists the items with the same sense. Your note and your `also` agree with theirs.
- `labelled` lists the senses that English Wiktionary labels Belgian for `nl` itself, or is `null`. It is a
  lead for the note, not a text to copy: its senses are English, and a quote holds Dutch only.
- A row you doubt carries `"unsure": "<why, in one line>"`. Check still checks it, and the reader reads it first.
- A verdict carries `id` and `verdict`, and no other field.

#### Reader focus

- Is the note true of Flanders today, at work? Dispute a form of one dialect (West Flemish, Limburg) passed off
  as Flemish, Dutch of the Netherlands passed off as Flemish, and a claim about a word's origin that nobody can
  check.
- Does the note teach what `meaning` does not? A note that says the meaning again in other words passes Check:
  dispute it.
- Are `fr` and `en` the same note, each natural in its own language? Dispute a side that reads as a
  word-for-word translation.
- The decoys. Would a learner plausibly give it? Dispute a decoy that some Fleming does say: it marks a right
  answer wrong. Dispute one that no learner would ever type: it teaches nothing.
- `also`. Is each form right for this item, in this sense, at work? It becomes an answer that the typed
  exercise accepts, and the row goes on to the content check (`readWhole` gives `new also`).
- An old note kept word for word: is it still true, and still worth saying?
- Siblings agree: the same sense gets the same note and the same `also`.
- A note that contradicts `labelled`: who is right?
- `unsure` rows first.

### Task 33: The reading tool
Class: mechanical
Ticket: {T-tools}
Promises: none
Why: decisions 5c and 8c, and the content check, which is the outline's call. The maintainer reads three
things, and each is one mode of `tools/content/reading.js`:
- **The content check's list** (the default). It is written to `<WS>/reading-list.md` by task 43. It holds:
  - every new Flemish form (6a: « maintainer reads every new be »);
  - every generated sentence (5c: « all on maintainer's reading list »);
  - every row the maintainer ruled;
  - a seeded sample of the other taken rows: 1 in 10, and at least 10 per kind.
- **Every row of one kind**, `--kind <kind>`. Gate 39 shows it for `explanations-be` (8c: « maintainer reads
  them »).
- **The words without a sentence at HEAD**, `--unsentenced`. Gate 35 shows them with the drafters' skip reasons,
  and the maintainer names which get a generated sentence (5c).

Under each row, the tool prints what each table of the row's kind holds for its Dutch at HEAD. The maintainer
reads what the course now says, not what a draft said. The tool writes nothing.

After this task:
- **What the kit gives the tool.** `kit.readKind(repo, kindDir)` reads a kind batch by batch, as Merge does.
  It returns `{ name, kind, lines, rows }`:
  - `lines` are each batch's Check lines, plus `fail <kind> -: batch <b> does not pass Check` for a batch that
    fails;
  - each row is `{ input, batch, ruling }` plus what `settle()` makes of it: `{ row, from }`, `{ drop: true }`
    or `{ why }`. `ruling` is the maintainer's `rulings.json` entry, or `null`.

  `kit.merge` now starts from `readKind`. Its output is unchanged, and the Merge section of `fanout.js` checks
  that.
- **A kind module may say what is read whole.** It does so with `readWhole(row, input, src)`, which returns a
  reason or `''`. The default is `() => ''`, and `loadKind` refuses a `readWhole` that is not a function:
  - `flemish` returns `'new be'` for a row that writes a `be`;
  - `examples-gen` returns `'generated sentence'` for every row.

  A kind written before this task may already export it: `loadKind` keeps exports it does not know.
- **The library.** `tools/content/lib/reading.js` exports:
  - `list(repo, ws)`, `every(repo, ws, name)` and `unsentenced(repo, ws, opts)`, each returning `{ ok, lines }`;
  - `size(n)` and `pick(name, ids)`, for the sample;
  - `SENTENCES`, which is `'examples'`, the kind `--unsentenced` reads.

  The sample takes the rows whose sha1 of `<kind> <id>` is smallest, so every run gives the same list. A row
  added later does not move the others.

           const a = lines.indexOf('## ' + name);
           let b = a + 1;
           while (b < lines.length && !/^## /.test(lines[b])) b++;
           return lines.slice(a, b);
         };

         /* L'espace de travail : le genre d'essai tel que la section 6 l'a fondu, le genre vide, et
            deux genres écrits ici. « lecture » prend les 25 premiers mots en deux lots, tous gardés,
            et un mot de plus d'un mot s'y lit en entier ; « exemples » donne des phrases, ou une
            raison de n'en pas donner (« skip »), et « skip: ask » va au mainteneur. */
         fs.cpSync(KIND, path.join(WS, 'drafts', 'essai'), { recursive: true });
         same(run('split.js', [TMP, path.join(WS, 'drafts', 'vide')]), { code: 0, lines: [] }, 'le genre vide se coupe dans l\'espace de lecture');
         kindFile('lecture', `module.exports = {
       stamp: ['meaning'],
       fields: ['mot'],
       tables: ['lecture'],
       split: C => {
         const ids = C.sources.filter(s => s.kind === 'word').slice(0, 25).map(s => s.id);
         const rows = list => list.map(id => ({ id, nl: C.byId(id).nl }));
         return [{ batch: 'a', rows: rows(ids.slice(0, 12)) }, { batch: 'b', rows: rows(ids.slice(12)) }];
       },
       check: (row, input) => row.mot === input.nl.toUpperCase() ? [] : ['mot is not ' + input.nl.toUpperCase()],
       readWhole: row => row.mot.indexOf(' ') >= 0 ? 'two words' : '',
       merge: row => ({ lecture: row.mot })
     };
     `);
         const LDIR = path.join(WS, 'drafts', 'lecture');
         same(run('split.js', [TMP, LDIR]), { code: 0, lines: ['a 12', 'b 13'] }, 'le genre « lecture » se coupe');
         ['a', 'b'].forEach(b => {
           const input = JSON.parse(text(path.join(LDIR, b, 'input.json')));
           put(path.join(LDIR, b), 'draft.json', input.map(r => Object.assign({ id: r.id, stamp: r.stamp, mot: r.nl.toUpperCase() },
             r.nl === 'tot ziens' ? { unsure: 'tot ziens, or tot straks?' } : {})));
           put(path.join(LDIR, b), 'review.json', input.map(r => ({ id: r.id, verdict: 'keep' })));
         });
         const LT = path.join(TMP, 'src', 'content', 'lecture.js');
         fs.writeFileSync(LT, '/* La table de lecture de test/tools/fanout.js. */\n' + table.MARKER + '\nNL.content.byDutch[\'lecture\'] = {\n};\n');
         same(run('merge.js', [TMP, LDIR]), { code: 0, lines: ['ok lecture 25 taken, 0 dropped', 'ok lecture.js 25 set, 0 removed'] }, 'le genre « lecture » se fond');
         /* Les mots sans phrase à HEAD, et un mot qui a la sienne, lus dans le cours et pas écrits ici :

         const sentenced = C.sources.find(s => s.kind === 'word' && s.drills && s.drills.length).id;
         kindFile('exemples', `module.exports = {

         const xs = JSON.parse(text(path.join(XEEN, 'input.json')));
         put(XEEN, 'draft.json', [

         put(XEEN, 'disputes.md', '## ' + bare[2] + '\nSource: ' + C.byId(bare[2]).nl + '\nRow: skip ask\nFirst reader: for maintainer: skip is ask\n');
         put(XEEN, 'rulings.json', [{ id: bare[2], ruling: 'drop', words: 'leave it', confirmed: true, date: '2026-10-22' }]);

         const sha1 = s => crypto.createHash('sha1').update(s).digest('hex');

         same(part(L.lines, 'exemples').slice(0, 3), ['## exemples', '', '3 rows: 2 taken, 1 dropped. Listed: 1 ruled, 0 read whole, 2 sampled of 2 others.'], 'une ligne écartée par le mainteneur est listée');

         same(lecture.slice(0, 3), ['## lecture', '', '25 rows: 25 taken, 0 dropped. Listed: 0 ruled, 4 read whole, 10 sampled of 21 others.'], 'un genre de 21 autres lignes en lit 10');
         same(lecture.filter(l => /^- /.test(l)), words.filter(id => whole.indexOf(id) >= 0 || sample.indexOf(id) >= 0).map(head),
           'les lignes à lire en entier et l\'échantillon, dans l\'ordre de l\'entrée');
         const w3 = lecture.indexOf(head('overleven:w3'));

         same(part(L.lines, 'vide'), ['## vide', '', '0 rows: 0 taken, 0 dropped. Listed: 0 ruled, 0 read whole, 0 sampled of 0 others.'], 'un genre sans ligne n\'a que ses comptes');
         same(reading.list(TMP, WS), L, 'la liste est la même à chaque lecture');
         same(run('reading.js', [TMP, WS]), { code: 0, lines: L.lines.filter(Boolean) }, 'reading.js imprime la liste');

         /* --kind : chaque ligne d'un genre. */
         const EVERY = ['# essai: every row', '', '5 rows: 4 taken, 1 dropped.', ''].concat(ESSAI.map(l => l.replace('; sampled', '')));
         same(reading.every(TMP, WS, 'essai'), { ok: true, lines: EVERY }, '--kind liste chaque ligne du genre, sans échantillon');
         same(run('reading.js', [TMP, WS, '--kind', 'essai']), { code: 0, lines: EVERY.filter(Boolean) }, 'reading.js --kind imprime chaque ligne');
         same(run('reading.js', [TMP, WS, '--kind', 'inconnu']), { code: 1, lines: ['fail inconnu -: never split: run Split first'] }, '--kind refuse un genre jamais coupé');

         /* --unsentenced : les mots sans phrase à HEAD, et la ligne de chacun dans le genre des exemples. */
         const U = reading.unsentenced(TMP, WS, { sentences: 'exemples' });
         ok(U.ok, '--unsentenced se lit : ' + U.lines.filter(l => /^fail /.test(l)).join(' | '));
         same(U.lines.slice(0, 10), ['# Words without a sentence', '', bare.length + ' words have no example sentence. Under each, its row in drafts/exemples.', '',
           head(bare[0]), '  - exemples: {"phrases":[],"skip":"no candidate fits"}; kept by the first reader',
           head(bare[1]), '  - exemples: no row',
           head(bare[2]), '  - exemples: ruled drop on 2026-10-22: leave it'
         ], 'chaque mot sans phrase : sa ligne gardée et sa raison, pas de ligne, ou la décision qui l\'écarte');
         same(U.lines.filter(l => /^- /.test(l)), bare.map(head), 'les mots sans phrase, dans l\'ordre du cours, et eux seuls (' + C.byId(sentenced).nl + ' a la sienne)');
         same(run('reading.js', [TMP, WS, '--unsentenced']), { code: 1, lines: ['fail examples -: never split: run Split first'] }, 'reading.js --unsentenced lit le genre examples');

         /* Les refus. */
         same(reading.list(TMP, path.join(TMP, 'nulle')), { ok: false, lines: ['fail reading -: no split kind in ' + path.join(TMP, 'nulle', 'drafts')] }, 'un espace sans genre coupé est refusé');
         const LA = path.join(LDIR, 'a'), lrev = text(path.join(LA, 'review.json'));
         put(LA, 'review.json', lrev.replace('"keep"', '"kept"'));
         const bad = reading.every(TMP, WS, 'lecture');
         ok(!bad.ok && bad.lines[bad.lines.length - 1] === 'fail lecture -: batch a does not pass Check', 'un lot qui ne passe pas Check est refusé : ' + JSON.stringify(bad.lines.slice(-1)));
         put(LA, 'review.json', lrev);
         fs.renameSync(path.join(LDIR, 'b', 'review.json'), path.join(LDIR, 'b', 'review.json.old'));
         const open = reading.list(TMP, WS);
         same([open.ok, open.lines.length, open.lines[0]], [false, 13, 'fail lecture ' + words[12] + ': unsettled, no review'], 'une ligne non réglée est refusée, et la liste avec');
         fs.renameSync(path.join(LDIR, 'b', 'review.json.old'), path.join(LDIR, 'b', 'review.json'));
         fs.renameSync(LT, LT + '.old');
         same(reading.every(TMP, WS, 'lecture'), { ok: false, lines: ['fail lecture -: no table file src/content/lecture.js'] }, 'une table sans fichier est refusée');
         fs.renameSync(LT + '.old', LT);
         edit('W(\'goeiedag\'', 'W(\'hallo\'');
         same(reading.every(TMP, WS, 'essai'), { ok: false, lines: ['fail essai overleven:w1: no longer an item'] }, 'une ligne dont l\'élément n\'est plus est refusée');
         fs.writeFileSync(LEX, lexicon);
         const USAGE = ['usage: node tools/content/reading.js <repo> <WS> [--kind <kind> | --unsentenced]'];
         [[TMP], [TMP, WS, '--kind'], [TMP, WS, '--unsentenced', 'essai'], [TMP, WS, '--tout']].forEach(a =>

         console.log('  lecture        liste, --kind, --unsentenced, échantillon ' + sample.length + ' sur ' + others.length + ', refus');
       }

     /* Un genre lu lot par lot, sans rien écrire : { name, kind, lines, rows }. lines sont les
        lignes de Check de chaque lot, puis, pour un lot qui ne passe pas, « batch <lot> does not
        pass Check » ; rows ne tient alors rien de ce lot. Une ligne de rows : { input, batch,
        ruling } (la décision du mainteneur, ou null) et ce que settle() en prend. kind est null
        quand aucun lot n'a été lu. */
     function readKind(repo, kindDir) {
       const name = path.basename(kindDir), list = path.join(kindDir, 'split.txt');
       if (!fs.existsSync(list)) return { name, kind: null, lines: ['fail ' + name + ' -: never split: run Split first'], rows: [] };
       const batches = fs.readFileSync(list, 'utf8').split('\n').filter(Boolean).map(l => l.split(' ')[0]);
       const lines = [], rows = [];
       let kind = null;
       batches.forEach(b => {
         const r = readBatch(repo, path.join(kindDir, b));
         kind = r.kind || kind;
         r.lines.forEach(l => lines.push(l));
         if (failed(r.lines)) { lines.push('fail ' + name + ' -: batch ' + b + ' does not pass Check'); return; }
         const ruling = id => (r.got['rulings.json'] || []).find(x => x.id === id) || null;
         r.input.forEach(input => rows.push(Object.assign({ input, batch: b, ruling: ruling(input.id) }, settle(input.id, r.got))));
       });
       return { name, kind, lines, rows };
     }

     function merge(repo, kindDir) {

  2. Create `tools/content/lib/reading.js`:
     ```js
     /* L'outil de lecture : ce que le mainteneur lit des lignes d'un espace de travail, avec ce que
        les tables du cours en tiennent à HEAD. N'écrit rien.

          const reading = require('./reading');
          reading.list(repo, ws)                 { ok, lines } — la liste du contrôle du contenu : par
                                                 genre coupé, chaque ligne que son genre fait lire en
                                                 entier (readWhole), chaque ligne que le mainteneur a
                                                 réglée, et un échantillon des autres lignes prises
          reading.every(repo, ws, name)          { ok, lines } — chaque ligne d'un genre
          reading.unsentenced(repo, ws, opts)    { ok, lines } — les mots sans phrase d'exemple à HEAD,
                                                 chacun avec sa ligne dans le genre opts.sentences
                                                 (par défaut SENTENCES, « examples »)
          reading.size(n)                        la taille de l'échantillon de n lignes
          reading.pick(name, ids)                l'échantillon : les mêmes ids à chaque lecture

        Les genres sont les dossiers de <ws>/drafts qui ont un split.txt. Les lignes sont du
        Markdown, en anglais : le mainteneur les lit sur la page de sa porte. Un genre illisible
        (un lot qui ne passe pas Check, une ligne non réglée, un élément qui n'est plus, une table
        sans fichier) rend des lignes « fail » et rien d'autre. */
     const fs = require('fs'), path = require('path'), crypto = require('crypto');
     const kit = require('./kit');
     const table = require('./table');
     const { course } = require('./course');

     const SENTENCES = 'examples';
     const INTRO = 'Read for the content check, at HEAD: every row its kind marks to read whole (a new Flemish form, a generated sentence), every row the maintainer ruled, and a sample of the other taken rows, 1 in 10 and at least 10 per kind, the same on every run. Under each row, what each of its kind\'s tables holds for it.';

     /* L'échantillon : 1 ligne sur 10, au moins 10, au plus toutes. Ses lignes sont celles dont
        le sha1 de « <genre> <id> » est le plus petit : la même liste à chaque lecture, et une
        ligne ajoutée ne déplace pas les autres. */
     const size = n => Math.min(n, Math.max(10, Math.ceil(n / 10)));
     const rank = (name, id) => crypto.createHash('sha1').update(name + ' ' + id).digest('hex');
     function pick(name, ids) {
       const chosen = new Set(ids.slice().sort((a, b) => rank(name, a) < rank(name, b) ? -1 : 1).slice(0, size(ids.length)));
       return ids.filter(id => chosen.has(id));
     }

     const failed = lines => lines.some(l => /^fail /.test(l));
     const has = (o, k) => Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(o, k);

     /* Un genre lu pour le mainteneur : ses lignes réglées, chacune avec sa source, et les
        entrées de ses tables à HEAD. */
     function read(repo, ws, name, C) {
       const r = kit.readKind(repo, path.join(path.resolve(ws), 'drafts', name));
       if (failed(r.lines)) return { lines: r.lines.filter(l => /^fail /.test(l)) };
       const lines = [], tables = r.kind ? r.kind.tables : [], entries = {};
       r.rows.forEach(x => {
         if (x.why) lines.push('fail ' + name + ' ' + x.input.id + ': unsettled, ' + x.why);
         else if (!C.byId(x.input.id)) lines.push('fail ' + name + ' ' + x.input.id + ': no longer an item');
         else x.src = C.byId(x.input.id);
       });
       tables.forEach(t => {
         const file = path.join(path.resolve(repo), 'src', 'content', t + '.js');
         if (fs.existsSync(file)) entries[t] = table.load(file).entries;
         else lines.push('fail ' + name + ' -: no table file src/content/' + t + '.js');
       });
       if (failed(lines)) return { lines };
       r.rows.forEach(x => { x.whole = x.row ? r.kind.readWhole(x.row, x.input, x.src) : ''; });
       return { lines, rows: r.rows, tables, entries };
     }

     /* Comment une ligne a été réglée. */
     const settled = x => x.ruling
       ? 'ruled ' + x.ruling.ruling + ' on ' + x.ruling.date + (x.ruling.words ? ': ' + x.ruling.words : '')
       : x.from === 'draft' ? 'kept by the first reader' : 'kept by the second reader';

     /* La ligne d'une source : son néerlandais, son id et son sens, langue par langue. */
     const heading = (src, G) => '- `' + src.nl + '` (' + src.id + ') — ' + G.LANGS.map(l => G.of(src, l)).join(' · ');

     /* Une ligne lue : sa source, pourquoi elle est là, puis ce que chaque table du genre tient
        sous son néerlandais, et le doute du rédacteur s'il en a dit un. */
     function block(x, k, G, also) {
       const why = (x.whole ? [x.whole] : []).concat([settled(x)], also || []);
       const out = [heading(x.src, G), '  - ' + why.join('; ')];
       k.tables.forEach(t => out.push('  - ' + t + '.js: ' + (has(k.entries[t], x.src.nl) ? table.literal(k.entries[t][x.src.nl]) : 'no entry')));
       if (x.row && x.row.unsure) out.push('  - unsure: ' + x.row.unsure);
       return out;
     }

     const counts = rows => rows.length + ' rows: ' + rows.filter(x => x.row).length + ' taken, ' + rows.filter(x => x.drop).length + ' dropped.';

     /* Les genres coupés de l'espace de travail, par ordre de nom. */
     function kinds(ws) {
       const dir = path.join(path.resolve(ws), 'drafts');
       return fs.existsSync(dir) ? fs.readdirSync(dir).filter(n => fs.existsSync(path.join(dir, n, 'split.txt'))).sort() : [];
     }

     function list(repo, ws) {
       const names = kinds(ws);
       if (!names.length) return { ok: false, lines: ['fail reading -: no split kind in ' + path.join(path.resolve(ws), 'drafts')] };
       const C = course(repo), G = C.NL.gloss;
       const lines = ['# Reading list', '', INTRO], fails = [];
       names.forEach(name => {
         const k = read(repo, ws, name, C);
         if (failed(k.lines)) { k.lines.forEach(l => fails.push(l)); return; }
         const ruled = k.rows.filter(x => x.ruling);
         const whole = k.rows.filter(x => !x.ruling && x.whole);
         const others = k.rows.filter(x => x.row && !x.ruling && !x.whole);
         const sampled = new Set(pick(name, others.map(x => x.input.id)));
         lines.push('', '## ' + name, '', counts(k.rows) + ' Listed: ' + ruled.length + ' ruled, ' + whole.length + ' read whole, ' + sampled.size + ' sampled of ' + others.length + ' others.');
         const listed = k.rows.filter(x => x.ruling || x.whole || sampled.has(x.input.id));
         if (listed.length) lines.push('');
         listed.forEach(x => block(x, k, G, sampled.has(x.input.id) ? ['sampled'] : []).forEach(l => lines.push(l)));
       });
       return fails.length ? { ok: false, lines: fails } : { ok: true, lines };
     }

     function every(repo, ws, name) {
       const C = course(repo), G = C.NL.gloss;
       const k = read(repo, ws, name, C);
       if (failed(k.lines)) return { ok: false, lines: k.lines };
       const lines = ['# ' + name + ': every row', '', counts(k.rows)];
       if (k.rows.length) lines.push('');
       k.rows.forEach(x => block(x, k, G).forEach(l => lines.push(l)));
       return { ok: true, lines };
     }

     function unsentenced(repo, ws, opts) {
       const name = (opts && opts.sentences) || SENTENCES;
       const C = course(repo), G = C.NL.gloss;
       const k = read(repo, ws, name, C);
       if (failed(k.lines)) return { ok: false, lines: k.lines };
       const byId = new Map(k.rows.map(x => [x.input.id, x]));
       const words = C.sources.filter(s => s.kind === 'word' && !(s.drills && s.drills.length));
       const lines = ['# Words without a sentence', '', words.length + ' words have no example sentence. Under each, its row in drafts/' + name + '.'];
       if (words.length) lines.push('');
       words.forEach(s => {
         const x = byId.get(s.id);
         lines.push(heading(s, G));
         if (!x) { lines.push('  - ' + name + ': no row'); return; }
         if (x.drop) { lines.push('  - ' + name + ': ' + settled(x)); return; }
         const rest = Object.assign({}, x.row);
         delete rest.id;
         delete rest.stamp;
         lines.push('  - ' + name + ': ' + JSON.stringify(rest) + '; ' + settled(x));
       });
       return { ok: true, lines };
     }

     module.exports = { SENTENCES, size, pick, list, every, unsentenced };
     ```
  3. Create `tools/content/reading.js`:
     ```js
     /* L'outil de lecture : ce que le mainteneur lit, en Markdown, avec ce que les tables du cours
        tiennent à HEAD.
          node tools/content/reading.js <dépôt> <espace de travail>                  la liste du contrôle du contenu
          node tools/content/reading.js <dépôt> <espace de travail> --kind <genre>   chaque ligne d'un genre
          node tools/content/reading.js <dépôt> <espace de travail> --unsentenced    les mots sans phrase d'exemple
        N'écrit rien. Sort avec 1, et ses lignes « fail », quand un genre n'est pas lisible. */
     const reading = require('./lib/reading');

     const USAGE = 'usage: node tools/content/reading.js <repo> <WS> [--kind <kind> | --unsentenced]';
     const [repo, ws, mode, name, more] = process.argv.slice(2);
     const known = mode === undefined || mode === '--kind' || mode === '--unsentenced';
     if (!repo || !ws || !known || (mode === '--kind') !== (name !== undefined) || more !== undefined) { console.log(USAGE); process.exit(1); }
     try {
       const r = mode === '--kind' ? reading.every(repo, ws, name) : mode === '--unsentenced' ? reading.unsentenced(repo, ws) : reading.list(repo, ws);
       r.lines.forEach(l => console.log(l));
       process.exit(r.ok ? 0 : 1);
     } catch (e) { console.log('fail reading -: ' + e.message); process.exit(1); }
     ```

### Task 35: GATE (b): the words that get a generated sentence
Class: gate
Ticket: {T-sentences}
After: 33, 34
Show: node tools/content/reading.js . "<WS>" --unsentenced
Ask: « Which of these words get a generated sentence? (none is an answer) »
Answer to: <WS>/drafts/examples-gen/named.txt
Why: decision 5c. After task 34 some words still have no example sentence: Tatoeba has none that keeps the
rules for them, or the drafters skipped every candidate, each skip with its reason. The first rule is #12's
story 39: a sentence uses nothing the course has not taught by its word's unit, not even an inflection of a
word it has taught (task 10). A word without a sentence gets no cloze, no tiles to put in order and no
dictation. A sentence written for the course fills that gap, but it is not a sentence a person wrote, so the
maintainer chooses which words get one, reads each one whole (task 33's list), and a second reader translates
it on their own (task 36). Show lists the words at HEAD, each with its unit and meaning, and under it what
task 14 did with it: `no row` when Split had no candidate to offer, or the drafter's `skip` with the reader's
verdict and the maintainer's ruling. In the proof (task 34's), it listed 31 words, each `no row`: Split had
no candidate for any of them. Among them are « goeiedag », « dag », « tot ziens », « u », « vijftig »,
« zeventig », « een half wit », « de choco », « afwerken » and « amai ».
Then:
- **Words named.** `named.txt` holds one per line, each written as Show writes it between backticks, with its
  article (« de choco »). A line that is empty or starts with `#` does not count. Task 36's Split cuts them
  into batches of whole units, about 40 rows each (`examples`' `MAX`); the proof's 31 words make one batch.
  If Split refuses the file (`named.txt: « <w> » is not a word of the course`, `« <w> » already has
  sentences`, `« <w> » twice`), the run controller asks the maintainer again with that line, writes the
  corrected list, and the gate stays `in progress` until Split accepts it.
- **« none ».** `named.txt` is created empty. Task 36's Split cuts 0 rows and prints nothing, so the fan-out
  has nothing to draft and is `done`. Task 41's Merge prints `ok examples-gen 0 taken, 0 dropped` and writes
  nothing.
- **Either way**, every word left unnamed keeps no sentence. That is decided here and is not raised again in
  this plan.

### Task 36: FAN examples-gen
Class: fan-out
Ticket: {T-sentences}
Kind: examples-gen
Drafting after: 13, 34, 35
Split: node tools/content/split.js . "<WS>/drafts/examples-gen"
Check: node tools/content/check.js "<WS>/drafts/examples-gen/<batch>"
Merged by: task 41
Why: decision 5c, « You name them ». At gate 35 the maintainer named, in `<WS>/drafts/examples-gen/named.txt`,
the words left without a sentence that get one written for the course. Split reads that file. It cuts the
named words into batches of whole units of about 40 rows (`examples`' `MAX`), each named after its first and
last unit: one batch, since task 34's proof left 31 words without a sentence (`overleven-bakker` in the
proof, for « goeiedag », « zeventig » and « de choco »). The drafter writes one
sentence per word. The reader writes their own English and French of it before reading the row's: that is the
second, independent translation the decision asks for. Task 41 merges each sentence into
`src/content/sourced.js` with `src: 'gen'`, and the maintainer reads every one whole at the content check
(task 33's `readWhole`). If `named.txt` names no word, Split cuts 0 rows and prints nothing: there is nothing
to draft, and this task is `done`. The stamp is task 12's: the meaning, the article and the number of
hand-written sentences. Tasks 37 to 40 run beside the drafting, and none of them changes a word's meaning,
article or sentences.

#### Format

```json
{"id": "tijd:w17", "stamp": "a6668273", "sentence": {"nl": "Hij is al zeventig jaar.", "gap": "zeventig", "en": "He is already seventy.", "fr": "Il a déjà septante ans."}}
```

and the reader's verdict on it:

```json
{"id": "tijd:w17", "verdict": "keep", "en": "He is seventy already.", "fr": "Il a déjà septante ans."}
```

- One row per input row, in its order. Copy `id` and `stamp` unchanged, then give `sentence`, and no other
  field.
- `sentence` is `{ "nl", "gap", "en", "fr" }`, each one line.
- `nl` is one sentence of plain spoken Dutch that a Flemish colleague would say as written: the word used in
  the sense `meaning` gives, in a scene of daily life or work. It has 4 to 8 tiles, its words as
  `NL.util.tiles` cuts them, punctuation left out.
- The course says you with `ge` or `gij` (« Hebt ge… », « Kunt ge… », « Bent ge… »), or `u`. Never `je`,
  `jij`, `jou` or `jouw`: Check refuses them. Nor « Zijt gij… »: no unit lists « zijt » among its words
  or phrases, so Check refuses it as a form the course never teaches.
- `gap` is the one tile the cloze hides: the word as `nl` writes it, with its capital at the start of the
  sentence (« Goeiedag »). For a word with an article, it is the noun without it (« choco »). For a word of
  several tiles, it is one of them.
- Write `nl` only from words the course teaches up to the word's unit (#12, story 39). Check refuses a form
  that a later unit teaches (`borrows from a later unit: <forms>`) and a form the course never teaches
  (`uses forms the course never teaches: <forms>`), even an inflection of a word it teaches: it refuses
  « oude » where the course teaches « oud ». Every form is one OpenTaal knows, or one `test/data/flemish.tsv`
  lists. When Check refuses a form, write the sentence again with another word; do not change the word's own
  form.
- `en` and `fr` say what `nl` says, in its register: `u` is « vous »; `ge` and `gij` are « tu » or « vous »,
  as the scene asks, as the course's own sentences do. A number is written the same way on both sides, in
  words or in digits: Check requires the same digits in `en` and `fr`.
- No name and no `{naam}`, `{stad}` or `{bedrijf}` token, in any of the three.
- A verdict is `keep` or `dispute: <reason>`. This format sends no row to the maintainer by rule, so a first
  reader never gives `for maintainer`.
- Every verdict, a `keep` or a `dispute`, carries `"en"` and `"fr"`: the reader's own translations of `nl`,
  each one line. Check refuses a verdict without them: `a verdict carries the reader's own en and fr of nl,
  each on one line`.

#### Reader focus

- **Translate `nl` before you read `en` and `fr`.** Read only `nl` and `meaning`, write your `en` and `fr`,
  and put them in the verdict. Then read the row's. If yours and the row's say different things, dispute,
  and say which reading is right. Wording that differs, as « He is already seventy. » and « He is seventy
  already. » do, is not a reason.
- **Is it Flanders?** Would a colleague in Brabant say it as written? Standard Dutch that Flanders also uses is
  right. Dispute what only the Netherlands says (« hartstikke », « doei », « pinnen », « een kopje koffie »),
  and a dialect word or spelling that the course does not teach.
- **The sense.** The sentence uses the word as `meaning` says, not a homograph or another sense.
- **The gap.** With `gap` hidden, can a learner who knows the meaning complete the sentence? The word is the
  only one that fits there, not one of many.
- **The register.** `u` with « vous », and `ge` or `gij` with the « tu » or « vous » the scene asks for. A shop,
  the doctor's or a stranger takes `u`.
- **The content.** It suits an adult learning at work: no violence, no politics, no religion, nothing a
  colleague would find odd out of context.
- **It reads like a person wrote it.** A sentence built only to hold the word (« De choco is de choco. »)
  teaches nothing: dispute it.

### Task 39: GATE (a): the maintainer reads the Flemish items' explanations
Class: gate
Ticket: {T-explanations}
After: 33, 38
Show: node tools/content/reading.js . "<WS>" --kind explanations-be
Ask: « The Flemish items' explanations: go for the rest? »
Answer to: Rulings
Why: decision 8c. The items whose Flemish form is not their Dutch are where the course says what no Dutch
source says, and where a bad decoy marks a right answer wrong. Task 38 merged their explanations first, so
that the maintainer reads them before the other 361 − N items are drafted to the same rules in 12 batches: a
fault in the format is fixed once, here, and not repeated 361 − N times. Show lists every row of
`explanations-be` as HEAD holds it, which is what a learner will see: each item's Dutch, id and meaning, how
its row was settled (`kept by the first reader`, or the maintainer's ruling), its entries in `notes.js`,
`also.js` and `decoys.js` (`no entry` where it has none), and its `unsure` line if the drafter left one. In the
proof, on task 38's stand-in rows, it printed 304 lines, starting, under its heading `# explanations-be: every row`, `60 rows: 60 taken, 0 dropped.`; the run
lists 60 + N. Show writes nothing. If it exits 1, its `fail` lines say why the kind cannot be read: tell the
maintainer those lines in place of the question. Until the maintainer answers, the code lane passes over the
gate as over a fan-out, and holds at task 43, whose fan-out (task 40) waits for this gate.
Then:
- **Go.** The Rulings line holds the question and « go ». The gate is `done`, and task 40's Split runs at the
  next point between two code-lane tasks (`one-session.md`, « Starting a fan-out task »).
- **Go, with changes to rows.** The maintainer names items and what to change in their note, `also` or
  decoys. The changes become one proposed `mechanical` task, placed before task 43, that writes them into
  `src/content/notes.js`, `also.js` and `decoys.js` and runs the full suite: `test/lang.js` reads every note's
  quoted Dutch, and `test/content.js` every decoy against the answers the course accepts. They cannot go back
  through the kind's rows: a second Merge of `explanations-be` refuses as stale every row whose note task 38
  wrote, since the stamp covers the note, and Split cuts nothing for a kind that has batches. The gate's
  Rulings line is the record those rows would have been, and no later Merge writes those keys: task 43 writes
  only the `explanations` kind's. Nothing goes stale either: these items are not `explanations` rows, and an
  `explanations` row names its siblings by `nl` and `be` only. The gate is `done`, and task 40's Split runs as
  for « go ».
- **A change to the format.** The run controller launches a design sitting (`design-sitting.md`) with the
  maintainer's words as its question, tells the maintainer its name, and stops the run as for `needs design`;
  the gate stays `in progress`. The sitting amends `<WS>/drafts/explanations/format.md`, which task 40's
  drafters and readers read. If Check must follow, its brief is a `mechanical` task before task 40 that changes
  the Check of tasks 27 and 28 (`tools/content/lib/explain.js` and its tests), and its hand-back tells the run
  controller to set the gate `done` once that task is `done`, so that task 40 drafts to the new Check. Rows of
  `explanations-be` that the new format would change are changes to rows, as above.

Split: node tools/content/split.js . "<WS>/drafts/explanations"
Check: node tools/content/check.js "<WS>/drafts/explanations/<batch>"
Merged by: task 43
Why: decisions 8a and 8b. Every word and phrase gets an explanation, and this kind holds the 361 − N whose
Flemish form is their Dutch, the items that `explanations-be` (task 31) did not hold. Their drafting waits
for gate 39, where the maintainer read the Flemish items' explanations. Gate 39 may change this format: a
design sitting then amends `<WS>/drafts/explanations/format.md` before the gate is `done`, and that file is
what drafters and readers read. A row writes the note in French and in English and the « on dit aussi »
forms. It writes no decoys: « Comment le dit-on ici ? » asks none of these items. Split cuts one batch per
unit, in the course's order. In the proof, before task 30 moved N items to `explanations-be`, that was
overleven 18, ikengij 29, tijd 48, bakker 28, thuis 31, familie 29, onderweg 33, werkbasis 32, dedag 30,
winkel 28, dokter 30 and weekend 25. 66 of the 361 have a note today, and 37 of those already meet this
format. Tasks 41 and 42 run beside the drafting, and neither changes a word's or a phrase's `be`, meaning,
note or `also`, which the stamp covers.

#### Format

```json
{"id": "winkel:w8", "stamp": "b1851dd4", "note": {"fr": "Un diminutif en « -je », donc « het » : « het zakje », comme « het broodje ».", "en": "A diminutive in “-je”, so “het”: “het zakje”, like “het broodje”."}, "also": []}
```

- One row per input row, in its order. Copy `id` and `stamp` unchanged, then give `note` and `also`. No other
  field except `unsure`.
- `note` says what `meaning` does not: an article a French speaker would guess wrong, a separable verb, the
  word order, a plural, the register (« u » or « je »), a false friend, how Flanders says it when that differs.
  Check refuses a note that only repeats the meaning.
- `note` is `{"fr": …, "en": …}`, the same note in French and in English. Each side is one line of at most 160
  characters and 2 sentences, with no `<` and no straight double quote. Write the typographic apostrophe, `’`.
- Quotes hold Dutch only (decision 8b): « … » in `fr`, “…” in `en`, no quote inside a quote, and both sides
  quote the same Dutch. A translation goes in parentheses, unquoted:
  `« Ik heb er geen goesting in » (je n’ai pas envie)`.
- Every quoted word is Dutch that OpenTaal or `flemish.tsv` knows, or a word of the row's own forms (`nl`, `be`,
  `also`). A French or an English word is never quoted:
  `Vient tout droit du français embêtant.`
- A word of the course that both sides leave bare is refused: quote it. Today's note for `winkel:w8`,
  `Diminutif en -je, donc het.`, leaves `het` and `-je` bare in both languages: the example above rewrites it.
- Each side is written in its own language. Outside quotes, Check refuses French function words in `en` (le,
  la, et, est, avec…) and English ones in `fr` (the, and, of, is, with…).
- Both sides hold the same digits and the same `{naam}`, `{stad}` and `{bedrijf}` tokens. Write a default name
  as its token, never the name itself.
- `note` in the input is today's note, or `null`. Keep it word for word when it meets this format and says
  something true and worth saying; otherwise rewrite it, keeping what it says that is right (decision 8a).
  A few old notes have `"en": null`: write the English.
- `also` lists the other Dutch forms that the typed exercise should accept for this item, in this sense, `[]`
  for none. One form per entry (no `/`, no `;`, and for a word no comma), a noun with its article, each word
  spelled as OpenTaal or `flemish.tsv` knows it. Check refuses `nl` itself, the same form twice, and the Dutch
  of another item unless that item is a sibling or the input's `also` already holds it. Keep the input's forms
  unless one is wrong. A form you add becomes a right answer, so the reader reads the row whole.
- `siblings` lists the items with the same sense. Your note and your `also` agree with theirs.
- `labelled` lists the senses that English Wiktionary labels Belgian for `nl` itself, or is `null`. It is a
  lead for the note, not a text to copy: its senses are English, and a quote holds Dutch only.
- A row you doubt carries `"unsure": "<why, in one line>"`. Check still checks it, and the reader reads it first.
- A verdict carries `id` and `verdict`, and no other field.

#### Reader focus

- Does the note teach what `meaning` does not? A note that says the meaning again in other words passes Check:
  dispute it.
- Is the grammar right? A wrong article, plural or verb form in a note teaches the error to every learner.
- Does the quoted Dutch hold up? An example in a note is grammatical, and uses the item as the note says.
- When a note says how Flanders says it, is that true at work today, and not one dialect's? These items have
  no Flemish form in `be.js`, so a note does not invent one.
- Are `fr` and `en` the same note, each natural in its own language? Dispute a side that reads as a
  word-for-word translation.
- `also`. Is each form right for this item, in this sense? It becomes an answer that the typed exercise
  accepts, and the row goes on to the content check (`readWhole` gives `new also`).
- An old note kept word for word: is it still true, and still worth saying?
- Siblings agree: the same sense gets the same note and the same `also`.
- `unsure` rows first.
